<h1 id="apify-api">Apify API v2-2026-11-09T143926Z</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.


The Apify API (version 2) provides programmatic access to the [Apify
platform](https://docs.apify.com). The API is organized
around [RESTful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representational_state_transfer)
HTTP endpoints.

You can download the complete OpenAPI schema of Apify API in the [YAML](http://docs.apify.com/api/openapi.yaml) or [JSON](http://docs.apify.com/api/openapi.json) formats. The source code is also available on [GitHub](https://github.com/apify/apify-docs/tree/master/apify-api/openapi).

All requests and responses (including errors) are encoded in
[JSON](http://www.json.org/) format with UTF-8 encoding,
with a few exceptions that are explicitly described in the reference.

To access the API, we recommend using one of our API clients:

Stable API clients:
- For [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/), we recommend the [`apify-client`](https://docs.apify.com/api/client/js) [NPM
package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/apify-client).
- For [Python](https://www.python.org/), we recommend the [`apify-client`](https://docs.apify.com/api/client/python) [PyPI
package](https://pypi.org/project/apify-client/).

Experimental API clients:
- For [Java](https://www.java.com/), we recommend the `apify-client` [Maven central component](https://central.sonatype.com/artifact/com.apify/apify-client).
- For [Rust](https://rust-lang.org/), we recommend the `apify-client` [crate](https://crates.io/crates/apify-client).
- For [.NET](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/), we recommend the `apify-client` [Nuget package](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Apify.Client).
- For [PHP](https://www.php.net/), we recommend the `apify-client` [Packagist package](https://packagist.org/packages/apify/apify-client).
- For [Go](https://go.dev/), we recommend the `apify-client` [package](https://github.com/apify/apify-client-go/releases).

The clients' functions correspond to the API endpoints and have the same
parameters. This simplifies development of apps that depend on the Apify
platform.

:::note Important Request Details

- `Content-Type` header: For requests with a JSON body, you must include the `Content-Type: application/json` header.

- Method override: You can override the HTTP method using the `method` query parameter. This is useful for clients that can only send `GET` requests. For example, to call a `POST` endpoint, append `?method=POST` to the URL of your `GET` request.

:::

## Authentication
<span id="/introduction/authentication"></span>

**You can find your API token on the
[Integrations](https://console.apify.com/settings/integrations) page in the
Apify Console.**

To use your token in a request, either:

- _(Recommended)_ Add the token to your request's `Authorization` header as `Bearer <token>`.
E.g., `Authorization: Bearer xxxxxxx`.
For details, see the [`Authorization` header](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Authorization) on MDN.
- Add it as the `token` parameter to your request URL. (Less secure).

Using your token in the request header is more secure than using it as a URL
parameter because URLs are often stored
in browser history and server logs. This creates a chance for someone
unauthorized to access your API token.

**Never share your API token or password with untrusted parties!**

For more information, see our
[integrations](https://docs.apify.com/platform/integrations) documentation.

### Agentic payments

AI agents can authenticate and pay for Actor runs without an Apify account
using agentic payments. Instead of an API token, the request carries a
payment credential that both authorizes and pays for the call. Apify supports
the [x402 protocol](https://docs.apify.com/platform/integrations/x402)
(`PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` header) and
[Skyfire](https://docs.apify.com/platform/integrations/skyfire)
(`skyfire-pay-id` header).

Agents can also pay once with x402 or the
[Machine Payments Protocol (MPP)](https://docs.apify.com/integrations/mpp)
and receive a temporary API token with a fixed spend cap from the Apify
Agent General Interface (AGI) at
[https://agi.apify.com](https://agi.apify.com). Use that token as a regular
`Bearer` token.

## Basic usage
<span id="/introduction/basic-usage"></span>

To run an Actor, send a POST request to the [Run Actor](/api/v2/actors-runs-post) endpoint using either the
Actor ID code (e.g. `vKg4IjxZbEYTYeW8T`) or its name (e.g.
`janedoe~my-actor`):

`https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/[actor_id]/runs`

If the Actor is not runnable anonymously, you will receive a 401 or 403
[response code](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Status).
This means you need to add your [secret API
token](https://console.apify.com/account#/integrations) to the request's
`Authorization` header ([recommended](#/introduction/authentication)) or as a
URL query parameter `?token=[your_token]` (less secure).

Optionally, you can include the query parameters described in the [Run Actor](/api/v2/actors-runs-post) section to customize your
run.

If you're using Node.js, the best way to run an Actor is using the
`Apify.call()` method from the [Apify
SDK](https://sdk.apify.com/docs/api/apify#apifycallactid-input-options). It
runs the Actor using the account you are currently logged into (determined
by the [secret API token](https://console.apify.com/account#/integrations)).
The result is an [Actor run
object](https://sdk.apify.com/docs/typedefs/actor-run) and its output (if
any).

A typical workflow is as follows:

1. Run an Actor or task using the [Run Actor](/api/v2/actors-runs-post) or
[Run Actor task](/api/v2/actor-task-runs-post) API endpoints.
2. Monitor the Actor run by periodically polling its progress using the [Get Actor run](/api/v2/actor-run-get) API
endpoint.
3. Fetch the results from the [Get dataset items](/api/v2/dataset-items-get) API endpoint using the
`defaultDatasetId`, which you receive in the Run request response.
Additional data may be stored in a key-value store. You can fetch them from
the [Get key-value store record](/api/v2/key-value-store-record-get) API endpoint
using the `defaultKeyValueStoreId` and the store's `key`.

**Note**: Instead of periodic polling, you can also run your Actor or task synchronously with the
[Run Actor synchronously and get key-value store record](/api/v2/actor-run-sync-post) or
[Run Actor task synchronously and get key-value store record](/api/v2/actor-task-run-sync-post)
endpoint. This will ensure that the request waits for 300 seconds (5
minutes) for the run to finish and returns its output. If the run takes
longer, the request will time out and throw an error.

## Legacy `/v2/acts/` URL prefix
<span id="/introduction/legacy-acts-prefix"></span>

The `/v2/acts/` prefix is deprecated but still fully functional, and 
such endpoint routes to the same handler as its `/v2/actors/...` counterpart. 
New integrations should use the canonical /v2/actors/ prefix, 
but existing clients keep working without changes.

## Response structure
<span id="/introduction/response-structure"></span>

Most API endpoints return a JSON object with the `data` property:

```
{
    "data": {
        ...
    }
}
```

However, there are a few explicitly described exceptions, such as
[Get dataset items](/api/v2/dataset-items-get) or
[Get key-value store record](/api/v2/key-value-store-record-get)
API endpoints, which return data in other formats.
In case of an error, the response has the HTTP status code in the range of
4xx or 5xx and the `data` property is replaced with `error`. For example:

```
{
    "error": {
        "type": "record-not-found",
        "message": "Store was not found."
    }
}
```

See [Errors](#/introduction/errors) for more details.

## Pagination
<span id="/introduction/pagination"></span>

All API endpoints that return a list of records
(e.g. [Get list of Actors](/api/v2/actors-get))
enforce pagination in order to limit the size of their responses.

Most of these API endpoints are paginated using the `offset` and `limit`
query parameters.
The only exception is
[Get list of key-value store keys](/api/v2/key-value-store-keys-get),
which is paginated using the `exclusiveStartKey` query parameter.

**IMPORTANT**: Each API endpoint that supports pagination enforces a certain
maximum value for the `limit` parameter,
in order to reduce the load on Apify servers.
The maximum limit could change in future so you should never
rely on a specific value and check the responses of these API endpoints.

### Using offset
<span id="/introduction/pagination/using-offset"></span>

Most API endpoints that return a list of records enable pagination using the
following query parameters:

<table>
  <tr>
    <td><code>limit</code></td>
    <td>Limits the response to contain a specific maximum number of items, e.g. <code>limit=20</code>.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td><code>offset</code></td>
    <td>Skips a number of items from the beginning of the list, e.g. <code>offset=100</code>.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td><code>desc</code></td>
    <td>
    By default, items are sorted in the order in which they were created or added to the list.
    This feature is useful when fetching all the items, because it ensures that items
    created after the client started the pagination will not be skipped.
    If you specify the <code>desc=1</code> parameter, the items will be returned in the reverse order,
    i.e. from the newest to the oldest items.
    </td>
  </tr>
</table>

The response of these API endpoints is always a JSON object with the
following structure:

```
{
    "data": {
        "total": 2560,
        "offset": 250,
        "limit": 1000,
        "count": 1000,
        "desc": false,
        "items": [
            { 1st object },
            { 2nd object },
            ...
            { 1000th object }
        ]
    }
}
```

The following table describes the meaning of the response properties:

<table>
  <tr>
    <th>Property</th>
    <th>Description</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td><code>total</code></td>
    <td>The total number of items available in the list.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td><code>offset</code></td>
    <td>The number of items that were skipped at the start.
    This is equal to the <code>offset</code> query parameter if it was provided, otherwise it is <code>0</code>.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td><code>limit</code></td>
    <td>The maximum number of items that can be returned in the HTTP response.
    It equals to the <code>limit</code> query parameter if it was provided or
    the maximum limit enforced for the particular API endpoint, whichever is smaller.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td><code>count</code></td>
    <td>The actual number of items returned in the HTTP response.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td><code>desc</code></td>
    <td><code>true</code> if data were requested in descending order and <code>false</code> otherwise.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td><code>items</code></td>
    <td>An array of requested items.</td>
  </tr>
</table>

### Using key
<span id="/introduction/pagination/using-key"></span>

The records in the [key-value
store](https://docs.apify.com/platform/storage/key-value-store)
are not ordered based on numerical indexes,
but rather by their keys in the UTF-8 binary order.
Therefore the
[Get list of key-value store keys](/api/v2/key-value-store-keys-get)
API endpoint only supports pagination using the following query parameters:

<table>
  <tr>
    <td><code>limit</code></td>
    <td>Limits the response to contain a specific maximum number items, e.g. <code>limit=20</code>.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td><code>exclusiveStartKey</code></td>
    <td>Skips all records with keys up to the given key including the given key,
    in the UTF-8 binary order.</td>
  </tr>
</table>

The response of the API endpoint is always a JSON object with following
structure:

```
{
    "data": {
        "limit": 1000,
        "isTruncated": true,
        "exclusiveStartKey": "my-key",
        "nextExclusiveStartKey": "some-other-key",
        "items": [
            { 1st object },
            { 2nd object },
            ...
            { 1000th object }
        ]
    }
}
```

The following table describes the meaning of the response properties:

<table>
  <tr>
    <th>Property</th>
    <th>Description</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td><code>limit</code></td>
    <td>The maximum number of items that can be returned in the HTTP response.
    It equals to the <code>limit</code> query parameter if it was provided or
    the maximum limit enforced for the particular endpoint, whichever is smaller.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td><code>isTruncated</code></td>
    <td><code>true</code> if there are more items left to be queried. Otherwise <code>false</code>.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td><code>exclusiveStartKey</code></td>
    <td>The last key that was skipped at the start. Is `null` for the first page.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td><code>nextExclusiveStartKey</code></td>
    <td>The value for the <code>exclusiveStartKey</code> parameter to query the next page of items.</td>
  </tr>
</table>

## Errors
<span id="/introduction/errors"></span>

The Apify API uses common HTTP status codes: 2xx range for success, 4xx
range for errors caused by the caller
(invalid requests) and 5xx range for server errors (these are rare).
Each error response contains a JSON object defining the `error` property,
which is an object with
the `type` and `message` properties that contain the error code and a
human-readable error description, respectively.

For example:

```
{
    "error": {
        "type": "record-not-found",
        "message": "Store was not found."
    }
}
```

Here is the table of the most common errors that can occur for many API
endpoints:

<table>
  <tr>
    <th>status</th>
    <th>type</th>
    <th>message</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>400</td>
    <td><code>invalid-request</code></td>
    <td>POST data must be a JSON object</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>400</td>
    <td><code>invalid-value</code></td>
    <td>Invalid value provided: Comments required</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>400</td>
    <td><code>invalid-record-key</code></td>
    <td>Record key contains invalid character</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>401</td>
    <td><code>token-not-provided</code></td>
    <td>Authentication token was not provided</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>404</td>
    <td><code>record-not-found</code></td>
    <td>Store was not found</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>429</td>
    <td><code>rate-limit-exceeded</code></td>
    <td>You have exceeded the rate limit of ... requests per second</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>405</td>
    <td><code>method-not-allowed</code></td>
    <td>This API endpoint can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS, POST</td>
  </tr>
</table>

## Rate limiting
<span id="/introduction/rate-limiting"></span>

All API endpoints limit the rate of requests in order to prevent overloading of Apify servers by misbehaving clients.

There are two kinds of rate limits - a global rate limit and a per-resource rate limit.

### Global rate limit
<span id="/introduction/rate-limiting/global-rate-limit"></span>

The global rate limit is set to _250 000 requests per minute_.
For [authenticated](#/introduction/authentication) requests, it is counted per user,
and for unauthenticated requests, it is counted per IP address.

### Per-resource rate limit
<span id="/introduction/rate-limiting/per-resource-rate-limit"></span>

The default per-resource rate limit is _60 requests per second per resource_, which in this context means a single Actor, a single Actor run, a single dataset, single key-value store etc.
The default rate limit is applied to every API endpoint except a few select ones, which have higher rate limits.
Each API endpoint returns its rate limit in `X-RateLimit-Limit` header.

These endpoints have a rate limit of _35 requests per second per resource_:

* [Batch add requests to request queue](/api/v2/request-queue-requests-batch-post)
* [Batch delete requests from request queue](/api/v2/request-queue-requests-batch-delete)
* [Get and lock request queue head](/api/v2/request-queue-head-lock-post)

These endpoints have a rate limit of _100 requests per second per resource_:

* [Download key-value store records](/api/v2/key-value-store-records-get) (ZIP archive)

These endpoints have a rate limit of _200 requests per second per resource_:

* [Get key-value store record](/api/v2/key-value-store-record-get)
* [Set key-value store record](/api/v2/key-value-store-record-put) and its [`POST` variant](/api/v2/key-value-store-record-post)
* [Delete key-value store record](/api/v2/key-value-store-record-delete)
* [Get list of key-value store keys](/api/v2/key-value-store-keys-get)

These endpoints have a rate limit of _350 requests per second per resource_:

* [Add request to request queue](/api/v2/request-queue-requests-post)
* [Get request from request queue](/api/v2/request-queue-request-get)
* [Update request in request queue](/api/v2/request-queue-request-put)
* [Delete request from request queue](/api/v2/request-queue-request-delete)
* [Prolong lock on request in request queue](/api/v2/request-queue-request-lock-put)
* [Delete lock on request in request queue](/api/v2/request-queue-request-lock-delete)

These endpoints have a rate limit of _400 requests per second per resource_:

* [Run Actor](/api/v2/actors-runs-post)
* [Run Actor task](/api/v2/actor-task-runs-post)
* [Run Actor task synchronously and get key-value store record](/api/v2/actor-task-run-sync-post) and its [`GET` variant](/api/v2/actor-task-run-sync-get)
* [Run Actor task synchronously and get dataset items](/api/v2/actor-task-run-sync-get-dataset-items-post) and its [`GET` variant](/api/v2/actor-task-run-sync-get-dataset-items-get)
* [Metamorph Actor run](/api/v2/actor-run-metamorph-post)
* [Store items in dataset](/api/v2/dataset-items-post)

### Rate limit exceeded errors
<span id="/introduction/rate-limiting/rate-limit-exceeded-errors"></span>

If the client is sending too many requests, the API endpoints respond with the HTTP status code `429 Too Many Requests`
and the following body:

```
{
    "error": {
        "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
        "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit of ... requests per second"
    }
}
```

### Retrying rate-limited requests with exponential backoff
<span id="/introduction/rate-limiting/retrying-rate-limited-requests-with-exponential-backoff"></span>

If the client receives the rate limit error, it should wait a certain period of time and then retry the request.
If the error happens again, the client should double the wait period and retry the request,
and so on. This algorithm is known as _exponential backoff_
and it can be described using the following pseudo-code:

1. Define a variable `DELAY=500`
2. Send the HTTP request to the API endpoint
3. If the response has status code not equal to 429 then you are done. Otherwise:
   * Wait for a period of time chosen randomly from the interval `DELAY` to `2*DELAY` milliseconds
   * Double the future wait period by setting `DELAY = 2*DELAY`
   * Continue with step 2

If all requests sent by the client implement the above steps,
the client will automatically use the maximum available bandwidth for its requests.

Note that the Apify API clients [for JavaScript](https://docs.apify.com/api/client/js)
and [for Python](https://docs.apify.com/api/client/python)
use the exponential backoff algorithm transparently, so that you do not need to worry about it.

## Referring to resources
<span id="/introduction/referring-to-resources"></span>

There are three main ways to refer to a resource you're accessing via API.

- the resource ID (e.g. `iKkPcIgVvwmztduf8`)
- `username~resourcename` - when using this access method, you will need to
use your API token, and access will only work if you have the correct
permissions.
- `~resourcename` - for this, you need to use an API token, and the
`resourcename` refers to a resource in the API token owner's account.

Base URLs:

* <a href="https://api.apify.com">https://api.apify.com</a>

License: <a href="https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0.html">Apache 2.0</a>

# Authentication

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer Bearer token provided in the `Authorization` header (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer your_token`—recommended). For details, see the [`Authorization` header](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Authorization) on MDN.

Use your API token to authenticate requests. You can find it on the [Integrations page](https://console.apify.com/account#/integrations) in Apify Console. This method is more secure than query parameters, as headers are not logged in browser history or server logs.

:::danger Security

Do not share your API token (or account password) with untrusted parties.

:::

_When is authentication required?_
- _Required_ for private Actors, tasks, or resources (e.g., builds of private Actors).
- _Required_ when using named formats for IDs (e.g., `username~store-name` for stores or `username~queue-name` for queues).
- _Optional_ for public Actors or resources (e.g., builds of public Actors can be queried without a token).

For more information, see our [integrations documentation](https://docs.apify.com/platform/integrations).

* API Key (apiKey)
    - Parameter Name: **token**, in: query. API token provided as a query parameter (e.g., `?token=your_token`—less secure).

Use your API token to authenticate requests. You can find it on the [Integrations page](https://console.apify.com/account#/integrations) in Apify Console.

:::danger Security

Do not share your API token (or account password) with untrusted parties.

:::

_When is authentication required?_
- _Required_ for private Actors, tasks, or resources (e.g., builds of private Actors).
- _Required_ when using named formats for IDs (e.g., `username~store-name` for stores or `username~queue-name` for queues).
- _Optional_ for public Actors or resources (e.g., builds of public Actors can be queried without a token).

For more information, see our [integrations documentation](https://docs.apify.com/platform/integrations).

<h1 id="apify-api-actors">Actors</h1>

The API endpoints in this section allow you to manage [Apify Actors](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors).

## Identify an Actor

For API endpoints that require the `actorId` parameter, provide one of the following:
- The Actor ID. It's part of the Actor's URL in Apify Console: `https://console.apify.com/actors/<ACTOR_ID>`. For example, `reGe1ST3OBgYZSsZJ`.
- The username of the Actor owner plus the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`). For example, `apify~instagram-scraper`.


## Get list of Actors

<a id="opIdactors_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actors`

Gets the list of all Actors that the user created or used. The response is a
list of objects, where each object contains a basic information about a single Actor.

To only get Actors created by the user, add the `my=1` query parameter.

The endpoint supports pagination using the `limit` and `offset` parameters
and it will not return more than 1000 records.

By default, the records are sorted by the `createdAt` field in ascending
order, therefore you can use pagination to incrementally fetch all Actors while new
ones are still being created. To sort the records in descending order, use the `desc=1` parameter.

You can also sort by your last run by using the `sortBy=stats.lastRunStartedAt` query parameter.
In this case, descending order means the most recently run Actor appears first.


<h3 id="get-list-of-actors-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|my|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then the returned list only contains Actors owned by the user. The default value is `false`.<br>|
|offset|query|number(double)|false|Number of items that should be skipped at the start. The default value is `0`.<br>|
|limit|query|number(double)|false|Maximum number of items to return. The default value as well as the maximum is `1000`.<br>|
|sortBy|query|string|false|Field to sort the records by. The default is `createdAt`. You can also use `stats.lastRunStartedAt` to sort<br>by the most recently ran Actors.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sortBy|createdAt|
|sortBy|stats.lastRunStartedAt|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "total": 2,
    "count": 2,
    "offset": 0,
    "limit": 1000,
    "desc": false,
    "items": [
      {
        "id": "br9CKmk457",
        "createdAt": "2019-10-29T07:34:24.202Z",
        "modifiedAt": "2019-10-30T07:34:24.202Z",
        "name": "MyAct",
        "username": "janedoe"
      },
      {
        "id": "ksiEKo23pz",
        "createdAt": "2019-11-30T07:34:24.202Z",
        "modifiedAt": "2019-12-12T07:34:24.202Z",
        "name": "MySecondAct",
        "username": "janedoe"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

## Create Actor

<a id="opIdactors_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "MyActor",
    "description": "My favourite Actor!",
    "title": "My Actor",
    "isPublic": false,
    "seoTitle": "My Actor",
    "seoDescription": "My Actor is the best",
    "versions": [
      {
        "versionNumber": "0.0",
        "sourceType": "SOURCE_FILES",
        "envVars": [
          {
            "name": "DOMAIN",
            "value": "http://example.com",
            "isSecret": false
          },
          {
            "name": "SECRET_PASSWORD",
            "value": "MyTopSecretPassword123",
            "isSecret": true
          }
        ],
        "applyEnvVarsToBuild": false,
        "buildTag": "latest",
        "sourceFiles": []
      }
    ],
    "categories": [],
    "defaultRunOptions": {
      "build": "latest",
      "timeoutSecs": 3600,
      "memoryMbytes": 2048,
      "restartOnError": false
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v2/actors`

Creates an Actor with the settings specified in an `Actor` object passed as
JSON in the POST payload.

Returns the created `Actor` object.

In the HTTP request, set the `Content-Type` header to `application/json`.

### Define a source code version

An Actor must specify at least one version of the source code.
For details, see [Actor versions](/api/v2/actors-actor-versions).

### Publish an Actor

To make your Actor [public](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/publishing),
use the [Update Actor](/api/v2/actor-put) endpoint.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "MyActor",
  "description": "My favourite Actor!",
  "title": "My Actor",
  "isPublic": false,
  "seoTitle": "My Actor",
  "seoDescription": "My Actor is the best",
  "versions": [
    {
      "versionNumber": "0.0",
      "sourceType": "SOURCE_FILES",
      "envVars": [
        {
          "name": "DOMAIN",
          "value": "http://example.com",
          "isSecret": false
        },
        {
          "name": "SECRET_PASSWORD",
          "value": "MyTopSecretPassword123",
          "isSecret": true
        }
      ],
      "applyEnvVarsToBuild": false,
      "buildTag": "latest",
      "sourceFiles": []
    }
  ],
  "categories": [],
  "defaultRunOptions": {
    "build": "latest",
    "timeoutSecs": 3600,
    "memoryMbytes": 2048,
    "restartOnError": false
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-actor-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string \| null|false|The identifier of the Actor. Use lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens. Spaces or special characters aren't allowed. Must be unique across your account.|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|Short description of the Actor, displayed in Apify Store and Console.|
|» title|body|string \| null|false|Human-readable name of the Actor, displayed in Apify Store and Console. Can contain spaces and capital letters. Recommended length is 40-50 characters. You can change this title without affecting the Actor's URL or SEO.|
|» isPublic|body|boolean|false|Whether the Actor is available to users in Apify Store. A new Actor is always private. To publish it, build it first, then update it with `isPublic` set to `true`.|
|» actorPermissionLevel|body|string|false|Determines the permission level that the Actor requires to run. For details, see [Actor permissions](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/development/permissions).<br>|

<h3 id="create-actor-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|413|Payload Too Large|Payload too large - the request body exceeds the size limit.|Inline|
|415|Unsupported Media Type|Unsupported media type - the Content-Encoding of the request is not supported.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

## Get Actor

<a id="opIdactor_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actors/{actorId}`

Gets an object that contains all the details about the Actor with the specified ID.

<h3 id="get-actor-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Update Actor

<a id="opIdactor_put"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "MyActor",
    "description": "My favourite Actor!",
    "isPublic": false,
    "actorPermissionLevel": "LIMITED_PERMISSIONS",
    "seoTitle": "My Actor",
    "seoDescription": "My Actor is the best",
    "title": "My Actor",
    "versions": [
      {
        "versionNumber": "0.0",
        "sourceType": "SOURCE_FILES",
        "envVars": [
          {
            "name": "DOMAIN",
            "value": "http://example.com",
            "isSecret": false
          },
          {
            "name": "SECRET_PASSWORD",
            "value": "MyTopSecretPassword123",
            "isSecret": true
          }
        ],
        "applyEnvVarsToBuild": false,
        "buildTag": "latest",
        "sourceFiles": []
      }
    ],
    "categories": [],
    "defaultRunOptions": {
      "build": "latest",
      "timeoutSecs": 3600,
      "memoryMbytes": 2048,
      "restartOnError": false
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/actors/{actorId}`

Updates an Actor's settings with the values specified in an `Actor` object
passed as JSON in the POST payload. Only the fields specified in the request body are updated.

Returns the full `Actor` object, the same as the
[Get Actor](/api/v2/actor-get) endpoint.

In the HTTP request, set the `Content-Type` header to `application/json`.

### Authentication

To provide the authentication token, we recommend using the request's
`Authorization` header, rather than the URL. For details,
see [Authentication](/api/v2#authentication).

### Make an Actor public

To make your Actor [public](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/publishing):
- Set `isPublic` to `true`.
- Provide `title` and `categories`. For reference, see [constants from the `apify-shared-js`
package](https://github.com/apify/apify-shared-js/blob/2d43ebc41ece9ad31cd6525bd523fb86939bf860/packages/consts/src/consts.ts#L452-L471)

### Update build tags

To change tags assigned to Actor builds, use the `taggedBuilds` object. It's a dictionary that maps tag names
to specific builds, where:
- the key is the tag name, for example `latest` or `beta`
- the value is either `null` or an object with a build ID

Changing tags is a patch operation. Only the tags that you provide in this object are updated.

Note that you can assign multiple tags to a single build, but you can't assign the same tag to multiple builds.

- To create or reassign a tag, provide the tag name with a build ID. For example, to assign
the `latest` tag to a build, use:

```json
{
  "latest": { "buildId": "z2EryhbfhgSyqj6Hn" }
}
```

- To remove a tag from a build, provide the tag name with a `null` value. For example, to remove the `beta` tag, use:

```json
{
  "beta": null
}
```

- You can perform multiple actions at once. The following example reassigns `latest`
and removes `beta`, while preserving other existing tags:

```json
{
  "latest": { "buildId": "z2EryhbfhgSyqj6Hn" },
  "beta": null
}
```


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "MyActor",
  "description": "My favourite Actor!",
  "isPublic": false,
  "actorPermissionLevel": "LIMITED_PERMISSIONS",
  "seoTitle": "My Actor",
  "seoDescription": "My Actor is the best",
  "title": "My Actor",
  "versions": [
    {
      "versionNumber": "0.0",
      "sourceType": "SOURCE_FILES",
      "envVars": [
        {
          "name": "DOMAIN",
          "value": "http://example.com",
          "isSecret": false
        },
        {
          "name": "SECRET_PASSWORD",
          "value": "MyTopSecretPassword123",
          "isSecret": true
        }
      ],
      "applyEnvVarsToBuild": false,
      "buildTag": "latest",
      "sourceFiles": []
    }
  ],
  "categories": [],
  "defaultRunOptions": {
    "build": "latest",
    "timeoutSecs": 3600,
    "memoryMbytes": 2048,
    "restartOnError": false
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-actor-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|false|The identifier of the Actor. Use lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens. Spaces or special characters aren't allowed. Must be unique across your account.|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|Short description of the Actor, displayed in Apify Store and Console.|
|» isPublic|body|boolean|false|Whether the Actor is available to users in Apify Store. If `false`, the Actor is private and only visible to you.|
|» actorPermissionLevel|body|string|false|Determines the permission level that the Actor requires to run. For details, see [Actor permissions](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/development/permissions).<br>|
|» seoTitle|body|string \| null|false|Name of the Actor to display by search engines such as Google. Can be different from the Actor's name displayed in Apify Store and Console. Recommended length is 40-50 characters.|
|» seoDescription|body|string \| null|false|Description of the Actor to display by search engines such as Google. Recommended length is 140-156 characters.|
|» title|body|string \| null|false|Human-readable name of the Actor, displayed in Apify Store and Console. Can contain spaces and capital letters. Recommended length is 40-50 characters. You can change this title without affecting the Actor's URL or SEO.|
|» restartOnError|body|boolean|false|**Deprecated.**|
|» versions|body|[object]|false|An array of `Version` objects. Each object represents a specific version of the Actor's source code: its location, builds, and environment configuration.|
|» » versionNumber|body|string|true|The version number of the Actor. Two numbers separated by a dot, that represent the `MAJOR.MINOR` part of the semantic versioning.|
|» » sourceType|body|string|true|Where the source code of the version lives.|
|» » envVars|body|[object]|false|Environment variables for the version.|
|» » » name|body|string|true|The name of the environment variable. Can't contain `=`.|
|» » » value|body|string|true|The value of the environment variable.|
|» » » isSecret|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether the environment variable is encrypted. Secret values aren't returned by the API.|
|» » applyEnvVarsToBuild|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether to inject the environment variables at build time.|
|» » buildTag|body|string \| null|false|The tag name to apply to a successful build of this version. Can be `null` when the version has no build tag.|
|» » sourceFiles|body|[object]|false|Applies when the `sourceType` is `SOURCE_FILES`. Represents the Actor's file structure as an array of files and folders.|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|object|false|Represents a single file in the Actor's source code.|
|» » » format|body|string|false|Format of the file's content, `TEXT` for plain text and `BASE64` for encoded content.|

<h3 id="update-actor-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found - the requested resource does not exist.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|413|Payload Too Large|Payload too large - the request body exceeds the size limit.|Inline|
|415|Unsupported Media Type|Unsupported media type - the Content-Encoding of the request is not supported.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

## Delete Actor

<a id="opIdactor_delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/actors/{actorId}`

Deletes an Actor with the specified ID.

<h3 id="delete-actor-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|

> Example responses

> 204 Response

```json
{}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "record-not-found",
    "message": "The requested resource was not found."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

<h3 id="delete-actor-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found - the requested resource does not exist.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

## Get list of Actor OAuth connections

<a id="opIdactor_oauthConnections_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/oauth-connections \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actors/{actorId}/oauth-connections`

Gets the OAuth connections configured on the Actor. Each connection defines an OAuth provider that users of the
Actor can connect their accounts through. Only public credential fields are returned, never the client secret.

An Actor has at most 5 connections, so the list is not paginated.

You need read access to the Actor.


<h3 id="get-list-of-actor-oauth-connections-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "total": 1,
    "items": [
      {
        "_id": "kD9fm2Xp4cJq7Lw8N",
        "actorId": "zdc3Pyhyz3m8vjDeM",
        "oAuthProviderType": "GOOGLE",
        "createdAt": "2026-01-28T10:00:00.000Z",
        "modifiedAt": "2026-01-28T10:00:00.000Z",
        "credentials": {
          "clientId": "1234567890-abc.apps.googleusercontent.com",
          "scope": "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file",
          "label": "My OAuth app",
          "imageUrl": "https://example.com/logo.png"
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "record-not-found",
    "message": "The requested resource was not found."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-list-of-actor-oauth-connections-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found - the requested resource does not exist.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Validate Actor input

<a id="opIdactor_validateInput_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/validate-input \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{}'
```

`POST /v2/actors/{actorId}/validate-input`

Validates the JSON payload against the Actor's
[input schema](https://docs.apify.com/actors/development/actor-definition/input-schema)
defined in the specified build.

If the specified build has no input schema, any input is considered valid.


> Body parameter

```json
{}
```

<h3 id="validate-actor-input-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|build|query|string|false|Actor build whose input schema is used for validation. Can be a build tag or build number.<br>Defaults to the `latest` build tag.<br>|
|body|body|object|true|The Actor input as a JSON object.<br><br>You can omit fields that have a `default` in the input schema. They're<br>filled in before validation.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "valid": true
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "record-not-found",
    "message": "The requested resource was not found."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 413 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "request-too-large",
    "message": "The POST payload is too large (limit: 9437184 bytes, actual length: 10485760 bytes)."
  }
}
```

> 415 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "unsupported-content-encoding",
    "message": "Content-Encoding \"bla\" is not supported."
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

<h3 id="validate-actor-input-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found - the requested resource does not exist.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|413|Payload Too Large|Payload too large - the request body exceeds the size limit.|Inline|
|415|Unsupported Media Type|Unsupported media type - the Content-Encoding of the request is not supported.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

<h3 id="validate-actor-input-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|valid|boolean|true|none|Always `true`. The endpoint responds with `200` only when the input<br>passes validation. Invalid input returns a `400` error.<br>|

Status Code **400**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|error|object|true|none|none|
|» type|string|false|none|Machine-processable error type identifier.|
|» message|string|false|none|Human-readable error message describing what went wrong.|
|» data|object|false|none|Additional machine-readable details about the error. Present only for some error types.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Get list of Actor OAuth accounts

<a id="opIdactorOAuthAccounts_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-oauth-accounts/kD9fm2Xp4cJq7Lw8N/accounts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actor-oauth-accounts/{connectionId}/accounts`

Gets the accounts you connected through the Actor OAuth connection, including their OAuth tokens. Only accounts
that finished authorization are returned.

There are at most 5 accounts per user and connection, so the list is not paginated.


<h3 id="get-list-of-actor-oauth-accounts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|connectionId|path|string|true|Actor OAuth connection ID.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "total": 1,
    "items": [
      {
        "_id": "Rk3mP8xQ2vN5tY7wZ",
        "userId": "wRsJZtadYvn4mBZmm",
        "connectionId": "kD9fm2Xp4cJq7Lw8N",
        "createdAt": "2026-01-28T10:00:00.000Z",
        "modifiedAt": "2026-01-28T10:05:00.000Z",
        "authorizedAt": "2026-01-28T10:05:00.000Z",
        "description": "jane.doe@example.com",
        "data": {}
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "record-not-found",
    "message": "The requested resource was not found."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-list-of-actor-oauth-accounts-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found - the requested resource does not exist.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

<h3 id="get-list-of-actor-oauth-accounts-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|object|true|none|none|
|» total|integer|true|none|none|
|» items|[object]|true|none|none|
|» » _id|string|true|none|none|
|» » userId|string|true|none|none|
|» » connectionId|string|true|none|none|
|» » createdAt|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|» » modifiedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|» » authorizedAt|string \| null(date-time)|false|none|none|
|» » description|string \| null|false|none|Label of the connected account, usually its email address.|
|» » data|object|true|none|The OAuth tokens of the account, such as `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `scope` and `expiry_date`. The exact<br>fields depend on the OAuth provider.<br>|

Status Code **400**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|error|object|true|none|none|
|» type|string|false|none|Machine-processable error type identifier.|
|» message|string|false|none|Human-readable error message describing what went wrong.|
|» data|object|false|none|Additional machine-readable details about the error. Present only for some error types.|

httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Get Actor OAuth account

<a id="opIdactorOAuthAccount_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-oauth-accounts/Rk3mP8xQ2vN5tY7wZ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actor-oauth-accounts/{accountId}`

Gets an account connected through an Actor OAuth connection, including its OAuth tokens.

This endpoint only accepts the API token of an Actor run (the `APIFY_TOKEN` environment variable of the run).
The run must belong to the Actor that the account's OAuth connection is configured on, and the account must
belong to the user the run's token acts for. Any other token gets a `403` error.


<h3 id="get-actor-oauth-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accountId|path|string|true|Actor OAuth account ID.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "_id": "Rk3mP8xQ2vN5tY7wZ",
    "userId": "wRsJZtadYvn4mBZmm",
    "connectionId": "kD9fm2Xp4cJq7Lw8N",
    "createdAt": "2026-01-28T10:00:00.000Z",
    "modifiedAt": "2026-01-28T10:05:00.000Z",
    "authorizedAt": "2026-01-28T10:05:00.000Z",
    "description": "jane.doe@example.com",
    "data": {}
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "record-not-found",
    "message": "The requested resource was not found."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-actor-oauth-account-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found - the requested resource does not exist.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

<h3 id="get-actor-oauth-account-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|object|true|none|An account a user connected through an Actor OAuth connection.|
|» _id|string|true|none|none|
|» userId|string|true|none|none|
|» connectionId|string|true|none|none|
|» createdAt|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|» modifiedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|» authorizedAt|string \| null(date-time)|false|none|none|
|» description|string \| null|false|none|Label of the connected account, usually its email address.|
|» data|object|true|none|The OAuth tokens of the account, such as `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `scope` and `expiry_date`. The exact<br>fields depend on the OAuth provider.<br>|

Status Code **400**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|error|object|true|none|none|
|» type|string|false|none|Machine-processable error type identifier.|
|» message|string|false|none|Human-readable error message describing what went wrong.|
|» data|object|false|none|Additional machine-readable details about the error. Present only for some error types.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

<h1 id="apify-api-actorsactor-versions">Actors/Actor versions</h1>

The API endpoints in this section allow you to manage your Apify Actors versions.

- The version object contains the source code of a specific version of an Actor.
- The `sourceType` property indicates where the source code is hosted, and based
on its value the `Version` object has the following additional property:

| **Value** | **Description**  |
|---|---|
| `"SOURCE_FILES"`   | Source code is comprised of multiple files specified in the `sourceFiles` array. Each item of the array is an object with the following fields:<br/> - `name`: File path and name<br/> - `format`: Format of the content, can be either `"TEXT"` or `"BASE64"`<br/> - `content`: File content<br/><br/>Source files can be shown and edited in the Apify Console's Web IDE. |
| `"GIT_REPO"` | Source code is cloned from a Git repository, whose URL is specified in the `gitRepoUrl` field. |
| `"TARBALL"` | Source code is downloaded as a zip archive from a URL specified in the `tarballUrl` field. |
|`"GITHUB_GIST"`| Source code is taken from a GitHub Gist, whose URL is specified in the `gitHubGistUrl` field. |

For more information about source code and Actor versions, check out [Source code](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/development/actor-definition/source-code)
in Actors documentation.


## Get list of Actor versions

<a id="opIdactor_versions_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/versions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actors/{actorId}/versions`

Gets the list of versions of a specific Actor. The response is a JSON object
with the list of `Version` objects, where each
contains basic information about a single version.


<h3 id="get-list-of-actor-versions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "total": 5,
    "items": [
      {
        "versionNumber": "0.1",
        "envVars": null,
        "sourceType": "SOURCE_FILES",
        "applyEnvVarsToBuild": false,
        "buildTag": "latest",
        "sourceFiles": []
      },
      {
        "versionNumber": "0.2",
        "sourceType": "GIT_REPO",
        "envVars": null,
        "applyEnvVarsToBuild": false,
        "buildTag": "latest",
        "gitRepoUrl": "https://github.com/jane35/my-actor"
      },
      {
        "versionNumber": "0.3",
        "sourceType": "TARBALL",
        "envVars": null,
        "applyEnvVarsToBuild": false,
        "buildTag": "latest",
        "tarballUrl": "https://github.com/jane35/my-actor/archive/master.zip"
      },
      {
        "versionNumber": "0.4",
        "sourceType": "GITHUB_GIST",
        "envVars": null,
        "applyEnvVarsToBuild": false,
        "buildTag": "latest",
        "gitHubGistUrl": "https://gist.github.com/jane35/e51feb784yu89"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "record-not-found",
    "message": "The requested resource was not found."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-list-of-actor-versions-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found - the requested resource does not exist.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

<h3 id="get-list-of-actor-versions-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|object|true|none|none|
|» total|integer|true|none|none|
|» items|[object]|true|none|none|
|» » versionNumber|string|true|none|The version number of the Actor. Two numbers separated by a dot, that represent the `MAJOR.MINOR` part of the semantic versioning.|
|» » sourceType|string \| null|true|none|Where the source code of the version lives.|
|» » » *anyOf*|string|false|none|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|null|false|none|none|
|» » envVars|[object] \| null|false|none|Environment variables for the version.|
|» » » *anyOf*|[object]|false|none|none|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» name|string|true|none|The name of the environment variable.|
|» value|string|false|none|The value of the environment variable. If `isSecret` is `true`, this value isn't returned by the API.|
|» isSecret|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether the environment variable is encrypted. Secret values aren't returned by the API.|
|» valueHash|string|false|none|A short hash of the secret value, to detect value changes. Returned only for secret environment variables, in place of `value`.|
|» » » *anyOf*|null|false|none|none|
|» » applyEnvVarsToBuild|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether to inject the environment variables at build time.|
|» » buildTag|string \| null|false|none|The tag name to apply to a successful build of this version. Can be `null` when the version has no build tag.|
|» » sourceFiles|[object]|false|none|Applies when the `sourceType` is `SOURCE_FILES`. Represents the Actor's file structure as an array of files and folders.|
|» » » *anyOf*|object|false|none|Represents a single file in the Actor's source code.|
|» » » format|string|false|none|Format of the file's content, `TEXT` for plain text and `BASE64` for encoded content.|
|» » » content|string|false|none|The contents of the file. Interpreted based on the value of `format`.|
|» » » name|string|true|none|The path of the file relative to the Actor's root directory.|
|» » » *anyOf*|object|false|none|Represents a folder in the Actor's source code structure. Distinguished from<br>SourceCodeFile by the presence of the `folder` property set to `true`.<br>|
|» » » name|string|true|none|The path of the folder relative to the Actor's root directory.|

|» » gitHubGistUrl|string \| null|false|none|URL of the GitHub Gist to clone the source code from. Applies when the `sourceType` is `GITHUB_GIST`.|
|» » actorPath|string \| null|false|none|The Actor's directory inside the uploaded source, as a path relative to the upload root with `/` separators, for example `actors/typescript-actor`. Applies when the `sourceType` is `SOURCE_FILES` or `TARBALL`. When absent or `null`, the upload root is the Actor's directory. On a `TARBALL` version, only users with write access to the Actor get it. It has 1 to 255 characters, with no leading, trailing, or repeated `/` and no `.` or `..` segments.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Create Actor version

<a id="opIdactor_versions_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/versions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "versionNumber": "0.1",
    "sourceType": "GIT_REPO",
    "gitRepoUrl": "https://github.com/my-github-account/actor-repo"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/actors/{actorId}/versions`

Creates a version of an Actor using values specified in a `Version`
object passed as JSON in the POST
payload.

The request must specify `versionNumber` and `sourceType` parameters (as
strings) in the JSON payload and a `Content-Type: application/json` HTTP
header.

Each `sourceType` requires its own additional properties to be passed to the
JSON payload object. These are outlined in the `Version`
object table below and in more detail in
the [Apify
documentation](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/development/deployment/source-types).

For example, if an Actor's source code is stored in a [GitHub
repository](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/development/deployment/source-types#git-repository),
you will set the `sourceType` to `GIT_REPO` and pass the repository's URL in
the `gitRepoUrl` property.

```
{
    "versionNumber": "0.1",
    "sourceType": "GIT_REPO",
    "gitRepoUrl": "https://github.com/my-github-account/actor-repo"
}
```

If the Actor is in a subdirectory of the uploaded `SOURCE_FILES` or
`TARBALL` source, such as in a monorepo, set `actorPath` to that
directory, for example `"actorPath": "actors/typescript-actor"`.

The response is the `Version` object as
returned by the [Get Actor version](/api/v2/actor-version-get) endpoint.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "versionNumber": "0.1",
  "sourceType": "GIT_REPO",
  "gitRepoUrl": "https://github.com/my-github-account/actor-repo"
}
```

<h3 id="create-actor-version-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» versionNumber|body|string|true|The version number of the Actor. Two numbers separated by a dot, that represent the `MAJOR.MINOR` part of the semantic versioning.|
|» sourceType|body|string|true|Where the source code of the version lives.|
|» envVars|body|[object]|false|Environment variables for the version.|
|» » name|body|string|true|The name of the environment variable. Can't contain `=`.|
|» » value|body|string|true|The value of the environment variable.|
|» » isSecret|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether the environment variable is encrypted. Secret values aren't returned by the API.|
|» applyEnvVarsToBuild|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether to inject the environment variables at build time.|
|» buildTag|body|string \| null|false|The tag name to apply to a successful build of this version. Can be `null` when the version has no build tag.|
|» sourceFiles|body|[object]|false|Applies when the `sourceType` is `SOURCE_FILES`. Represents the Actor's file structure as an array of files and folders.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|Represents a single file in the Actor's source code.|
|» » format|body|string|false|Format of the file's content, `TEXT` for plain text and `BASE64` for encoded content.|
|» » content|body|string|false|The contents of the file. Interpreted based on the value of `format`.|
|» » name|body|string|true|The path of the file relative to the Actor's root directory.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|Represents a folder in the Actor's source code structure. Distinguished from<br>SourceCodeFile by the presence of the `folder` property set to `true`.<br>|
|» » name|body|string|true|The path of the folder relative to the Actor's root directory.|
|» » folder|body|boolean|true|Whether it's a folder. Distinguishes folders from files.|
|» gitRepoUrl|body|string|false|URL of the Git repository to clone the source code from. Applies when the `sourceType` is `GIT_REPO`.|
|» tarballUrl|body|string|false|URL of the zip archive to download the source code from. Applies when the `sourceType` is `TARBALL`.|
|» gitHubGistUrl|body|string|false|URL of the GitHub Gist to clone the source code from. Applies when the `sourceType` is `GITHUB_GIST`.|
|» actorPath|body|string \| null|false|The Actor's directory inside the uploaded source, as a path relative to the upload root with `/` separators, for example `actors/typescript-actor`. Applies when the `sourceType` is `SOURCE_FILES` or `TARBALL`. The API rejects a path when the `sourceType` is `GIT_REPO` or `GITHUB_GIST`. When omitted or `null`, the upload root is the Actor's directory. It has 1 to 255 characters, with no leading, trailing, or repeated `/` and no `.` or `..` segments.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» sourceType|SOURCE_FILES|
|» sourceType|GIT_REPO|
|» sourceType|TARBALL|
|» sourceType|GITHUB_GIST|
|» » format|BASE64|
|» » format|TEXT|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "versionNumber": "0.0",
    "sourceType": "SOURCE_FILES",
    "envVars": [
      {
        "name": "MY_ENV_VAR",
        "value": "my-value",
        "isSecret": false,
        "valueHash": "a1b2c3"
      }
    ],
    "applyEnvVarsToBuild": false,
    "buildTag": "latest",
    "sourceFiles": [
      {
        "format": "TEXT",
        "content": "console.log('This is the main.js file');",
        "name": "src/main.js"
      }
    ],
    "gitRepoUrl": "string",
    "tarballUrl": "string",
    "gitHubGistUrl": "string",
    "actorPath": "actors/typescript-actor",
    "githubWebhookId": 0,
    "gitlabWebhookId": 0,
    "bitbucketWebhookId": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-actor-version-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **201**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|object|true|none|none|
|» versionNumber|string|true|none|The version number of the Actor. Two numbers separated by a dot, that represent the `MAJOR.MINOR` part of the semantic versioning.|
|» sourceType|string \| null|true|none|Where the source code of the version lives.|
|» » *anyOf*|string|false|none|none|
|» » *anyOf*|null|false|none|none|
|» envVars|[object] \| null|false|none|Environment variables for the version.|
|» » *anyOf*|[object]|false|none|none|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» name|string|true|none|The name of the environment variable.|
|» value|string|false|none|The value of the environment variable. If `isSecret` is `true`, this value isn't returned by the API.|
|» isSecret|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether the environment variable is encrypted. Secret values aren't returned by the API.|
|» valueHash|string|false|none|A short hash of the secret value, to detect value changes. Returned only for secret environment variables, in place of `value`.|
|» » *anyOf*|null|false|none|none|
|» applyEnvVarsToBuild|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether to inject the environment variables at build time.|
|» buildTag|string \| null|false|none|The tag name to apply to a successful build of this version. Can be `null` when the version has no build tag.|
|» sourceFiles|[object]|false|none|Applies when the `sourceType` is `SOURCE_FILES`. Represents the Actor's file structure as an array of files and folders.|
|» » *anyOf*|object|false|none|Represents a single file in the Actor's source code.|
|» » format|string|false|none|Format of the file's content, `TEXT` for plain text and `BASE64` for encoded content.|
|» » content|string|false|none|The contents of the file. Interpreted based on the value of `format`.|
|» » name|string|true|none|The path of the file relative to the Actor's root directory.|
|» » *anyOf*|object|false|none|Represents a folder in the Actor's source code structure. Distinguished from<br>SourceCodeFile by the presence of the `folder` property set to `true`.<br>|
|» » name|string|true|none|The path of the folder relative to the Actor's root directory.|
|» » folder|boolean|true|none|Whether it's a folder. Distinguishes folders from files.|
|» gitRepoUrl|string \| null|false|none|URL of the Git repository to clone the source code from. Applies when the `sourceType` is `GIT_REPO`.|
|» tarballUrl|string \| null|false|none|URL to download the source code from as a zip archive. Applies when the `sourceType` is `TARBALL`.|
|» gitHubGistUrl|string \| null|false|none|URL of the GitHub Gist to clone the source code from. Applies when the `sourceType` is `GITHUB_GIST`.|
|» actorPath|string \| null|false|none|The Actor's directory inside the uploaded source, as a path relative to the upload root with `/` separators, for example `actors/typescript-actor`. Applies when the `sourceType` is `SOURCE_FILES` or `TARBALL`. When absent or `null`, the upload root is the Actor's directory. On a `TARBALL` version, only users with write access to the Actor get it. It has 1 to 255 characters, with no leading, trailing, or repeated `/` and no `.` or `..` segments.|
|» githubWebhookId|integer \| null|false|none|ID of the GitHub webhook that triggers a build on push. Present when build on push is enabled for a GitHub repository.|
|» gitlabWebhookId|integer \| null|false|none|ID of the GitLab webhook that triggers a build on push. Present when build on push is enabled for a GitLab repository.|
|» bitbucketWebhookId|string \| null|false|none|ID of the Bitbucket webhook that triggers a build on push. Present when build on push is enabled for a Bitbucket repository.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Get Actor version

<a id="opIdactor_version_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/versions/0.1 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actors/{actorId}/versions/{versionNumber}`

Gets a `Version` object that contains all the details about a specific version of an Actor.


<h3 id="get-actor-version-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|versionNumber|path|string|true|Actor version.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "versionNumber": "0.0",
    "sourceType": "SOURCE_FILES",
    "envVars": [
      {
        "name": "MY_ENV_VAR",
        "value": "my-value",
        "isSecret": false,
        "valueHash": "a1b2c3"
      }
    ],
    "applyEnvVarsToBuild": false,
    "buildTag": "latest",
    "sourceFiles": [
      {
        "format": "TEXT",
        "content": "console.log('This is the main.js file');",
        "name": "src/main.js"
      }
    ],
    "gitRepoUrl": "string",
    "tarballUrl": "string",
    "gitHubGistUrl": "string",
    "actorPath": "actors/typescript-actor",
    "githubWebhookId": 0,
    "gitlabWebhookId": 0,
    "bitbucketWebhookId": "string"
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "record-not-found",
    "message": "The requested resource was not found."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
