```json
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-actor-version-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found - the requested resource does not exist.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

<h3 id="get-actor-version-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|object|true|none|none|
|» versionNumber|string|true|none|The version number of the Actor. Two numbers separated by a dot, that represent the `MAJOR.MINOR` part of the semantic versioning.|
|» sourceType|string \| null|true|none|Where the source code of the version lives.|
|» » *anyOf*|string|false|none|none|
|» » *anyOf*|null|false|none|none|
|» envVars|[object] \| null|false|none|Environment variables for the version.|
|» » *anyOf*|[object]|false|none|none|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» name|string|true|none|The name of the environment variable.|
|» value|string|false|none|The value of the environment variable. If `isSecret` is `true`, this value isn't returned by the API.|
|» isSecret|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether the environment variable is encrypted. Secret values aren't returned by the API.|
|» valueHash|string|false|none|A short hash of the secret value, to detect value changes. Returned only for secret environment variables, in place of `value`.|
|» » *anyOf*|null|false|none|none|
|» applyEnvVarsToBuild|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether to inject the environment variables at build time.|
|» buildTag|string \| null|false|none|The tag name to apply to a successful build of this version. Can be `null` when the version has no build tag.|
|» sourceFiles|[object]|false|none|Applies when the `sourceType` is `SOURCE_FILES`. Represents the Actor's file structure as an array of files and folders.|
|» » *anyOf*|object|false|none|Represents a single file in the Actor's source code.|
|» » format|string|false|none|Format of the file's content, `TEXT` for plain text and `BASE64` for encoded content.|
|» » content|string|false|none|The contents of the file. Interpreted based on the value of `format`.|
|» » name|string|true|none|The path of the file relative to the Actor's root directory.|
|» » *anyOf*|object|false|none|Represents a folder in the Actor's source code structure. Distinguished from<br>SourceCodeFile by the presence of the `folder` property set to `true`.<br>|
|» » name|string|true|none|The path of the folder relative to the Actor's root directory.|
|» » folder|boolean|true|none|Whether it's a folder. Distinguishes folders from files.|
|» gitRepoUrl|string \| null|false|none|URL of the Git repository to clone the source code from. Applies when the `sourceType` is `GIT_REPO`.|
|» tarballUrl|string \| null|false|none|URL to download the source code from as a zip archive. Applies when the `sourceType` is `TARBALL`.|
|» gitHubGistUrl|string \| null|false|none|URL of the GitHub Gist to clone the source code from. Applies when the `sourceType` is `GITHUB_GIST`.|
|» actorPath|string \| null|false|none|The Actor's directory inside the uploaded source, as a path relative to the upload root with `/` separators, for example `actors/typescript-actor`. Applies when the `sourceType` is `SOURCE_FILES` or `TARBALL`. When absent or `null`, the upload root is the Actor's directory. On a `TARBALL` version, only users with write access to the Actor get it. It has 1 to 255 characters, with no leading, trailing, or repeated `/` and no `.` or `..` segments.|
|» githubWebhookId|integer \| null|false|none|ID of the GitHub webhook that triggers a build on push. Present when build on push is enabled for a GitHub repository.|
|» gitlabWebhookId|integer \| null|false|none|ID of the GitLab webhook that triggers a build on push. Present when build on push is enabled for a GitLab repository.|
|» bitbucketWebhookId|string \| null|false|none|ID of the Bitbucket webhook that triggers a build on push. Present when build on push is enabled for a Bitbucket repository.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Delete Actor version

<a id="opIdactor_version_delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/versions/0.1 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/actors/{actorId}/versions/{versionNumber}`

Deletes a specific version of Actor's source code.


<h3 id="delete-actor-version-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|versionNumber|path|string|true|Actor version.|

> Example responses

> 204 Response

```json
{}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "record-not-found",
    "message": "The requested resource was not found."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content||Inline|

|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|

</aside>

## Update Actor version build on push

<a id="opIdactor_version_buildOnPush_put"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/versions/0.1/build-on-push \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "providerId": "github-app",
    "enabled": true
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/actors/{actorId}/versions/{versionNumber}/build-on-push`

Turns automatic builds on push on or off for an Actor version whose source is a git repository.

Enabling registers a push webhook on the repository through the connected git account given by `providerId`, so
that every push to the repository builds the version. Disabling turns the webhook off on GitHub, or removes it
on GitLab and Bitbucket.

You need write access to the Actor. The version must have its source type set to a git repository, and the
connected account must have permission to manage the repository's webhooks.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "providerId": "github-app",
  "enabled": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-actor-version-build-on-push-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|versionNumber|path|string|true|Actor version.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» providerId|body|string|true|The connected git account to register the push webhook through: `github-app` for the GitHub App, or the ID<br>of a connected GitLab or Bitbucket integration, as returned by the [Get git provider integrations](/api/v2/integrations-git-get) endpoint.<br>|
|» enabled|body|boolean|true|`true` registers the push webhook so that pushes to the repository build the version; `false` turns it off.|

```json
    "type": "invalid-input",

  }
}
```

</aside>

## Get list of environment variables of Actor version

<a id="opIdactor_version_envVars_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/versions/0.1/env-vars \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actors/{actorId}/versions/{versionNumber}/env-vars`

Gets the list of environment variables for a specific version of an Actor.
The response is a JSON object with the list of `EnvVar` objects, where each contains basic information about a single environment variable.


<h3 id="get-list-of-environment-variables-of-actor-version-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|versionNumber|path|string|true|Actor version.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "total": 5,
    "items": [
      {
        "name": "MY_ENV_VAR",
        "value": "my-value",
        "isSecret": false,
        "valueHash": "a1b2c3"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "record-not-found",
    "message": "The requested resource was not found."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-list-of-environment-variables-of-actor-version-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found - the requested resource does not exist.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

<h3 id="get-list-of-environment-variables-of-actor-version-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|object|true|none|none|
|» total|integer|true|none|none|
|» items|[object]|true|none|none|
|» » name|string|true|none|The name of the environment variable.|
|» » value|string|false|none|The value of the environment variable. If `isSecret` is `true`, this value isn't returned by the API.|
|» » isSecret|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether the environment variable is encrypted. Secret values aren't returned by the API.|
|» » valueHash|string|false|none|A short hash of the secret value, to detect value changes. Returned only for secret environment variables, in place of `value`.|

Status Code **400**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|error|object|true|none|none|
|» type|string|false|none|Machine-processable error type identifier.|
|» message|string|false|none|Human-readable error message describing what went wrong.|
|» data|object|false|none|Additional machine-readable details about the error. Present only for some error types.|

## Create environment variable in Actor version

<a id="opIdactor_version_envVars_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/versions/0.1/env-vars \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "ENV_VAR_NAME",
    "value": "my-env-var"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/actors/{actorId}/versions/{versionNumber}/env-vars`

Creates an environment variable of an Actor using values specified in an
`EnvVar` object passed as
JSON in the POST payload.

The request must specify `name` and `value` parameters (as strings) in the
JSON payload and a `Content-Type: application/json` HTTP header.

```
{
    "name": "ENV_VAR_NAME",
    "value": "my-env-var"
}
```

The response is the `EnvVar`
object as returned by the [Get environment variable of Actor version](/api/v2/actor-version-env-var-get)
endpoint.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "ENV_VAR_NAME",
  "value": "my-env-var"
}
```

<h3 id="create-environment-variable-in-actor-version-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|versionNumber|path|string|true|Actor version.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the environment variable. Can't contain `=`.|
|» value|body|string|true|The value of the environment variable.|
|» isSecret|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether the environment variable is encrypted. Secret values aren't returned by the API.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "name": "MY_ENV_VAR",
    "value": "my-value",
    "isSecret": false
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "record-not-found",
    "message": "The requested resource was not found."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 413 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "request-too-large",
    "message": "The POST payload is too large (limit: 9437184 bytes, actual length: 10485760 bytes)."
  }
}
```

> 415 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "unsupported-content-encoding",
    "message": "Content-Encoding \"bla\" is not supported."
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-environment-variable-in-actor-version-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found - the requested resource does not exist.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|

|415|Unsupported Media Type|Unsupported media type - the Content-Encoding of the request is not supported.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

<h3 id="create-environment-variable-in-actor-version-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **201**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|object|true|none|none|
|» name|string|true|none|The name of the environment variable.|
|» value|string|false|none|The value of the environment variable. If `isSecret` is `true`, this value isn't returned by the API.|
|» isSecret|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether the environment variable is encrypted. Secret values aren't returned by the API.|
|» valueHash|string|false|none|A short hash of the secret value, to detect value changes. Returned only for secret environment variables, in place of `value`.|

Status Code **400**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|error|object|true|none|none|
|» type|string|false|none|Machine-processable error type identifier.|
|» message|string|false|none|Human-readable error message describing what went wrong.|
|» data|object|false|none|Additional machine-readable details about the error. Present only for some error types.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|3d-secure-auth-failed|
|» type|access-right-already-exists|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Get environment variable of Actor version

<a id="opIdactor_version_envVar_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/versions/0.1/env-vars/MY_ENV_VAR \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actors/{actorId}/versions/{versionNumber}/env-vars/{envVarName}`

Gets an `EnvVar` object that
contains all the details about a specific environment variable of an Actor.

If `isSecret` is set to `true`, then `value` will never be returned.


<h3 id="get-environment-variable-of-actor-version-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|versionNumber|path|string|true|Actor version.|
|envVarName|path|string|true|The name of the environment variable|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "name": "MY_ENV_VAR",
    "value": "my-value",
    "isSecret": false
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "record-not-found",
    "message": "The requested resource was not found."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-environment-variable-of-actor-version-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found - the requested resource does not exist.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

<h3 id="get-environment-variable-of-actor-version-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|object|true|none|none|
|» name|string|true|none|The name of the environment variable.|
|» value|string|false|none|The value of the environment variable. If `isSecret` is `true`, this value isn't returned by the API.|
|» isSecret|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether the environment variable is encrypted. Secret values aren't returned by the API.|
|» valueHash|string|false|none|A short hash of the secret value, to detect value changes. Returned only for secret environment variables, in place of `value`.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Delete environment variable from Actor version

<a id="opIdactor_version_envVar_delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/versions/0.1/env-vars/MY_ENV_VAR \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/actors/{actorId}/versions/{versionNumber}/env-vars/{envVarName}`

Deletes a specific environment variable.

<h3 id="delete-environment-variable-from-actor-version-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|versionNumber|path|string|true|Actor version.|
|envVarName|path|string|true|The name of the environment variable|

> Example responses

> 204 Response

```json
{}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "record-not-found",
    "message": "The requested resource was not found."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

<h1 id="apify-api-actorsactor-builds">Actors/Actor builds</h1>

The API endpoints in this section allow you to manage your Apify Actors builds.


## Get list of Actor's builds

<a id="opIdactors_builds_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/builds \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actors/{actorId}/builds`

Gets the list of builds of a specific Actor. The response is a JSON with the
list of objects, where each object contains basic information about a single build.

The endpoint supports pagination using the `limit` and `offset` parameters
and it will not return more than 1000 records.

By default, the records are sorted by the `startedAt` field in ascending order,
therefore you can use pagination to incrementally fetch all builds while new
ones are still being started. To sort the records in descending order, use
the `desc=1` parameter.


<h3 id="get-list-of-actors-builds-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|offset|query|number(double)|false|Number of items that should be skipped at the start. The default value is `0`.<br>|
|limit|query|number(double)|false|Maximum number of items to return. The default value as well as the maximum is `1000`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "total": 1,
    "offset": 0,
    "limit": 1000,
    "desc": false,
    "count": 1,
    "items": [
      {
        "id": "HG7ML7M8z78YcAPEB",
        "actId": "janedoe~my-actor",
        "userId": "klmdEpoiojmdEMlk3",
        "status": "READY",
        "startedAt": "2019-11-30T07:34:24.202Z",
        "finishedAt": "2019-12-12T09:30:12.202Z",
        "usageTotalUsd": 0.02,
        "buildNumber": "0.1.1",
        "buildNumberInt": 10000,
        "meta": {
          "origin": "DEVELOPMENT",
          "clientIp": "172.234.12.34",
          "userAgent": "Mozilla/5.0 (iPad)",
          "githubActionsRunUrl": "https://github.com/apify/my-actor/actions/runs/123456789",
          "actorRunId": "HG7ML7M8z78YcAPEB",
          "webhookDispatchId": "Zib4xbZsmvZeK55ua"
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-list-of-actors-builds-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|object|true|none|none|
|» total|integer|true|none|The total number of items available across all pages.|
|» offset|integer|true|none|The starting position for this page of results.|
|» limit|integer|true|none|The maximum number of items returned per page.|
|» desc|boolean|true|none|Whether the results are sorted in descending order.|
|» count|integer|true|none|The number of items returned in this response.|
|» items|[object]|true|none|none|
|» » id|string|true|none|none|
|» » actId|string|false|none|none|
|» » userId|string|false|none|none|
|» » status|string|true|none|Status of an Actor job (run or build).|
|» » startedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|» » finishedAt|string \| null(date-time)|false|none|none|
|» » usageTotalUsd|number|false|none|Total cost in USD for this build. Requires authentication token to access.|
|» » buildNumber|string|true|none|none|
|» » buildNumberInt|integer|false|none|none|
|» » meta|object|false|none|none|
|» » » origin|string|true|none|none|
|» » » clientIp|string|false|none|IP address of the client that started the build.|
|» » » userAgent|string|false|none|User agent of the client that started the build. Returned only to the Actor owner.|
|» » » githubActionsRunUrl|string|false|none|URL of the GitHub Actions run that started the build. Present only for builds started from CI.|
|» » » actorRunId|string|false|none|ID of the Actor run that started the build. Returned only to the Actor owner.|
|» » » webhookDispatchId|string|false|none|ID of the webhook dispatch that started the build. Returned only to the Actor owner.|

## Build Actor

<a id="opIdactors_builds_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/builds?version=0.0' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/actors/{actorId}/builds`

Builds an Actor.
The response is the build object as returned by the
[Get Actor build](/api/v2/actor-build-get) endpoint.


<h3 id="build-actor-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|version|query|string|true|Actor version number to be built.|
|useCache|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1`, the system will use a cache to speed up the build<br>process. Pass `false` or `0` to build without the cache. By default,<br>cache is used.<br>|
|betaPackages|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then the Actor is built with beta versions of Apify NPM<br>packages. By default, the build uses `latest` packages.<br>|
|tag|query|string|false|Tag to be applied to the build on success. By default, the tag is taken<br>from Actor version's `buildTag` property.<br>|
|waitForFinish|query|number(double)|false|The maximum number of seconds the server waits for the build to finish.<br>By default it is `0`, the maximum value is `60`. <!-- MAX_ACTOR_JOB_ASYNC_WAIT_SECS --><br>If the build finishes in time then the returned build object will have a<br>terminal status (e.g. `SUCCEEDED`), otherwise it will have a transitional status (e.g. `RUNNING`).<br>|

<h3 id="build-actor-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|402|Payment Required|Payment required - the user has exceeded their usage limit, does not have enough credits, or the request lacks authentication and payment credentials.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found - the requested resource does not exist.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|408|Request Timeout|The HTTP request exceeded the timeout limit|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

<h3 id="build-actor-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **201**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|object|true|none|none|
|» id|string|true|none|none|
|» actId|string|true|none|none|
|» userId|string|true|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

## Get default Actor build

<a id="opIdactor_build_default_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/builds/default \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /v2/actors/{actorId}/builds/default`

Get the default build for an Actor.

Use the optional `waitForFinish` parameter to synchronously wait for the build to finish.
This avoids the need for periodic polling when waiting for the build to complete.

This endpoint does not require an authentication token. Instead, calls are authenticated using the Actor's unique ID.
However, if you access the endpoint without a token, certain attributes (e.g., `usageUsd` and `usageTotalUsd`) will be hidden.


<h3 id="get-default-actor-build-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|waitForFinish|query|number(double)|false|The maximum number of seconds the server waits for the build to finish.<br>By default it is `0`, the maximum value is `60`. <!-- MAX_ACTOR_JOB_ASYNC_WAIT_SECS --><br>If the build finishes in time then the returned build object will have a<br>terminal status (e.g. `SUCCEEDED`), otherwise it will have a transitional status (e.g. `RUNNING`).<br>|

## Get OpenAPI definition of Actor build

<a id="opIdactor_openapi_json_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/builds/{buildId}/openapi.json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /v2/actors/{actorId}/builds/{buildId}/openapi.json`

Get the OpenAPI definition for Actor builds. Two similar endpoints are available:

- [Get OpenAPI definition of Actor build](/api/v2/actor-openapi-json-get) (`/v2/actors/{actorId}/builds/{buildId}/openapi.json`): Requires both `actorId` and `buildId`. Use `default` as the `buildId` to get the OpenAPI schema for the default Actor build.

- [Get OpenAPI definition of Actor build](/api/v2/actor-build-openapi-json-get) (`/v2/actor-builds/{buildId}/openapi.json`): Requires only `buildId`.

Get the OpenAPI definition for a specific Actor build.

To fetch the default Actor build, simply pass `default` as the `buildId`.
Authentication is based on the build's unique ID. No authentication token is required.

:::note

You can also use the [Get OpenAPI definition of Actor build](/api/v2/actor-build-openapi-json-get) endpoint (`/v2/actor-builds/{buildId}/openapi.json`) to get the OpenAPI definition for a build.

:::


<h3 id="get-openapi-definition-of-actor-build-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|

## Get Actor build

<a id="opIdactors_build_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/builds/soSkq9ekdmfOslopH \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /v2/actors/{actorId}/builds/{buildId}`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

By passing the optional `waitForFinish` parameter the API endpoint will
synchronously wait for the build to finish.
This is useful to avoid periodic polling when waiting for an Actor build to
finish.

This endpoint does not require the authentication token. Instead, calls are authenticated using a hard-to-guess ID of the build. However,
if you access the endpoint without the token, certain attributes, such as `usageUsd` and `usageTotalUsd`, will be hidden.


<h3 id="get-actor-build-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|buildId|path|string|true|ID of the build, found in the build's Info tab.|
|waitForFinish|query|number(double)|false|The maximum number of seconds the server waits for the build to finish.<br>By default it is `0`, the maximum value is `60`. <!-- MAX_ACTOR_JOB_ASYNC_WAIT_SECS --><br>If the build finishes in time then the returned build object will have a<br>terminal status (e.g. `SUCCEEDED`), otherwise it will have a transitional status (e.g. `RUNNING`).<br>|

## Abort Actor build

<a id="opIdactors_build_abort_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/builds/soSkq9ekdmfOslopH/abort \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/actors/{actorId}/builds/{buildId}/abort`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**[DEPRECATED]** API endpoints related to build of the Actor were moved
under new namespace `actor-builds` ([Manage Actor builds](/api/v2/actor-builds)). Aborts an
Actor build and returns an object that contains all the details about the
build.

Only builds that are starting or running are aborted. For builds with status
`FINISHED`, `FAILED`, `ABORTING` and `TIMED-OUT` this call does nothing.


<h3 id="abort-actor-build-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|buildId|path|string|true|ID of the build, found in the build's Info tab.|

> Example responses

```json
{

    "id": "HG7ML7M8z78YcAPEB",

    "finishedAt": "2019-12-12T09:30:12.202Z",

    },

      "ACTOR_COMPUTE_UNITS": 0.02
    },
```

```json
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "record-not-found",
    "message": "The requested resource was not found."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

<h3 id="abort-actor-build-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found - the requested resource does not exist.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

<h1 id="apify-api-actorsactor-runs">Actors/Actor runs</h1>

The API endpoints in this section allow you to manage your Apify Actors runs.

Some API endpoints return run objects. If a run object includes usage costs in dollars, note that these values are calculated based on your effective unit pricing at the time of the query. As a result, the dollar amounts should be treated as informational only and not as exact figures.

For completed runs, aggregated fields such as `stats` or dollar usage totals are eventually consistent and update within a few seconds. For values that must match finalized totals, wait about 10 seconds after the run completed, then fetch the run again.

For more information about platform usage and resource calculations, see the [Usage and Resources documentation](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/running/usage-and-resources#usage).


## Get list of Actor's runs

<a id="opIdactors_runs_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/runs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actors/{actorId}/runs`

Gets the list of runs of a specific Actor. The response is a list of
objects, where each object contains basic information about a single Actor run.

The endpoint supports pagination using the `limit` and `offset` parameters
and it will not return more than 1000 array elements.

By default, the records are sorted by the `startedAt` field in ascending
order, therefore you can use pagination to incrementally fetch all records while
new ones are still being created. To sort the records in descending order, use
`desc=1` parameter. You can also filter runs by status ([available
statuses](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/running/runs-and-builds#lifecycle)).


<h3 id="get-list-of-actors-runs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|offset|query|number(double)|false|Number of items that should be skipped at the start. The default value is `0`.<br>|
|limit|query|number(double)|false|Maximum number of items to return. The default value as well as the maximum is `1000`.<br>|
|status|query|[string]|false|Single status or comma-separated list of statuses, see ([available<br>statuses](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/running/runs-and-builds#lifecycle)). Used to filter runs by the specified statuses only.<br>|
|startedAfter|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter runs that started after the specified date and time (inclusive).<br>The value must be a valid ISO 8601 datetime string (UTC).<br>|
|startedBefore|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter runs that started before the specified date and time (inclusive).<br>The value must be a valid ISO 8601 datetime string (UTC).<br>|
|deployment|query|[string]|false|Single Actor Standby deployment or comma-separated list of deployments (`SINGLE_TENANT`, `MULTI_TENANT_FREE_USERS`,<br>`MULTI_TENANT_PAYING_USERS` or `MULTI_TENANT_OWNER_PAID`). Used to filter Actor Standby runs by the pool that<br>serves them. Requires the `status` parameter with only non-terminal statuses (`READY`, `RUNNING`, `TIMING-OUT` or<br>`ABORTING`).<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "total": 2,
    "offset": 0,
    "limit": 1000,
    "desc": false,
    "count": 2,
    "items": [
      {
        "id": "HG7ML7M8z78YcAPEB",
        "actId": "HDSasDasz78YcAPEB",
```

|200|X-Apify-Pagination-Limit|string||The maximum number of items returned per page.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Run Actor

<a id="opIdactors_runs_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/runs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "foo": "bar"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/actors/{actorId}/runs`

Runs an Actor and immediately returns without waiting for the run to finish.

The POST payload including its `Content-Type` header is passed as `INPUT` to
the Actor (usually `application/json`).

The Actor is started with the default options; you can override them using
various URL query parameters.

The response is the Run object as returned by the [Get Actor run](/api/v2/actor-run-get) API
endpoint.

If you want to wait for the run to finish and receive the actual output of
the Actor as the response, please use the [Run Actor synchronously and get key-value store record](/api/v2/actor-run-sync-post)
or [Run Actor synchronously and get dataset items](/api/v2/actor-run-sync-get-dataset-items-post)
endpoint instead.

To fetch the Actor run results that are typically stored in the default
dataset, you'll need to pass the ID received in the `defaultDatasetId` field
received in the response JSON to the [Get dataset items](/api/v2/dataset-items-get)
API endpoint.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "foo": "bar"
}
```

<h3 id="run-actor-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|timeout|query|number(double)|false|Optional timeout for the run, in seconds. By default, the run uses the timeout from its configuration.<br>|
|memory|query|number(double)|false|Memory limit for the run, in megabytes. You can set the amount of memory to a power of 2 with a minimum of 128.<br>By default, the run uses the memory limit from its configuration. Don't change this value unless the Actor's<br>documentation recommends it or you're aware of the consequences.<br>|
|maxItems|query|number(double)|false|Specifies the maximum number of dataset items that will be charged for pay-per-result Actors.<br>This does NOT guarantee that the Actor will return only this many items.<br>It only ensures you won't be charged for more than this number of items.<br>Only works for pay-per-result Actors.<br>Value can be accessed in the actor run using `ACTOR_MAX_PAID_DATASET_ITEMS` environment variable.<br>|
|maxTotalChargeUsd|query|number(double)|false|Specifies the maximum total cost of the run.<br>Use it to cap the total amount charged for all pricing models.<br>You can access the maximum cost in your Actor<br>by using the `ACTOR_MAX_TOTAL_CHARGE_USD` environment variable.<br>|
|restartOnError|query|boolean|false|Determines whether the run will be restarted if it fails.<br>|
|build|query|string|false|Specifies the Actor build to run. It can be either a build tag or build number.<br>By default, the run uses the build from its configuration (typically `latest`).<br>|
|waitForFinish|query|number(double)|false|The maximum number of seconds the server waits for the run to finish. By<br>default it is `0`, the maximum value is `60`. <!-- MAX_ACTOR_JOB_ASYNC_WAIT_SECS --><br>If the run finishes in time then the returned run object will have a terminal status (e.g. `SUCCEEDED`),<br>otherwise it will have a transitional status (e.g. `RUNNING`).<br>|
|webhooks|query|string|false|Specifies optional webhooks associated with the Actor run, which can be used to receive a notification<br>e.g. when the Actor finished or failed. The value is a Base64-encoded JSON array whose items follow<br>the WebhookRepresentation schema. For more information, see<br>[Webhooks documentation](https://docs.apify.com/platform/integrations/webhooks).<br>|
|forcePermissionLevel|query|string|false|Overrides the Actor's permission level for this specific run. Use to test restricted permissions<br>before deploying changes to your Actor or to temporarily elevate or restrict access. If you don't specify this<br>parameter, the Actor uses its configured default permission level. For more information on permissions, see the<br>[documentation](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/development/permissions).<br>|
|body|body|object|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|forcePermissionLevel|LIMITED_PERMISSIONS|
|forcePermissionLevel|FULL_PERMISSIONS|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Run Actor synchronously and get key-value store record (GET)

<a id="opIdactor_runSync_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/run-sync \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actors/{actorId}/run-sync`

Runs a specific Actor and returns a key-value store record. The response contains the
record stored under the `OUTPUT` key in the run's default key-value store.
This is a legacy approach that has been replaced by the Actor
[output object](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/development/actor-definition/output-schema#output-object-definition);
the record may not exist, in which case the response contains no data. Use the
`outputRecordKey` query parameter to return a different record.
The run must finish in 300<!-- MAX_ACTOR_JOB_SYNC_WAIT_SECS --> seconds
otherwise the API endpoint returns a timeout error.
The Actor is not passed any input.

Beware that it might be impossible to maintain an idle HTTP connection for a
long period of time,
due to client timeout or network conditions. Make sure your HTTP client is
configured to have a long enough connection timeout.
If the connection breaks, you will not receive any information about the run
and its status.

To run the Actor asynchronously, use the [Run Actor](/api/v2/actors-runs-post) API endpoint instead.


<h3 id="run-actor-synchronously-and-get-key-value-store-record-get-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|outputRecordKey|query|string|false|Key of the record from the run's default key-value store to return in the<br>response. Defaults to `OUTPUT`. Actors aren't required to store a record<br>under this key, so if it doesn't exist the response contains no data.<br>|
|timeout|query|number(double)|false|Optional timeout for the run, in seconds. By default, the run uses the timeout from its configuration.<br>|
|memory|query|number(double)|false|Memory limit for the run, in megabytes. You can set the amount of memory to a power of 2 with a minimum of 128.<br>By default, the run uses the memory limit from its configuration. Don't change this value unless the Actor's<br>documentation recommends it or you're aware of the consequences.<br>|
|maxItems|query|number(double)|false|Specifies the maximum number of dataset items that will be charged for pay-per-result Actors.<br>This does NOT guarantee that the Actor will return only this many items.<br>It only ensures you won't be charged for more than this number of items.<br>Only works for pay-per-result Actors.<br>Value can be accessed in the actor run using `ACTOR_MAX_PAID_DATASET_ITEMS` environment variable.<br>|
|maxTotalChargeUsd|query|number(double)|false|Specifies the maximum total cost of the run.<br>Use it to cap the total amount charged for all pricing models.<br>You can access the maximum cost in your Actor<br>by using the `ACTOR_MAX_TOTAL_CHARGE_USD` environment variable.<br>|
|restartOnError|query|boolean|false|Determines whether the run will be restarted if it fails.<br>|
|build|query|string|false|Specifies the Actor build to run. It can be either a build tag or build number.<br>By default, the run uses the build from its configuration (typically `latest`).<br>|
|webhooks|query|string|false|Specifies optional webhooks associated with the Actor run, which can be used to receive a notification<br>e.g. when the Actor finished or failed. The value is a Base64-encoded JSON array whose items follow<br>the WebhookRepresentation schema. For more information, see<br>[Webhooks documentation](https://docs.apify.com/platform/integrations/webhooks).<br>|
|forcePermissionLevel|query|string|false|Overrides the Actor's permission level for this specific run. Use to test restricted permissions<br>before deploying changes to your Actor or to temporarily elevate or restrict access. If you don't specify this<br>parameter, the Actor uses its configured default permission level. For more information on permissions, see the<br>[documentation](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/development/permissions).<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|forcePermissionLevel|LIMITED_PERMISSIONS|
|forcePermissionLevel|FULL_PERMISSIONS|

<aside class="warning">

httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Run Actor synchronously and get key-value store record

<a id="opIdactor_runSync_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/run-sync \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "foo": "bar"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/actors/{actorId}/run-sync`

Runs a specific Actor and returns a key-value store record.

The POST payload including its `Content-Type` header is passed as `INPUT` to
the Actor (usually <code>application/json</code>).

The response contains the record stored under the `OUTPUT` key in the run's
default key-value store. This is a legacy approach that has been replaced by
the Actor [output object](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/development/actor-definition/output-schema#output-object-definition);
Actors aren't required to store a record under this key, so the response may
not contain any data. Use the `outputRecordKey` query parameter to return a
different record.

The Actor is started with the default options; you can override them using
various URL query parameters.
If the Actor run exceeds 300<!-- MAX_ACTOR_JOB_SYNC_WAIT_SECS --> seconds,
the HTTP response will have status 408 (Request Timeout).

Beware that it might be impossible to maintain an idle HTTP connection for a
long period of time, due to client timeout or network conditions. Make sure your HTTP client is
configured to have a long enough connection timeout.
If the connection breaks, you will not receive any information about the run
and its status.

To run the Actor asynchronously, use the [Run Actor](/api/v2/actors-runs-post) API endpoint instead.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "foo": "bar"
}
```

<h3 id="run-actor-synchronously-and-get-key-value-store-record-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|outputRecordKey|query|string|false|Key of the record from the run's default key-value store to return in the<br>response. Defaults to `OUTPUT`. Actors aren't required to store a record<br>under this key, so if it doesn't exist the response contains no data.<br>|
|timeout|query|number(double)|false|Optional timeout for the run, in seconds. By default, the run uses the timeout from its configuration.<br>|
|memory|query|number(double)|false|Memory limit for the run, in megabytes. You can set the amount of memory to a power of 2 with a minimum of 128.<br>By default, the run uses the memory limit from its configuration. Don't change this value unless the Actor's<br>documentation recommends it or you're aware of the consequences.<br>|
|maxItems|query|number(double)|false|Specifies the maximum number of dataset items that will be charged for pay-per-result Actors.<br>This does NOT guarantee that the Actor will return only this many items.<br>It only ensures you won't be charged for more than this number of items.<br>Only works for pay-per-result Actors.<br>Value can be accessed in the actor run using `ACTOR_MAX_PAID_DATASET_ITEMS` environment variable.<br>|
|maxTotalChargeUsd|query|number(double)|false|Specifies the maximum total cost of the run.<br>Use it to cap the total amount charged for all pricing models.<br>You can access the maximum cost in your Actor<br>by using the `ACTOR_MAX_TOTAL_CHARGE_USD` environment variable.<br>|
|restartOnError|query|boolean|false|Determines whether the run will be restarted if it fails.<br>|
|build|query|string|false|Specifies the Actor build to run. It can be either a build tag or build number.<br>By default, the run uses the build from its configuration (typically `latest`).<br>|
|webhooks|query|string|false|Specifies optional webhooks associated with the Actor run, which can be used to receive a notification<br>e.g. when the Actor finished or failed. The value is a Base64-encoded JSON array whose items follow<br>the WebhookRepresentation schema. For more information, see<br>[Webhooks documentation](https://docs.apify.com/platform/integrations/webhooks).<br>|
|forcePermissionLevel|query|string|false|Overrides the Actor's permission level for this specific run. Use to test restricted permissions<br>before deploying changes to your Actor or to temporarily elevate or restrict access. If you don't specify this<br>parameter, the Actor uses its configured default permission level. For more information on permissions, see the<br>[documentation](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/development/permissions).<br>|
|body|body|object|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|forcePermissionLevel|LIMITED_PERMISSIONS|
|forcePermissionLevel|FULL_PERMISSIONS|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "bar": "foo"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 402 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "x402-payment-required",
    "message": "Please provide X402-PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header with the payment. See https://x402.org."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "record-not-found",
    "message": "The requested resource was not found."
  }
}
```

> 408 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "run-timeout-exceeded",
    "message": "Actor run exceeded the timeout of 300 seconds for this API endpoint"
  }
}
```

> 415 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "unsupported-content-encoding",
    "message": "Content-Encoding \"bla\" is not supported."
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

<h3 id="run-actor-synchronously-and-get-key-value-store-record-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|402|Payment Required|Payment required - the user has exceeded their usage limit, does not have enough credits, or the request lacks authentication and payment credentials.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found - the requested resource does not exist.|Inline|
|408|Request Timeout|The HTTP request exceeded the timeout limit|Inline|
|415|Unsupported Media Type|Unsupported media type - the Content-Encoding of the request is not supported.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Run Actor synchronously and get dataset items (GET)

<a id="opIdactor_runSyncGetDatasetItems_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/run-sync-get-dataset-items \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actors/{actorId}/run-sync-get-dataset-items`

Runs a specific Actor and returns its dataset items.
The run must finish in 300<!-- MAX_ACTOR_JOB_SYNC_WAIT_SECS --> seconds
otherwise the API endpoint returns a timeout error.
The Actor is not passed any input.

It allows to send all possible options in parameters from [Get dataset items](/api/v2/dataset-items-get) API endpoint.

Beware that it might be impossible to maintain an idle HTTP connection for a
long period of time,
due to client timeout or network conditions. Make sure your HTTP client is
configured to have a long enough connection timeout.
If the connection breaks, you will not receive any information about the run
and its status.

To run the Actor asynchronously, use the [Run Actor](/api/v2/actors-runs-post) API endpoint instead.


<h3 id="run-actor-synchronously-and-get-dataset-items-get-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|timeout|query|number(double)|false|Optional timeout for the run, in seconds. By default, the run uses the timeout from its configuration.<br>|
|memory|query|number(double)|false|Memory limit for the run, in megabytes. You can set the amount of memory to a power of 2 with a minimum of 128.<br>By default, the run uses the memory limit from its configuration. Don't change this value unless the Actor's<br>documentation recommends it or you're aware of the consequences.<br>|
|maxItems|query|number(double)|false|Specifies the maximum number of dataset items that will be charged for pay-per-result Actors.<br>This does NOT guarantee that the Actor will return only this many items.<br>It only ensures you won't be charged for more than this number of items.<br>Only works for pay-per-result Actors.<br>Value can be accessed in the actor run using `ACTOR_MAX_PAID_DATASET_ITEMS` environment variable.<br>|
|maxTotalChargeUsd|query|number(double)|false|Specifies the maximum total cost of the run.<br>Use it to cap the total amount charged for all pricing models.<br>You can access the maximum cost in your Actor<br>by using the `ACTOR_MAX_TOTAL_CHARGE_USD` environment variable.<br>|
|restartOnError|query|boolean|false|Determines whether the run will be restarted if it fails.<br>|
|build|query|string|false|Specifies the Actor build to run. It can be either a build tag or build number.<br>By default, the run uses the build from its configuration (typically `latest`).<br>|
|webhooks|query|string|false|Specifies optional webhooks associated with the Actor run, which can be used to receive a notification<br>e.g. when the Actor finished or failed. The value is a Base64-encoded JSON array whose items follow<br>the WebhookRepresentation schema. For more information, see<br>[Webhooks documentation](https://docs.apify.com/platform/integrations/webhooks).<br>|
|forcePermissionLevel|query|string|false|Overrides the Actor's permission level for this specific run. Use to test restricted permissions<br>before deploying changes to your Actor or to temporarily elevate or restrict access. If you don't specify this<br>parameter, the Actor uses its configured default permission level. For more information on permissions, see the<br>[documentation](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/development/permissions).<br>|
|format|query|string|false|Format of the results, possible values are: `json`, `jsonl`, `csv`, `html`, `xlsx`, `xml` and `rss`. The default value is `json`.<br>|
|clean|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then the API endpoint returns only non-empty items and skips hidden fields (i.e. fields starting with the # character).<br>The `clean` parameter is just a shortcut for `skipHidden=true` and `skipEmpty=true` parameters.<br>Note that since some objects might be skipped from the output, that the result might contain less items than the `limit` value.<br>|
|offset|query|number(double)|false|Number of items that should be skipped at the start. The default value is `0`.<br>|
|limit|query|number(double)|false|Maximum number of items to return. By default there is no limit.|
|fields|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of fields which should be picked from the items, only these fields will remain in the resulting record objects.<br>Note that the fields in the outputted items are sorted the same way as they are specified in the `fields` query parameter.<br>You can use this feature to effectively fix the output format.<br>|
|outputFields|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of output field names that positionally rename the fields specified in the `fields` parameter.<br>For example, `?fields=headline,url&outputFields=title,link` renames `headline` to `title` and `url` to `link` in the output.<br>The number of names in `outputFields` must match the number of names in `fields`.<br>Requires the `fields` parameter to be specified as well.<br>|
|omit|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of fields which should be omitted from the items.|
|unwind|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of fields which should be unwound, in order which they should be processed. Each field should be either an array or an object.<br>If the field is an array then every element of the array will become a separate record and merged with parent object.<br>If the unwound field is an object then it is merged with the parent object.<br>If the unwound field is missing or its value is neither an array nor an object and therefore cannot be merged with a parent object then the item gets preserved as it is.<br>Note that the unwound items ignore the `desc` parameter.<br>|
|flatten|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of fields which should transform nested objects into flat structures.<br><br>For example, with `flatten="foo"` the object `{"foo":{"bar": "hello"}}` is turned into `{"foo.bar": "hello"}`.<br><br>The original object with properties is replaced with the flattened object.<br>|
|desc|query|boolean|false|By default, results are returned in the same order as they were stored.<br>To reverse the order, set this parameter to `true` or `1`.<br>|
|attachment|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then the response will define the `Content-Disposition:<br>attachment` header, forcing a web browser to download the file rather<br>than to display it. By default this header is not present.<br>|
|delimiter|query|string|false|A delimiter character for CSV files, only used if `format=csv`. You<br>might need to URL-encode the character (e.g. use `%09` for tab or `%3B`<br>for semicolon). The default delimiter is a simple comma (`,`).<br>|
|bom|query|boolean|false|All text responses are encoded in UTF-8 encoding. By default, the<br>`format=csv` files are prefixed with the UTF-8 Byte Order Mark (BOM), while `json`, `jsonl`, `xml`, `html` and `rss` files are not.<br><br>If you want to override this default behavior, specify `bom=1` query parameter to include the BOM or `bom=0` to skip it.<br>|
|xmlRoot|query|string|false|Overrides default root element name of `xml` output. By default the root element is `items`.<br>|
|xmlRow|query|string|false|Overrides default element name that wraps each page or page function result object in `xml` output. By default the element name is `item`.<br>|
|skipHeaderRow|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then header row in the `csv` format is skipped.|
|skipHidden|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then hidden fields are skipped from the output, i.e. fields starting with the `#` character.<br>|
|skipEmpty|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then empty items are skipped from the output.<br><br>Note that if used, the results might contain less items than the limit value.<br>|
|simplified|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then, the endpoint applies the `fields=url,pageFunctionResult,errorInfo`<br>and `unwind=pageFunctionResult` query parameters. This feature is used to emulate simplified results provided by the<br>legacy Apify Crawler product and it's not recommended to use it in new integrations.<br>|
|view|query|string|false|Defines the view configuration for dataset items based on the schema definition.<br>This parameter determines how the data will be filtered and presented.<br>For complete specification details, see the [dataset schema documentation](/storage/dataset-schema).<br>|
|skipFailedPages|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then, the all the items with errorInfo property will be skipped from the output.<br><br>This feature is here to emulate functionality of API version 1 used for the legacy Apify Crawler product and it's not recommended to use it in new integrations.<br>|
|feedTitle|query|string|false|Overrides the auto-generated RSS channel `<title>` element.<br>Only used when `format=rss`. If not provided, the title defaults to `Dataset <label>`.<br>|
|feedDescription|query|string|false|Overrides the auto-generated RSS channel `<description>` element.<br>Only used when `format=rss`. If not provided, the description defaults to `Items in dataset with id "<datasetId>".`<br>|

## Run Actor synchronously and get dataset items

<a id="opIdactor_runSyncGetDatasetItems_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/run-sync-get-dataset-items \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "foo": "bar"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/actors/{actorId}/run-sync-get-dataset-items`

Runs a specific Actor and returns its dataset items.

The POST payload including its `Content-Type` header is passed as `INPUT` to
the Actor (usually `application/json`).
The HTTP response contains the Actors dataset items, while the format of
items depends on specifying dataset items' `format` parameter.

You can send all the same options in parameters as the [Get dataset items](/api/v2/dataset-items-get) API endpoint.

The Actor is started with the default options; you can override them using
URL query parameters.
If the Actor run exceeds 300<!-- MAX_ACTOR_JOB_SYNC_WAIT_SECS --> seconds,
the HTTP response will return the 408 status code (Request Timeout).

Beware that it might be impossible to maintain an idle HTTP connection for a
long period of time,
due to client timeout or network conditions. Make sure your HTTP client is
configured to have a long enough connection timeout.
If the connection breaks, you will not receive any information about the run
and its status.

To run the Actor asynchronously, use the [Run Actor](/api/v2/actors-runs-post) API endpoint instead.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "foo": "bar"
}
```

<h3 id="run-actor-synchronously-and-get-dataset-items-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|timeout|query|number(double)|false|Optional timeout for the run, in seconds. By default, the run uses the timeout from its configuration.<br>|
|memory|query|number(double)|false|Memory limit for the run, in megabytes. You can set the amount of memory to a power of 2 with a minimum of 128.<br>By default, the run uses the memory limit from its configuration. Don't change this value unless the Actor's<br>documentation recommends it or you're aware of the consequences.<br>|
|maxItems|query|number(double)|false|Specifies the maximum number of dataset items that will be charged for pay-per-result Actors.<br>This does NOT guarantee that the Actor will return only this many items.<br>It only ensures you won't be charged for more than this number of items.<br>Only works for pay-per-result Actors.<br>Value can be accessed in the actor run using `ACTOR_MAX_PAID_DATASET_ITEMS` environment variable.<br>|
|maxTotalChargeUsd|query|number(double)|false|Specifies the maximum total cost of the run.<br>Use it to cap the total amount charged for all pricing models.<br>You can access the maximum cost in your Actor<br>by using the `ACTOR_MAX_TOTAL_CHARGE_USD` environment variable.<br>|
|restartOnError|query|boolean|false|Determines whether the run will be restarted if it fails.<br>|
|build|query|string|false|Specifies the Actor build to run. It can be either a build tag or build number.<br>By default, the run uses the build from its configuration (typically `latest`).<br>|
|webhooks|query|string|false|Specifies optional webhooks associated with the Actor run, which can be used to receive a notification<br>e.g. when the Actor finished or failed. The value is a Base64-encoded JSON array whose items follow<br>the WebhookRepresentation schema. For more information, see<br>[Webhooks documentation](https://docs.apify.com/platform/integrations/webhooks).<br>|
|forcePermissionLevel|query|string|false|Overrides the Actor's permission level for this specific run. Use to test restricted permissions<br>before deploying changes to your Actor or to temporarily elevate or restrict access. If you don't specify this<br>parameter, the Actor uses its configured default permission level. For more information on permissions, see the<br>[documentation](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/development/permissions).<br>|
|format|query|string|false|Format of the results, possible values are: `json`, `jsonl`, `csv`, `html`, `xlsx`, `xml` and `rss`. The default value is `json`.<br>|
|clean|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then the API endpoint returns only non-empty items and skips hidden fields (i.e. fields starting with the # character).<br>The `clean` parameter is just a shortcut for `skipHidden=true` and `skipEmpty=true` parameters.<br>Note that since some objects might be skipped from the output, that the result might contain less items than the `limit` value.<br>|
|offset|query|number(double)|false|Number of items that should be skipped at the start. The default value is `0`.<br>|
|limit|query|number(double)|false|Maximum number of items to return. By default there is no limit.|
|fields|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of fields which should be picked from the items, only these fields will remain in the resulting record objects.<br>Note that the fields in the outputted items are sorted the same way as they are specified in the `fields` query parameter.<br>You can use this feature to effectively fix the output format.<br>|
|outputFields|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of output field names that positionally rename the fields specified in the `fields` parameter.<br>For example, `?fields=headline,url&outputFields=title,link` renames `headline` to `title` and `url` to `link` in the output.<br>The number of names in `outputFields` must match the number of names in `fields`.<br>Requires the `fields` parameter to be specified as well.<br>|
|omit|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of fields which should be omitted from the items.|
|unwind|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of fields which should be unwound, in order which they should be processed. Each field should be either an array or an object.<br>If the field is an array then every element of the array will become a separate record and merged with parent object.<br>If the unwound field is an object then it is merged with the parent object.<br>If the unwound field is missing or its value is neither an array nor an object and therefore cannot be merged with a parent object then the item gets preserved as it is.<br>Note that the unwound items ignore the `desc` parameter.<br>|
|flatten|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of fields which should transform nested objects into flat structures.<br><br>For example, with `flatten="foo"` the object `{"foo":{"bar": "hello"}}` is turned into `{"foo.bar": "hello"}`.<br><br>The original object with properties is replaced with the flattened object.<br>|
|desc|query|boolean|false|By default, results are returned in the same order as they were stored.<br>To reverse the order, set this parameter to `true` or `1`.<br>|
|attachment|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then the response will define the `Content-Disposition:<br>attachment` header, forcing a web browser to download the file rather<br>than to display it. By default this header is not present.<br>|
|delimiter|query|string|false|A delimiter character for CSV files, only used if `format=csv`. You<br>might need to URL-encode the character (e.g. use `%09` for tab or `%3B`<br>for semicolon). The default delimiter is a simple comma (`,`).<br>|
|bom|query|boolean|false|All text responses are encoded in UTF-8 encoding. By default, the<br>`format=csv` files are prefixed with the UTF-8 Byte Order Mark (BOM), while `json`, `jsonl`, `xml`, `html` and `rss` files are not.<br><br>If you want to override this default behavior, specify `bom=1` query parameter to include the BOM or `bom=0` to skip it.<br>|
|xmlRoot|query|string|false|Overrides default root element name of `xml` output. By default the root element is `items`.<br>|
|xmlRow|query|string|false|Overrides default element name that wraps each page or page function result object in `xml` output. By default the element name is `item`.<br>|
|skipHeaderRow|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then header row in the `csv` format is skipped.|
|skipHidden|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then hidden fields are skipped from the output, i.e. fields starting with the `#` character.<br>|
|skipEmpty|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then empty items are skipped from the output.<br><br>Note that if used, the results might contain less items than the limit value.<br>|
|simplified|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then, the endpoint applies the `fields=url,pageFunctionResult,errorInfo`<br>and `unwind=pageFunctionResult` query parameters. This feature is used to emulate simplified results provided by the<br>legacy Apify Crawler product and it's not recommended to use it in new integrations.<br>|
|view|query|string|false|Defines the view configuration for dataset items based on the schema definition.<br>This parameter determines how the data will be filtered and presented.<br>For complete specification details, see the [dataset schema documentation](/storage/dataset-schema).<br>|
|skipFailedPages|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then, the all the items with errorInfo property will be skipped from the output.<br><br>This feature is here to emulate functionality of API version 1 used for the legacy Apify Crawler product and it's not recommended to use it in new integrations.<br>|
|feedTitle|query|string|false|Overrides the auto-generated RSS channel `<title>` element.<br>Only used when `format=rss`. If not provided, the title defaults to `Dataset <label>`.<br>|
|feedDescription|query|string|false|Overrides the auto-generated RSS channel `<description>` element.<br>Only used when `format=rss`. If not provided, the description defaults to `Items in dataset with id "<datasetId>".`<br>|
|body|body|object|true|none|

## Resurrect Actor run

<a id="opIdactor_run_resurrect_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/runs/3KH8gEpp4d8uQSe8T/resurrect \
  -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/actors/{actorId}/runs/{runId}/resurrect`

**[DEPRECATED]** API endpoints related to run of the Actor were moved under
new namespace `actor-runs`
([Manage Actor runs](/api/v2/actor-runs)). Resurrects a finished
Actor run and returns an object that contains all the details about the
resurrected run.

Only finished runs, i.e. runs with status `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`, `ABORTED`
and `TIMED-OUT` can be resurrected.
Run status will be updated to RUNNING and its container will be restarted
with the same storages
(the same behaviour as when the run gets migrated to the new server).

For more information, see the [Actor
docs](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/running/runs-and-builds#resurrect-a-finished-run).


<h3 id="resurrect-actor-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|runId|path|string|true|Actor run ID.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Get Actor's last run

<a id="opIdactor_runs_last_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/runs/last \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actors/{actorId}/runs/last`

This is not a single endpoint, but an entire group of endpoints that lets you to
retrieve and manage the last run of given Actor or any of its default storages.
All the endpoints require an authentication token.

The base path represents the last Actor run object is:

`/v2/actors/{actorId}/runs/last{?token,status,origin}`

Using the `status` query parameter you can ensure to only get a run with a certain status
(e.g. `status=SUCCEEDED`). Similarly, the `origin` query parameter filters runs by the means
by which they were started (e.g. `origin=API`). The output of this endpoint and other query
parameters are the same as in the [Get Actor run](/api/v2/actor-run-get) endpoint.

##### Convenience endpoints for last Actor run

* [Last Actor run's default dataset](/api/v2/last-actor-runs-default-dataset)

* [Last Actor run's default key-value store](/api/v2/last-actor-runs-default-key-value-store)

* [Last Actor run's default request queue](/api/v2/last-actor-runs-default-request-queue)

* [Last Actor run's log](/api/v2/last-actor-runs-log)


<h3 id="get-actors-last-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|status|query|string|false|Filter for the run status.|
|origin|query|string|false|Filter for the run origin, i.e. the means by which the run was started.|
|waitForFinish|query|number(double)|false|The maximum number of seconds the server waits for the run to finish. By<br>default it is `0`, the maximum value is `60`. <!-- MAX_ACTOR_JOB_ASYNC_WAIT_SECS --><br>If the run finishes in time then the returned run object will have a terminal status (e.g. `SUCCEEDED`),<br>otherwise it will have a transitional status (e.g. `RUNNING`).<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|origin|DEVELOPMENT|
|origin|WEB|
|origin|API|
|origin|SCHEDULER|
|origin|TEST|
|origin|WEBHOOK|
|origin|ACTOR|
|origin|CLI|
|origin|CI|
|origin|STANDBY|
|origin|MCP|
