<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Get Actor run

<a id="opIdactors_run_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/runs/3KH8gEpp4d8uQSe8T \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actors/{actorId}/runs/{runId}`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**[DEPRECATED]** API endpoints related to run of the Actor were moved under
new namespace `actor-runs`
([Manage Actor runs](/api/v2/actor-runs)).

Gets an object that contains all the details about a specific run of an Actor.

By passing the optional `waitForFinish` parameter the API endpoint will
synchronously wait for the run to finish.
This is useful to avoid periodic polling when waiting for Actor run to
complete.

This endpoint does not require the authentication token. Instead, calls are authenticated using a hard-to-guess ID of the run. However,
if you access the endpoint without the token, certain attributes, such as `usageUsd` and `usageTotalUsd`, will be hidden.


<h3 id="get-actor-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|runId|path|string|true|Actor run ID.|
|waitForFinish|query|number(double)|false|The maximum number of seconds the server waits for the run to finish. By<br>default it is `0`, the maximum value is `60`. <!-- MAX_ACTOR_JOB_ASYNC_WAIT_SECS --><br>If the run finishes in time then the returned run object will have a terminal status (e.g. `SUCCEEDED`),<br>otherwise it will have a transitional status (e.g. `RUNNING`).<br>|

## Abort Actor run

<a id="opIdactors_run_abort_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/runs/3KH8gEpp4d8uQSe8T/abort \
  -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/actors/{actorId}/runs/{runId}/abort`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**[DEPRECATED]** API endpoints related to run of the Actor were moved under
new namespace `actor-runs`
([Manage Actor runs](/api/v2/actor-runs)). Aborts an Actor run and
returns an object that contains all the details about the run.

Only runs that are starting or running are aborted. For runs with status
`FINISHED`, `FAILED`, `ABORTING` and `TIMED-OUT` this call does nothing.


<h3 id="abort-actor-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|runId|path|string|true|Actor run ID.|
|gracefully|query|boolean|false|If true passed, the Actor run will abort gracefully.<br>It will send `aborting` and `persistState` event into run and force-stop the run after 30 seconds.<br>It is helpful in cases where you plan to resurrect the run later.<br>|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Metamorph Actor run

<a id="opIdactors_run_metamorph_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/runs/3KH8gEpp4d8uQSe8T/metamorph?targetActorId=HDSasDasz78YcAPEB' \
  -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/actors/{actorId}/runs/{runId}/metamorph`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**[DEPRECATED]** API endpoints related to run of the Actor were moved under
new namespace `actor-runs`
([Manage Actor runs](/api/v2/actor-runs)). Transforms an Actor run
into a run of another Actor with a new input.

This is useful if you want to use another Actor to finish the work
of your current Actor run, without the need to create a completely new run
and waiting for its finish.
For the users of your Actors, the metamorph operation is transparent, they
will just see your Actor got the work done.

There is a limit on how many times you can metamorph a single run. You can
check the limit in [the Actor runtime limits](https://docs.apify.com/platform/limits#actor-limits).

Internally, the system stops the Docker container corresponding to the Actor
run and starts a new container using a different Docker image.
All the default storages are preserved and the new input is stored under the
`INPUT-METAMORPH-1` key in the same default key-value store.

For more information, see the [Actor docs](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/development/programming-interface/metamorph).


<h3 id="metamorph-actor-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|runId|path|string|true|Actor run ID.|
|targetActorId|query|string|true|ID of a target Actor that the run should be transformed into.|
|build|query|string|false|Optional build of the target Actor.<br><br>It can be either a build tag or build number. By default, the run uses<br>the build specified in the default run configuration for the target<br>Actor (typically `latest`).<br>|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

<h1 id="apify-api-actorswebhook-collection">Actors/Webhook collection</h1>

The API endpoint in this section allows you to get a list of webhooks of a specific Actor.


## Get list of Actor's webhooks

<a id="opIdactor_webhooks_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/webhooks \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actors/{actorId}/webhooks`

Gets the list of webhooks of a specific Actor. The response is a JSON with
the list of objects, where each object contains basic information about a single webhook.

The endpoint supports pagination using the `limit` and `offset` parameters
and it will not return more than 1000 records.

By default, the records are sorted by the `createdAt` field in ascending
order, to sort the records in descending order, use the `desc=1` parameter.


<h3 id="get-list-of-actors-webhooks-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|offset|query|number(double)|false|Number of items that should be skipped at the start. The default value is `0`.<br>|
|limit|query|number(double)|false|Maximum number of items to return. The default value as well as the maximum is `1000`.<br>|

> Example responses

<h1 id="apify-api-actor-builds">Actor builds</h1>

The API endpoints described in this section enable you to manage, and delete Apify Actor builds.

Note that if any returned build object contains usage in dollars, your effective
unit pricing at the time of query has been used for computation of this dollar equivalent, and hence it should be
used only for informative purposes.

You can learn more about platform usage in the [documentation](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/running/usage-and-resources#usage).


## Get list of user's Actor builds

<a id="opIdactorBuilds_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-builds \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actor-builds`

Gets a list of all builds for a user. The response is a JSON array of
objects, where each object contains basic information about a single build.

The endpoint supports pagination using the `limit` and `offset` parameters
and it will not return more than 1000 records.

By default, the records are sorted by the `startedAt` field in ascending
order. Therefore, you can use pagination to incrementally fetch all builds while
new ones are still being started. To sort the records in descending order, use
the `desc=1` parameter.


<h3 id="get-list-of-users-actor-builds-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|offset|query|number(double)|false|Number of items that should be skipped at the start. The default value is `0`.<br>|
|limit|query|number(double)|false|Maximum number of items to return. The default value as well as the maximum is `1000`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "total": 1,
    "offset": 0,
    "limit": 1000,
    "desc": false,
    "count": 1,
    "items": [
      {
        "id": "HG7ML7M8z78YcAPEB",
        "actId": "janedoe~my-actor",
        "userId": "klmdEpoiojmdEMlk3",
        "status": "READY",
        "startedAt": "2019-11-30T07:34:24.202Z",
        "finishedAt": "2019-12-12T09:30:12.202Z",
        "usageTotalUsd": 0.02,
        "buildNumber": "0.1.1",
        "buildNumberInt": 10000,
        "meta": {
          "origin": "DEVELOPMENT",
          "clientIp": "172.234.12.34",
          "userAgent": "Mozilla/5.0 (iPad)",
          "githubActionsRunUrl": "https://github.com/apify/my-actor/actions/runs/123456789",
          "actorRunId": "HG7ML7M8z78YcAPEB",
          "webhookDispatchId": "Zib4xbZsmvZeK55ua"
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|» total|integer|true|none|The total number of items available across all pages.|
|» offset|integer|true|none|The starting position for this page of results.|
|» limit|integer|true|none|The maximum number of items returned per page.|
|» desc|boolean|true|none|Whether the results are sorted in descending order.|
|» count|integer|true|none|The number of items returned in this response.|
|» items|[object]|true|none|none|
|» » id|string|true|none|none|
|» » actId|string|false|none|none|
|» » userId|string|false|none|none|
|» » status|string|true|none|Status of an Actor job (run or build).|
|» » startedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|none|

|» » usageTotalUsd|number|false|none|Total cost in USD for this build. Requires authentication token to access.|

|» » » webhookDispatchId|string|false|none|ID of the webhook dispatch that started the build. Returned only to the Actor owner.|

## Get Actor build

<a id="opIdactorBuild_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-builds/soSkq9ekdmfOslopH \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /v2/actor-builds/{buildId}`

Gets an object that contains all the details about a specific build of an
Actor.

By passing the optional `waitForFinish` parameter the API endpoint will
synchronously wait for the build to finish. This is useful to avoid periodic
polling when waiting for an Actor build to finish.

This endpoint does not require the authentication token. Instead, calls are authenticated using a hard-to-guess ID of the build. However,
if you access the endpoint without the token, certain attributes, such as `usageUsd` and `usageTotalUsd`, will be hidden.


<h3 id="get-actor-build-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|buildId|path|string|true|ID of the build, found in the build's Info tab.|
|waitForFinish|query|number(double)|false|The maximum number of seconds the server waits for the build to finish.<br>By default it is `0`, the maximum value is `60`. <!-- MAX_ACTOR_JOB_ASYNC_WAIT_SECS --><br>If the build finishes in time then the returned build object will have a<br>terminal status (e.g. `SUCCEEDED`), otherwise it will have a transitional status (e.g. `RUNNING`).<br>|

## Delete Actor build

<a id="opIdactorBuild_delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-builds/soSkq9ekdmfOslopH \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/actor-builds/{buildId}`

Delete the build. The build that is the current default build for the Actor
cannot be deleted.

Only users with build permissions for the Actor can delete builds.


<h3 id="delete-actor-build-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|buildId|path|string|true|ID of the build, found in the build's Info tab.|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "record-not-found",
    "message": "The requested resource was not found."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Abort Actor build

<a id="opIdactorBuild_abort_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-builds/soSkq9ekdmfOslopH/abort \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/actor-builds/{buildId}/abort`

Aborts an Actor build and returns an object that contains all the details
about the build.

Only builds that are starting or running are aborted. For builds with status
`FINISHED`, `FAILED`, `ABORTING` and `TIMED-OUT` this call does nothing.


<h3 id="abort-actor-build-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|buildId|path|string|true|ID of the build, found in the build's Info tab.|

<h3 id="abort-actor-build-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found - the requested resource does not exist.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

## Get Actor build's log

<a id="opIdactorBuild_log_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-builds/soSkq9ekdmfOslopH/log \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actor-builds/{buildId}/log`

Retrieves Actor build's logs.

This endpoint is a shortcut for getting the build's log. Same as [Get Actor build or run log](/api/v2/log-get) endpoint.


<h3 id="get-actor-builds-log-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|buildId|path|string|true|ID of the build, found in the build's Info tab.|
|stream|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then the logs will be streamed as long as the run or build is running.<br>|
|download|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then the web browser will download the log file rather than open it in a tab.<br>|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Get OpenAPI definition of Actor build

<a id="opIdactorBuild_openapi_json_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-builds/{buildId}/openapi.json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /v2/actor-builds/{buildId}/openapi.json`

Get the OpenAPI definition for Actor builds. Two similar endpoints are available:

- [Get OpenAPI definition of Actor build](/api/v2/actor-openapi-json-get) (`/v2/actors/{actorId}/builds/{buildId}/openapi.json`): Requires both `actorId` and `buildId`. Use `default` as the `buildId` to get the OpenAPI schema for the default Actor build.
- [Get OpenAPI definition of Actor build](/api/v2/actor-build-openapi-json-get) (`/v2/actor-builds/{buildId}/openapi.json`): Requires only `buildId`.

Get the OpenAPI definition for a specific Actor build.
Authentication is based on the build's unique ID. No authentication token is required.

:::note

You can also use the [Get OpenAPI definition of Actor build](/api/v2/actor-openapi-json-get) endpoint (`/v2/actors/{actorId}/builds/{buildId}/openapi.json`) to get the OpenAPI definition for a build.

:::


> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "record-not-found",
    "message": "The requested resource was not found."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-openapi-definition-of-actor-build-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The OpenAPI specification document for the Actor build.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found - the requested resource does not exist.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

<h1 id="apify-api-actor-runs">Actor runs</h1>

The API endpoints described in this section enable you to manage, and delete Apify Actor runs.

If any returned run object contains usage in dollars, your effective unit pricing at the time of query
has been used for computation of this dollar equivalent, and hence it should be used only for informative purposes.

For completed runs, aggregated fields such as `stats` or dollar usage totals are eventually consistent and update within a few seconds. For values that must match finalized totals, wait about 10 seconds after the run completed, then fetch the run again.

You can learn more about platform usage in the [documentation](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/running/usage-and-resources#usage).


## Get list of user's Actor runs

<a id="opIdactorRuns_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-runs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actor-runs`

Gets a list of all runs for a user. The response is a list of objects, where
each object contains basic information about a single Actor run.

The endpoint supports pagination using the `limit` and `offset` parameters
and it will not return more than 1000 array elements.

By default, the records are sorted by the `startedAt` field in ascending
order. Therefore, you can use pagination to incrementally fetch all records while
new ones are still being created. To sort the records in descending order, use
`desc=1` parameter. You can also filter runs by `startedAt`` and `status`` fields ([available
statuses](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/running/runs-and-builds#lifecycle)).


<h3 id="get-list-of-users-actor-runs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|offset|query|number(double)|false|Number of items that should be skipped at the start. The default value is `0`.<br>|
|limit|query|number(double)|false|Maximum number of items to return. The default value as well as the maximum is `1000`.<br>|
|status|query|[string]|false|Single status or comma-separated list of statuses, see ([available<br>statuses](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/running/runs-and-builds#lifecycle)). Used to filter runs by the specified statuses only.<br>|
|startedAfter|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter runs that started after the specified date and time (inclusive).<br>The value must be a valid ISO 8601 datetime string (UTC).<br>|
|startedBefore|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter runs that started before the specified date and time (inclusive).<br>The value must be a valid ISO 8601 datetime string (UTC).<br>|
|deployment|query|[string]|false|Single Actor Standby deployment or comma-separated list of deployments (`SINGLE_TENANT`, `MULTI_TENANT_FREE_USERS`,<br>`MULTI_TENANT_PAYING_USERS` or `MULTI_TENANT_OWNER_PAID`). Used to filter Actor Standby runs by the pool that<br>serves them. Requires the `status` parameter with only non-terminal statuses (`READY`, `RUNNING`, `TIMING-OUT` or<br>`ABORTING`).<br>|

> Example responses

<h3 id="get-list-of-users-actor-runs-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|object|true|none|none|
|» total|integer|true|none|The total number of items available across all pages.|
|» offset|integer|true|none|The starting position for this page of results.|
|» limit|integer|true|none|The maximum number of items returned per page.|
|» desc|boolean|true|none|Whether the results are sorted in descending order.|
|» count|integer|true|none|The number of items returned in this response.|
|» items|[object]|true|none|none|
|» » id|string|true|none|none|
|» » actId|string|true|none|none|

## Get Actor run

<a id="opIdactorRun_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-runs/3KH8gEpp4d8uQSe8T \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actor-runs/{runId}`

This is not a single endpoint, but an entire group of endpoints that lets
you retrieve the run or any of its default storages.

##### Convenience endpoints for Actor run default storages

* [Default dataset](/api/v2/default-dataset)

* [Default key-value store](/api/v2/default-key-value-store)

* [Default request queue](/api/v2/default-request-queue)

Gets an object that contains all the details about a
specific run of an Actor.

By passing the optional `waitForFinish` parameter the API endpoint will synchronously wait
for the run to finish. This is useful to avoid periodic polling when waiting for Actor run to complete.
Note that the first response after completion can still show preliminary `stats`, costs, and event counts.
For stable figures, wait about 10 seconds and call the endpoint again.

This endpoint does not require the authentication token. Instead, calls are authenticated using a hard-to-guess ID of the run. However,
if you access the endpoint without the token, certain attributes, such as `usageUsd` and `usageTotalUsd`, will be hidden.


<h3 id="get-actor-run-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|runId|path|string|true|Actor run ID.|
|waitForFinish|query|number(double)|false|The maximum number of seconds the server waits for the run to finish. By<br>default it is `0`, the maximum value is `60`. <!-- MAX_ACTOR_JOB_ASYNC_WAIT_SECS --><br>If the run finishes in time then the returned run object will have a terminal status (e.g. `SUCCEEDED`),<br>otherwise it will have a transitional status (e.g. `RUNNING`).<br>|

## Update Actor run

<a id="opIdactorRun_put"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-runs/3KH8gEpp4d8uQSe8T \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "runId": "3KH8gEpp4d8uQSe8T",
    "statusMessage": "Actor has finished",
    "isStatusMessageTerminal": true
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/actor-runs/{runId}`

This endpoint can be used to update both the run's status message and to configure its general resource access level.

**Status message:**

You can set a single status message on your run that will be displayed in
the Apify Console UI. During an Actor run, you will typically do this in order
to inform users of your Actor about the Actor's progress.

The request body must contain `runId` and `statusMessage` properties. The
`isStatusMessageTerminal` property is optional and it indicates if the
status message is the very last one. In the absence of a status message, the
platform will try to substitute sensible defaults.

**General resource access:**

You can also update the run's general resource access setting, which determines who can view the run and its related data.

Allowed values:

* `FOLLOW_USER_SETTING` - The run inherits the general access setting from the account level.
* `ANYONE_WITH_ID_CAN_READ` - The run can be viewed anonymously by anyone who has its ID.
* `RESTRICTED` - Only users with explicit access to the resource can access the run.

When a run is accessible anonymously, all of the run's default storages and logs also become accessible anonymously.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "runId": "3KH8gEpp4d8uQSe8T",
  "statusMessage": "Actor has finished",
  "isStatusMessageTerminal": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-actor-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|runId|path|string|true|Actor run ID.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» runId|body|string|false|none|
|» statusMessage|body|string|false|none|
|» isStatusMessageTerminal|body|boolean|false|none|
|» generalAccess|body|string|false|Defines the general access level for the resource.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» generalAccess|ANYONE_WITH_ID_CAN_READ|
|» generalAccess|ANYONE_WITH_NAME_CAN_READ|
|» generalAccess|FOLLOW_USER_SETTING|
|» generalAccess|RESTRICTED|

## Delete Actor run

<a id="opIdactorRun_delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-runs/3KH8gEpp4d8uQSe8T \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/actor-runs/{runId}`

Delete the run. Only finished runs can be deleted. Only the person or
organization that initiated the run can delete it.


<h3 id="delete-actor-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|runId|path|string|true|Actor run ID.|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "record-not-found",
    "message": "The requested resource was not found."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|No content|None|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found - the requested resource does not exist.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

## Abort Actor run

<a id="opIdactorRun_abort_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-runs/3KH8gEpp4d8uQSe8T/abort \
  -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/actor-runs/{runId}/abort`

Aborts an Actor run and returns an object that contains all the details
about the run.

Only runs that are starting or running are aborted. For runs with status
`FINISHED`, `FAILED`, `ABORTING` and `TIMED-OUT` this call does nothing.


<h3 id="abort-actor-run-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|runId|path|string|true|Actor run ID.|
|gracefully|query|boolean|false|If true passed, the Actor run will abort gracefully.<br>It will send `aborting` and `persistState` event into run and force-stop the run after 30 seconds.<br>It is helpful in cases where you plan to resurrect the run later.<br>|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Metamorph Actor run

<a id="opIdactorRun_metamorph_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-runs/3KH8gEpp4d8uQSe8T/metamorph?targetActorId=HDSasDasz78YcAPEB' \
  -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/actor-runs/{runId}/metamorph`

Transforms an Actor run into a run of another Actor with a new input.

This is useful if you want to use another Actor to finish the work
of your current Actor run, without the need to create a completely new run
and waiting for its finish.

For the users of your Actors, the metamorph operation is transparent, they
will just see your Actor got the work done.

Internally, the system stops the Docker container corresponding to the Actor
run and starts a new container using a different Docker image.

All the default storages are preserved and the new input is stored under the
`INPUT-METAMORPH-1` key in the same default key-value store.

For more information, see the [Actor docs](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/development/programming-interface/metamorph).


<h3 id="metamorph-actor-run-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|runId|path|string|true|Actor run ID.|
|targetActorId|query|string|true|ID of a target Actor that the run should be transformed into.|
|build|query|string|false|Optional build of the target Actor.<br><br>It can be either a build tag or build number. By default, the run uses<br>the build specified in the default run configuration for the target<br>Actor (typically `latest`).<br>|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Reboot Actor run

<a id="opIdactorRun_reboot_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-runs/3KH8gEpp4d8uQSe8T/reboot \
  -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/actor-runs/{runId}/reboot`

Reboots an Actor run and returns an object that contains all the details
about the rebooted run.

Only runs that are running, i.e. runs with status `RUNNING` can be rebooted.

The run's container will be restarted, so any data not persisted in the
key-value store, dataset, or request queue will be lost.


<h3 id="reboot-actor-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|runId|path|string|true|Actor run ID.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Resurrect Actor run

<a id="opIdPostResurrectRun"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-runs/3KH8gEpp4d8uQSe8T/resurrect \
  -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/actor-runs/{runId}/resurrect`

Resurrects a finished Actor run and returns an object that contains all the details about the resurrected run.
Only finished runs, that is, runs with status `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`, `ABORTED` and `TIMED-OUT` can be resurrected.
Run status will be updated to RUNNING and its container will be restarted with the same storages
(the same behaviour as when the run gets migrated to the new server).

For more information, see the [Actor docs](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/running/runs-and-builds#resurrect-a-finished-run).


<h3 id="resurrect-actor-run-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|runId|path|string|true|Actor run ID.|
|maxItems|query|number(double)|false|Specifies the maximum number of dataset items that will be charged for pay-per-result Actors.<br>This does NOT guarantee that the Actor will return only this many items.<br>It only ensures you won't be charged for more than this number of items.<br>Only works for pay-per-result Actors.<br>Value can be accessed in the actor run using `ACTOR_MAX_PAID_DATASET_ITEMS` environment variable.<br>|
|maxTotalChargeUsd|query|number(double)|false|Specifies the maximum total cost of the run.<br>Use it to cap the total amount charged for all pricing models.<br>You can access the maximum cost in your Actor<br>by using the `ACTOR_MAX_TOTAL_CHARGE_USD` environment variable.<br>|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Charge events in Actor run

<a id="opIdPostChargeRun"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-runs/3KH8gEpp4d8uQSe8T/charge \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'idempotency-key: 2024-12-09T01:23:45.000Z-random-uuid' \
  -d '{
    "eventName": "ANALYZE_PAGE",
    "count": 1
  }'
```

`POST /v2/actor-runs/{runId}/charge`

Charge for events in the run of your [pay-per-event Actor](/actors/monetize/pay-per-event).
The event you are charging for must be one of the configured events in your Actor. If the Actor is not set up as pay per event, or if the event is not configured,
the endpoint will return an error. The endpoint must be called from the Actor run itself, with the same API token that the run was started with.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "eventName": "ANALYZE_PAGE",
  "count": 1
}
```

<h3 id="charge-events-in-actor-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|runId|path|string|true|Actor run ID.|
|idempotency-key|header|string|true|Always pass a unique idempotency key (any unique string) for each charge to avoid double charging in case of retries or network errors. The key expires 3 minutes after the charge, so a later request with the same key creates a new charge.|
|body|body|object|true|Define which event, and how many times, you want to charge for.|
|» eventName|body|string|true|none|
|» count|body|integer|true|none|
|» requestId|body|string|false|ID of the Server Actor request being charged, from the `X-Actor-Request-ID` header of the incoming request. Required for multi-tenant Server Actor runs, where it identifies the request the charge belongs to.|

> Example responses

```json
{}
```

```json
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

```json
}
```

<h3 id="charge-events-in-actor-run-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|The charge was successful. Note that you still have to make sure in your Actor that the total charge for the run respects the maximum value set by the user, as the API does not check this. Above the limit, the charges reported as successful in API will not be added to your payouts, but you will still bear the associated costs. Use the Apify charge manager or SDK to avoid having to deal with this manually.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found - the requested resource does not exist.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|413|Payload Too Large|Payload too large - the request body exceeds the size limit.|Inline|
|415|Unsupported Media Type|Unsupported media type - the Content-Encoding of the request is not supported.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

## Get log of an Actor run

<a id="opIdactorRun_log_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-runs/3KH8gEpp4d8uQSe8T/log \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actor-runs/{runId}/log`

Retrieves Actor run's logs.

This endpoint is a shortcut for getting the run's log. Same as [Get Actor build or run log](/api/v2/log-get) endpoint.


<h3 id="get-log-of-an-actor-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|runId|path|string|true|Actor run ID.|
|stream|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then the logs will be streamed as long as the run or build is running.<br>|
|download|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then the web browser will download the log file rather than open it in a tab.<br>|
|raw|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1`, the logs will be kept verbatim. By default, the API removes<br>ANSI escape codes from the logs, keeping only printable characters.<br>|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

<h1 id="apify-api-actor-tasks">Actor tasks</h1>

The API endpoints described in this section enable you to create, manage, delete, and run Apify Actor tasks.
For more information, see the [Actor tasks documentation](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/running/tasks).

:::note

For all the API endpoints that accept the `actorTaskId` parameter to
specify a task, you can pass either the task ID (e.g. `HG7ML7M8z78YcAPEB`) or a tilde-separated
username of the task's owner and the task's name (e.g. `janedoe~my-task`).

:::

Some of the API endpoints return run objects. If any such run object
contains usage in dollars, your effective unit pricing at the time of query
has been used for computation of this dollar equivalent, and hence it should be
used only for informative purposes.

You can learn more about platform usage in the [documentation](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/running/usage-and-resources#usage).


## Get list of Actor tasks

<a id="opIdactorTasks_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-tasks \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actor-tasks`

Gets the complete list of tasks that a user has created or used.

The response is a list of objects in which each object contains essential
information about a single task.

The endpoint supports pagination using the `limit` and `offset` parameters,
and it does not return more than a 1000 records.

By default, the records are sorted by the `createdAt` field in ascending
order; therefore you can use pagination to incrementally fetch all tasks while new
ones are still being created. To sort the records in descending order, use
the `desc=1` parameter.


<h3 id="get-list-of-actor-tasks-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|offset|query|number(double)|false|Number of items that should be skipped at the start. The default value is `0`.<br>|
|limit|query|number(double)|false|Maximum number of items to return. The default value as well as the maximum is `1000`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "total": 2,
    "offset": 0,
    "limit": 1000,
    "desc": false,
    "count": 2,
    "items": [
      {
        "id": "zdc3Pyhyz3m8vjDeM",
        "userId": "wRsJZtadYvn4mBZmm",
        "actId": "asADASadYvn4mBZmm",
        "actName": "my-actor",
        "name": "my-task",
        "username": "janedoe",
        "actUsername": "janedoe",
        "createdAt": "2018-10-26T07:23:14.855Z",
        "modifiedAt": "2018-10-26T13:30:49.578Z",
        "stats": {
          "totalRuns": 15
        }
      },
      {
        "id": "aWE3asdas3m8vjDeM",
        "userId": "wRsJZtadYvn4mBZmm",
        "actId": "asADASadYvn4mBZmm",
        "actName": "my-actor",
        "actUsername": "janedoe",
        "name": "my-task-2",
        "username": "janedoe",
        "createdAt": "2018-10-26T07:23:14.855Z",
        "modifiedAt": "2018-10-26T13:30:49.578Z",
        "stats": {
          "totalRuns": 4
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-list-of-actor-tasks-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

<h3 id="get-list-of-actor-tasks-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|object|true|none|none|
|» total|integer|true|none|The total number of items available across all pages.|
|» offset|integer|true|none|The starting position for this page of results.|
|» limit|integer|true|none|The maximum number of items returned per page.|
|» desc|boolean|true|none|Whether the results are sorted in descending order.|
|» count|integer|true|none|The number of items returned in this response.|
|» items|[object]|true|none|none|
|» » id|string|true|none|none|
|» » userId|string|true|none|none|
|» » actId|string|true|none|none|
|» » actName|string \| null|false|none|none|
|» » name|string|true|none|none|
|» » title|string \| null|false|none|none|
|» » username|string \| null|false|none|none|
|» » actUsername|string \| null|false|none|none|
|» » createdAt|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|» » modifiedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|» » stats|object \| null|false|none|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|object|false|none|none|
|» » » totalRuns|integer|false|none|none|
|» » » lastRunStartedAt|string \| null(date-time)|false|none|Time when the last run of the task started. In the task list, it's `null` if the task has no runs. In a single task, it's omitted if the task has no runs.|
|» » » *anyOf*|null|false|none|none|
|» » isPublic|boolean|false|none|Whether the task is published. Based on the `publicConfig.publishedAt` field.<br>|

Status Code **400**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|error|object|true|none|none|
|» type|string|false|none|Machine-processable error type identifier.|
|» message|string|false|none|Human-readable error message describing what went wrong.|
|» data|object|false|none|Additional machine-readable details about the error. Present only for some error types.|

## Create Actor task

<a id="opIdactorTasks_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-tasks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "actId": "asADASadYvn4mBZmm",
    "name": "my-task",
    "options": {
      "build": "latest",
      "timeoutSecs": 300,
      "memoryMbytes": 128
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v2/actor-tasks`

Create a new task with settings specified by the object passed as JSON in
the POST payload.

The response is the full task object as returned by the
[Get Actor task](/api/v2/actor-task-get) endpoint.

The request needs to specify the `Content-Type: application/json` HTTP header!

When providing your API authentication token, we recommend using the
request's `Authorization` header, rather than the URL.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "actId": "asADASadYvn4mBZmm",
  "name": "my-task",
  "options": {
    "build": "latest",
    "timeoutSecs": 300,
    "memoryMbytes": 128
  }
}
```

## Get Actor task

<a id="opIdactorTask_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-tasks/janedoe~my-task \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actor-tasks/{actorTaskId}`

Get an object that contains all the details about a task.

<h3 id="get-actor-task-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorTaskId|path|string|true|Task ID or a tilde-separated owner's username and task's name.|

## Update Actor task

<a id="opIdactorTask_put"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-tasks/janedoe~my-task \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "my-task",
    "options": {
      "build": "latest",
      "timeoutSecs": 300,
      "memoryMbytes": 128
    },
    "input": {
      "hello": "world"
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/actor-tasks/{actorTaskId}`

Update settings of a task using values specified by an object passed as JSON
in the POST payload.

If the object does not define a specific property, its value is not updated.

The `publicConfig` field carries the display configuration of the task's public
landing page, and `isPublic` publishes or unpublishes the task itself. Both require
write permission to the task's Actor.

To publish a task, its Actor must be public and both `publicConfig.inputSchemaFields` and
`publicConfig.datasetView` must be set. Note that an Actor can have up to 10 published tasks
and your account up to 100.
If the task doesn't meet all these conditions, the request fails and no fields are updated,
including those unrelated to publishing.

Publishing lists the task among the Actor's examples and makes its input public, so anyone
can view and copy it. The landing page itself is shown only while `publicConfig` still
validates against the Actor's current build, so a new build can stop the page from being
offered while the task stays published and copyable.

The response is the full task object as returned by the
[Get Actor task](/api/v2/actor-task-get) endpoint.

The request needs to specify the `Content-Type: application/json` HTTP
header!

When providing your API authentication token, we recommend using the
request's `Authorization` header, rather than the URL.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "my-task",
  "options": {
    "build": "latest",
    "timeoutSecs": 300,
    "memoryMbytes": 128
  },
  "input": {
    "hello": "world"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-actor-task-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorTaskId|path|string|true|Task ID or a tilde-separated owner's username and task's name.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|false|none|
|» options|body|object \| null|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » build|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » timeoutSecs|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» » memoryMbytes|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» » maxItems|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» » maxTotalChargeUsd|body|number \| null|false|none|
|» » restartOnError|body|boolean \| null|false|none|
|» » isMaxTotalChargeUsdSetByUser|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether the user explicitly set `maxTotalChargeUsd`. Returned only in schedule action `runOptions`, and only if it was provided.|
|» » forcePermissionLevel|body|string \| null|false|Permission level to run the Actor with, overriding the Actor's own setting. Returned only in schedule action `runOptions`, and only if it was provided.|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|Determines the permission level that the Actor requires to run. For details, see [Actor permissions](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/development/permissions).<br>|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» input|body|object \| [object] \| null|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|The input configuration for the Actor task. This is a user-defined JSON object<br>that will be passed to the Actor when the task is run.<br>|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» title|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» actorStandby|body|object \| null|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » isEnabled|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether standby mode is enabled for the Actor.|
|» » desiredRequestsPerActorRun|body|integer \| null|false|Target number of concurrent HTTP requests a single run is configured to handle.|
|» » maxRequestsPerActorRun|body|integer \| null|false|Maximum number of concurrent HTTP requests that can be routed to a single run.|
|» » idleTimeoutSecs|body|integer \| null|false|In seconds, how long a run can stay idle without incoming requests before it's terminated.|
|» » build|body|string \| null|false|Which build to run in standby mode. Either a build tag or a version number.|
|» » memoryMbytes|body|integer \| null|false|In MB, the amount of memory allocated to the run.|
|» » disableStandbyFieldsOverride|body|boolean \| null|false|If `true`, prevents the standby mode configuration from being overridden elsewhere.|
|» » shouldPassActorInput|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether to pass the Actor's input to the standby run. If `false`, the standby runs start with no input.|
|» » tenancy|body|string \| null|false|Whether each user gets their own standby runs (`SINGLE_TENANT`) or runs are shared across users (`MULTI_TENANT`).|
|» » isConsoleAuthEnabled|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether standby requests can be authenticated with an Apify Console session.<br>When creating an Actor, omit this field or set it to `false`. When updating an Actor, only Apify administrators can change it; other users can only send the current value, or `false` if it's not set yet.<br>|
|» » isTokenlessEnabled|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether standby requests can be made without an API token.<br>When creating an Actor, omit this field or set it to `false`. When updating an Actor, only Apify administrators can change it; other users can only send the current value, or `false` if it's not set yet.<br>|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» publicConfig|body|object|false|Configuration that controls how the published task appears on its public landing page.<br>Editing this object requires write permission to the Actor that the task belongs to.<br><br>The fields you send are merged into the stored configuration, so you only need to include<br>the ones you're changing. To clear a field, set it to `null`. Sending `publicConfig: null`<br>is rejected, so the object as a whole can't be cleared.<br>|
|» » seoTitle|body|string \| null|false|Name of the Actor task to display by search engines such as Google. Defaults to the task<br>title. At most 60 characters.<br>|
|» » seoDescription|body|string \| null|false|Description of the Actor task to display by search engines such as Google. Defaults to the<br>task description. At most 160 characters.<br>|
|» » inputSchemaFields|body|[string]|false|Names of the task input fields displayed on the public task page.|
|» » datasetName|body|string \| null|false|Name of the dataset from the Actor's dataset schema whose results are displayed. When<br>`null`, the Actor's default dataset is used. That is, the only dataset the Actor declares,<br>or the one named `default` when it declares several.<br>|
|» » datasetView|body|string \| null|false|Key of the dataset view from the Actor's dataset schema used to display results. Must be<br>one of the views declared on the resolved dataset. You can't publish a task without it.<br>|
|» » categorization|body|string \| null|false|ID of the use-case category of the task.|
|» » highlightedFields|body|[string]|false|Names of the dataset fields highlighted on the public task page.|
|» » faq|body|[object]|false|Frequently asked questions displayed on the public task page.|
|» » » question|body|string|true|none|
|» » » answer|body|string|true|none|
|» isPublic|body|boolean|false|Set to `true` to publish the task on its public landing page, or `false` to unpublish it.<br>Sending the value the task already has does nothing.<br>|

## Delete Actor task

<a id="opIdactorTask_delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-tasks/janedoe~my-task \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/actor-tasks/{actorTaskId}`

Delete the task specified through the `actorTaskId` parameter.

<h3 id="delete-actor-task-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorTaskId|path|string|true|Task ID or a tilde-separated owner's username and task's name.|

> Example responses

> 204 Response

```json
{}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "record-not-found",
    "message": "The requested resource was not found."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

<h3 id="delete-actor-task-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found - the requested resource does not exist.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

## Get Actor task input

<a id="opIdactorTask_input_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-tasks/janedoe~my-task/input \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actor-tasks/{actorTaskId}/input`

Returns the input of a given task.

<h3 id="get-actor-task-input-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorTaskId|path|string|true|Task ID or a tilde-separated owner's username and task's name.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "myField1": "some-value",
  "myField2": "another-value",
  "myField3": 1
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "record-not-found",
    "message": "The requested resource was not found."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-actor-task-input-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found - the requested resource does not exist.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

<h3 id="get-actor-task-input-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

## Update Actor task input

<a id="opIdactorTask_input_put"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-tasks/janedoe~my-task/input \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "myField2": "updated-value"
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/actor-tasks/{actorTaskId}/input`

Updates the input of a task using values specified by an object passed as
JSON in the PUT payload.

If the object does not define a specific property, its value is not updated.

The response is the full task input as returned by the
[Get Actor task input](/api/v2/actor-task-input-get) endpoint.

The request needs to specify the `Content-Type: application/json` HTTP
header!

When providing your API authentication token, we recommend using the
request's `Authorization` header, rather than the URL.
For details, see [Authentication](/api/v2#authentication).


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "myField2": "updated-value"
}
```

<h3 id="update-actor-task-input-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorTaskId|path|string|true|Task ID or a tilde-separated owner's username and task's name.|
|body|body|object|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "myField1": "some-value",
  "myField2": "updated-value",
  "myField3": 1
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "record-not-found",
    "message": "The requested resource was not found."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 413 Response

```json
  "error": {
    "type": "request-too-large",
    "message": "The POST payload is too large (limit: 9437184 bytes, actual length: 10485760 bytes)."
  }
}
```

> 415 Response

```json
  "error": {
    "type": "unsupported-content-encoding",

  }
}
```

```json
  }
```

## Get list of Actor task's webhooks

<a id="opIdactorTask_webhooks_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-tasks/janedoe~my-task/webhooks \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actor-tasks/{actorTaskId}/webhooks`

Gets the list of webhooks of a specific Actor task. The response is a JSON
with the list of objects, where each object contains basic information about a single webhook.

The endpoint supports pagination using the `limit` and `offset` parameters
and it will not return more than 1000 records.

By default, the records are sorted by the `createdAt` field in ascending
order, to sort the records in descending order, use the `desc=1` parameter.


<h3 id="get-list-of-actor-tasks-webhooks-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorTaskId|path|string|true|Task ID or a tilde-separated owner's username and task's name.|
|offset|query|number(double)|false|Number of items that should be skipped at the start. The default value is `0`.<br>|
|limit|query|number(double)|false|Maximum number of items to return. The default value as well as the maximum is `1000`.<br>|

</aside>

## Get list of Actor task's runs

<a id="opIdactorTask_runs_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-tasks/janedoe~my-task/runs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actor-tasks/{actorTaskId}/runs`

Get a list of runs of a specific task. The response is a list of objects,
where each object contains essential information about a single task run.

The endpoint supports pagination using the `limit` and `offset` parameters,
and it does not return more than a 1000 array elements.

By default, the records are sorted by the `startedAt` field in ascending
order; therefore you can use pagination to incrementally fetch all records while
new ones are still being created. To sort the records in descending order, use
the `desc=1` parameter. You can also filter runs by status ([available
statuses](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/running/runs-and-builds#lifecycle)).


<h3 id="get-list-of-actor-tasks-runs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorTaskId|path|string|true|Task ID or a tilde-separated owner's username and task's name.|
|offset|query|number(double)|false|Number of items that should be skipped at the start. The default value is `0`.<br>|
|limit|query|number(double)|false|Maximum number of items to return. The default value as well as the maximum is `1000`.<br>|
|status|query|[string]|false|Single status or comma-separated list of statuses, see ([available<br>statuses](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/running/runs-and-builds#lifecycle)). Used to filter runs by the specified statuses only.<br>|

> Example responses

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Run Actor task

<a id="opIdactorTask_runs_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-tasks/janedoe~my-task/runs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "foo": "bar"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/actor-tasks/{actorTaskId}/runs`

Runs an Actor task and immediately returns without waiting for the run to
finish.

Optionally, you can override the Actor input configuration by passing a JSON
object as the POST payload and setting the `Content-Type: application/json` HTTP header.

Note that if the object in the POST payload does not define a particular
input property, the Actor run uses the default value defined by the task (or Actor's input
schema if not defined by the task).

The response is the Actor Run object as returned by the [Get Actor run](/api/v2/actor-run-get) endpoint.

If you want to wait for the run to finish and receive the actual output of
the Actor run as the response, use the [Run Actor task synchronously and get key-value store record](/api/v2/actor-task-run-sync-post)
or [Run Actor task synchronously and get dataset items](/api/v2/actor-task-run-sync-get-dataset-items-post)
endpoint instead.

To fetch the Actor run results that are typically stored in the default
dataset, you'll need to pass the ID received in the `defaultDatasetId` field
received in the response JSON to the
[Get dataset items](/api/v2/dataset-items-get) API endpoint.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "foo": "bar"
}
```

<h3 id="run-actor-task-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorTaskId|path|string|true|Task ID or a tilde-separated owner's username and task's name.|
|timeout|query|number(double)|false|Optional timeout for the run, in seconds. By default, the run uses the timeout from its configuration.<br>|
|memory|query|number(double)|false|Memory limit for the run, in megabytes. You can set the amount of memory to a power of 2 with a minimum of 128.<br>By default, the run uses the memory limit from its configuration. Don't change this value unless the Actor's<br>documentation recommends it or you're aware of the consequences.<br>|
|maxItems|query|number(double)|false|Specifies the maximum number of dataset items that will be charged for pay-per-result Actors.<br>This does NOT guarantee that the Actor will return only this many items.<br>It only ensures you won't be charged for more than this number of items.<br>Only works for pay-per-result Actors.<br>Value can be accessed in the actor run using `ACTOR_MAX_PAID_DATASET_ITEMS` environment variable.<br>|
|maxTotalChargeUsd|query|number(double)|false|Specifies the maximum total cost of the run.<br>Use it to cap the total amount charged for all pricing models.<br>You can access the maximum cost in your Actor<br>by using the `ACTOR_MAX_TOTAL_CHARGE_USD` environment variable.<br>|
|restartOnError|query|boolean|false|Determines whether the run will be restarted if it fails.<br>|
|build|query|string|false|Specifies the Actor build to run. It can be either a build tag or build number.<br>By default, the run uses the build from its configuration (typically `latest`).<br>|
|waitForFinish|query|number(double)|false|The maximum number of seconds the server waits for the run to finish. By<br>default it is `0`, the maximum value is `60`. <!-- MAX_ACTOR_JOB_ASYNC_WAIT_SECS --><br>If the run finishes in time then the returned run object will have a terminal status (e.g. `SUCCEEDED`),<br>otherwise it will have a transitional status (e.g. `RUNNING`).<br>|
|webhooks|query|string|false|Specifies optional webhooks associated with the Actor run, which can be used to receive a notification<br>e.g. when the Actor finished or failed. The value is a Base64-encoded JSON array whose items follow<br>the WebhookRepresentation schema. For more information, see<br>[Webhooks documentation](https://docs.apify.com/platform/integrations/webhooks).<br>|
|body|body|object|true|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Run Actor task synchronously and get key-value store record (GET)

<a id="opIdactorTask_runSync_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-tasks/janedoe~my-task/run-sync \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actor-tasks/{actorTaskId}/run-sync`

Runs an Actor task and synchronously returns a key-value store record.

The response contains the record stored under the `OUTPUT` key in the run's
default key-value store. This is a legacy approach that has been replaced by
the Actor [output object](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/development/actor-definition/output-schema#output-object-definition);
Actors aren't required to store a record under this key, so the response may
not contain any data. Use the `outputRecordKey` query parameter to return a
different record.

The run must finish in 300<!-- MAX_ACTOR_JOB_SYNC_WAIT_SECS --> seconds
otherwise the HTTP request fails with a timeout error (this won't abort
the run itself).

Beware that it might be impossible to maintain an idle HTTP connection for
an extended period, due to client timeout or network conditions. Make sure your HTTP client is
configured to have a long enough connection timeout.

If the connection breaks, you will not receive any information about the run
and its status.

To run the Task asynchronously, use the
[Run Actor task](/api/v2/actor-task-runs-post)
endpoint instead.


<h3 id="run-actor-task-synchronously-and-get-key-value-store-record-get-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorTaskId|path|string|true|Task ID or a tilde-separated owner's username and task's name.|
|timeout|query|number(double)|false|Optional timeout for the run, in seconds. By default, the run uses the timeout from its configuration.<br>|
|memory|query|number(double)|false|Memory limit for the run, in megabytes. You can set the amount of memory to a power of 2 with a minimum of 128.<br>By default, the run uses the memory limit from its configuration. Don't change this value unless the Actor's<br>documentation recommends it or you're aware of the consequences.<br>|
|maxItems|query|number(double)|false|Specifies the maximum number of dataset items that will be charged for pay-per-result Actors.<br>This does NOT guarantee that the Actor will return only this many items.<br>It only ensures you won't be charged for more than this number of items.<br>Only works for pay-per-result Actors.<br>Value can be accessed in the actor run using `ACTOR_MAX_PAID_DATASET_ITEMS` environment variable.<br>|
|maxTotalChargeUsd|query|number(double)|false|Specifies the maximum total cost of the run.<br>Use it to cap the total amount charged for all pricing models.<br>You can access the maximum cost in your Actor<br>by using the `ACTOR_MAX_TOTAL_CHARGE_USD` environment variable.<br>|
|restartOnError|query|boolean|false|Determines whether the run will be restarted if it fails.<br>|
|build|query|string|false|Specifies the Actor build to run. It can be either a build tag or build number.<br>By default, the run uses the build from its configuration (typically `latest`).<br>|
|outputRecordKey|query|string|false|Key of the record from the run's default key-value store to return in the<br>response. Defaults to `OUTPUT`. Actors aren't required to store a record<br>under this key, so if it doesn't exist the response contains no data.<br>|
|webhooks|query|string|false|Specifies optional webhooks associated with the Actor run, which can be used to receive a notification<br>e.g. when the Actor finished or failed. The value is a Base64-encoded JSON array whose items follow<br>the WebhookRepresentation schema. For more information, see<br>[Webhooks documentation](https://docs.apify.com/platform/integrations/webhooks).<br>|

httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Run Actor task synchronously and get key-value store record

<a id="opIdactorTask_runSync_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-tasks/janedoe~my-task/run-sync \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "foo": "bar"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/actor-tasks/{actorTaskId}/run-sync`

Runs an Actor task and synchronously returns a key-value store record.

The response contains the record stored under the `OUTPUT` key in the run's
default key-value store. This is a legacy approach that has been replaced by
the Actor [output object](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/development/actor-definition/output-schema#output-object-definition);
Actors aren't required to store a record under this key, so the response may
not contain any data. Use the `outputRecordKey` query parameter to return a
different record.

The run must finish in 300<!-- MAX_ACTOR_JOB_SYNC_WAIT_SECS --> seconds
otherwise the HTTP request fails with a timeout error (this won't abort
the run itself).

Optionally, you can override the Actor input configuration by passing a JSON
object as the POST payload and setting the `Content-Type: application/json` HTTP header.

Note that if the object in the POST payload does not define a particular
input property, the Actor run uses the default value defined by the task (or Actor's input
schema if not defined by the task).

Beware that it might be impossible to maintain an idle HTTP connection for
an extended period, due to client timeout or network conditions. Make sure your HTTP client is
configured to have a long enough connection timeout.

If the connection breaks, you will not receive any information about the run
and its status.

Input fields from Actor task configuration can be overloaded with values
passed as the POST payload.

Just make sure to specify `Content-Type` header to be `application/json` and
input to be an object.

To run the task asynchronously, use the [Run Actor task](/api/v2/actor-task-runs-post) API endpoint instead.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "foo": "bar"
}
```

<h3 id="run-actor-task-synchronously-and-get-key-value-store-record-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorTaskId|path|string|true|Task ID or a tilde-separated owner's username and task's name.|
|timeout|query|number(double)|false|Optional timeout for the run, in seconds. By default, the run uses the timeout from its configuration.<br>|
|memory|query|number(double)|false|Memory limit for the run, in megabytes. You can set the amount of memory to a power of 2 with a minimum of 128.<br>By default, the run uses the memory limit from its configuration. Don't change this value unless the Actor's<br>documentation recommends it or you're aware of the consequences.<br>|
|maxItems|query|number(double)|false|Specifies the maximum number of dataset items that will be charged for pay-per-result Actors.<br>This does NOT guarantee that the Actor will return only this many items.<br>It only ensures you won't be charged for more than this number of items.<br>Only works for pay-per-result Actors.<br>Value can be accessed in the actor run using `ACTOR_MAX_PAID_DATASET_ITEMS` environment variable.<br>|
|maxTotalChargeUsd|query|number(double)|false|Specifies the maximum total cost of the run.<br>Use it to cap the total amount charged for all pricing models.<br>You can access the maximum cost in your Actor<br>by using the `ACTOR_MAX_TOTAL_CHARGE_USD` environment variable.<br>|
|restartOnError|query|boolean|false|Determines whether the run will be restarted if it fails.<br>|
|build|query|string|false|Specifies the Actor build to run. It can be either a build tag or build number.<br>By default, the run uses the build from its configuration (typically `latest`).<br>|
|outputRecordKey|query|string|false|Key of the record from the run's default key-value store to return in the<br>response. Defaults to `OUTPUT`. Actors aren't required to store a record<br>under this key, so if it doesn't exist the response contains no data.<br>|
|webhooks|query|string|false|Specifies optional webhooks associated with the Actor run, which can be used to receive a notification<br>e.g. when the Actor finished or failed. The value is a Base64-encoded JSON array whose items follow<br>the WebhookRepresentation schema. For more information, see<br>[Webhooks documentation](https://docs.apify.com/platform/integrations/webhooks).<br>|
|body|body|object|true|none|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "bar": "foo"
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|402|Payment Required|Payment required - the user has exceeded their usage limit, does not have enough credits, or the request lacks authentication and payment credentials.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found - the requested resource does not exist.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|408|Request Timeout|The HTTP request exceeded the timeout limit|Inline|
|413|Payload Too Large|Payload too large - the request body exceeds the size limit.|Inline|
|415|Unsupported Media Type|Unsupported media type - the Content-Encoding of the request is not supported.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|
