## Run Actor task synchronously and get dataset items (GET)

<a id="opIdactorTask_runSyncGetDatasetItems_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-tasks/janedoe~my-task/run-sync-get-dataset-items \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actor-tasks/{actorTaskId}/run-sync-get-dataset-items`

Run a specific task and return its dataset items.

The run must finish in 300<!-- MAX_ACTOR_JOB_SYNC_WAIT_SECS --> seconds
otherwise the HTTP request fails with a timeout error (this won't abort
the run itself).

You can send all the same options in parameters as the [Get dataset items](/api/v2/dataset-items-get) API endpoint.

Beware that it might be impossible to maintain an idle HTTP connection for
an extended period, due to client timeout or network conditions. Make sure your HTTP client is
configured to have a long enough connection timeout.

If the connection breaks, you will not receive any information about the run
and its status.

To run the Task asynchronously, use the [Run Actor task](/api/v2/actor-task-runs-post) endpoint
instead.


<h3 id="run-actor-task-synchronously-and-get-dataset-items-get-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorTaskId|path|string|true|Task ID or a tilde-separated owner's username and task's name.|
|timeout|query|number(double)|false|Optional timeout for the run, in seconds. By default, the run uses the timeout from its configuration.<br>|
|memory|query|number(double)|false|Memory limit for the run, in megabytes. You can set the amount of memory to a power of 2 with a minimum of 128.<br>By default, the run uses the memory limit from its configuration. Don't change this value unless the Actor's<br>documentation recommends it or you're aware of the consequences.<br>|
|maxItems|query|number(double)|false|Specifies the maximum number of dataset items that will be charged for pay-per-result Actors.<br>This does NOT guarantee that the Actor will return only this many items.<br>It only ensures you won't be charged for more than this number of items.<br>Only works for pay-per-result Actors.<br>Value can be accessed in the actor run using `ACTOR_MAX_PAID_DATASET_ITEMS` environment variable.<br>|
|maxTotalChargeUsd|query|number(double)|false|Specifies the maximum total cost of the run.<br>Use it to cap the total amount charged for all pricing models.<br>You can access the maximum cost in your Actor<br>by using the `ACTOR_MAX_TOTAL_CHARGE_USD` environment variable.<br>|
|build|query|string|false|Specifies the Actor build to run. It can be either a build tag or build number.<br>By default, the run uses the build from its configuration (typically `latest`).<br>|
|webhooks|query|string|false|Specifies optional webhooks associated with the Actor run, which can be used to receive a notification<br>e.g. when the Actor finished or failed. The value is a Base64-encoded JSON array whose items follow<br>the WebhookRepresentation schema. For more information, see<br>[Webhooks documentation](https://docs.apify.com/platform/integrations/webhooks).<br>|
|format|query|string|false|Format of the results, possible values are: `json`, `jsonl`, `csv`, `html`, `xlsx`, `xml` and `rss`. The default value is `json`.<br>|
|clean|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then the API endpoint returns only non-empty items and skips hidden fields (i.e. fields starting with the # character).<br>The `clean` parameter is just a shortcut for `skipHidden=true` and `skipEmpty=true` parameters.<br>Note that since some objects might be skipped from the output, that the result might contain less items than the `limit` value.<br>|
|offset|query|number(double)|false|Number of items that should be skipped at the start. The default value is `0`.<br>|
|limit|query|number(double)|false|Maximum number of items to return. By default there is no limit.|
|fields|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of fields which should be picked from the items, only these fields will remain in the resulting record objects.<br>Note that the fields in the outputted items are sorted the same way as they are specified in the `fields` query parameter.<br>You can use this feature to effectively fix the output format.<br>|
|outputFields|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of output field names that positionally rename the fields specified in the `fields` parameter.<br>For example, `?fields=headline,url&outputFields=title,link` renames `headline` to `title` and `url` to `link` in the output.<br>The number of names in `outputFields` must match the number of names in `fields`.<br>Requires the `fields` parameter to be specified as well.<br>|
|omit|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of fields which should be omitted from the items.|
|unwind|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of fields which should be unwound, in order which they should be processed. Each field should be either an array or an object.<br>If the field is an array then every element of the array will become a separate record and merged with parent object.<br>If the unwound field is an object then it is merged with the parent object.<br>If the unwound field is missing or its value is neither an array nor an object and therefore cannot be merged with a parent object then the item gets preserved as it is.<br>Note that the unwound items ignore the `desc` parameter.<br>|
|flatten|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of fields which should transform nested objects into flat structures.<br><br>For example, with `flatten="foo"` the object `{"foo":{"bar": "hello"}}` is turned into `{"foo.bar": "hello"}`.<br><br>The original object with properties is replaced with the flattened object.<br>|
|desc|query|boolean|false|By default, results are returned in the same order as they were stored.<br>To reverse the order, set this parameter to `true` or `1`.<br>|
|attachment|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then the response will define the `Content-Disposition:<br>attachment` header, forcing a web browser to download the file rather<br>than to display it. By default this header is not present.<br>|
|delimiter|query|string|false|A delimiter character for CSV files, only used if `format=csv`. You<br>might need to URL-encode the character (e.g. use `%09` for tab or `%3B`<br>for semicolon). The default delimiter is a simple comma (`,`).<br>|
|bom|query|boolean|false|All text responses are encoded in UTF-8 encoding. By default, the<br>`format=csv` files are prefixed with the UTF-8 Byte Order Mark (BOM), while `json`, `jsonl`, `xml`, `html` and `rss` files are not.<br><br>If you want to override this default behavior, specify `bom=1` query parameter to include the BOM or `bom=0` to skip it.<br>|
|xmlRoot|query|string|false|Overrides default root element name of `xml` output. By default the root element is `items`.<br>|
|xmlRow|query|string|false|Overrides default element name that wraps each page or page function result object in `xml` output. By default the element name is `item`.<br>|
|skipHeaderRow|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then header row in the `csv` format is skipped.|
|skipHidden|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then hidden fields are skipped from the output, i.e. fields starting with the `#` character.<br>|
|skipEmpty|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then empty items are skipped from the output.<br><br>Note that if used, the results might contain less items than the limit value.<br>|
|simplified|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then, the endpoint applies the `fields=url,pageFunctionResult,errorInfo`<br>and `unwind=pageFunctionResult` query parameters. This feature is used to emulate simplified results provided by the<br>legacy Apify Crawler product and it's not recommended to use it in new integrations.<br>|
|view|query|string|false|Defines the view configuration for dataset items based on the schema definition.<br>This parameter determines how the data will be filtered and presented.<br>For complete specification details, see the [dataset schema documentation](/storage/dataset-schema).<br>|
|skipFailedPages|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then, the all the items with errorInfo property will be skipped from the output.<br><br>This feature is here to emulate functionality of API version 1 used for the legacy Apify Crawler product and it's not recommended to use it in new integrations.<br>|
|feedTitle|query|string|false|Overrides the auto-generated RSS channel `<title>` element.<br>Only used when `format=rss`. If not provided, the title defaults to `Dataset <label>`.<br>|
|feedDescription|query|string|false|Overrides the auto-generated RSS channel `<description>` element.<br>Only used when `format=rss`. If not provided, the description defaults to `Items in dataset with id "<datasetId>".`<br>|

|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|408|Request Timeout|The HTTP request exceeded the timeout limit|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

## Run Actor task synchronously and get dataset items

<a id="opIdactorTask_runSyncGetDatasetItems_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-tasks/janedoe~my-task/run-sync-get-dataset-items \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "foo": "bar"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/actor-tasks/{actorTaskId}/run-sync-get-dataset-items`

Runs an Actor task and synchronously returns its dataset items.

The run must finish in 300<!-- MAX_ACTOR_JOB_SYNC_WAIT_SECS --> seconds
otherwise the HTTP request fails with a timeout error (this won't abort
the run itself).

Optionally, you can override the Actor input configuration by passing a JSON
object as the POST payload and setting the `Content-Type: application/json` HTTP header.

Note that if the object in the POST payload does not define a particular
input property, the Actor run uses the default value defined by the task (or the Actor's
input schema if not defined by the task).

You can send all the same options in parameters as the [Get dataset items](/api/v2/dataset-items-get) API endpoint.

Beware that it might be impossible to maintain an idle HTTP connection for
an extended period, due to client timeout or network conditions. Make sure your HTTP client is
configured to have a long enough connection timeout.

If the connection breaks, you will not receive any information about the run
and its status.

Input fields from Actor task configuration can be overloaded with values
passed as the POST payload.

Just make sure to specify the `Content-Type` header as `application/json`
and that the input is an object.

To run the task asynchronously, use the [Run Actor task](/api/v2/actor-task-runs-post) API endpoint instead.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "foo": "bar"
}
```

<h3 id="run-actor-task-synchronously-and-get-dataset-items-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorTaskId|path|string|true|Task ID or a tilde-separated owner's username and task's name.|
|timeout|query|number(double)|false|Optional timeout for the run, in seconds. By default, the run uses the timeout from its configuration.<br>|
|memory|query|number(double)|false|Memory limit for the run, in megabytes. You can set the amount of memory to a power of 2 with a minimum of 128.<br>By default, the run uses the memory limit from its configuration. Don't change this value unless the Actor's<br>documentation recommends it or you're aware of the consequences.<br>|
|maxItems|query|number(double)|false|Specifies the maximum number of dataset items that will be charged for pay-per-result Actors.<br>This does NOT guarantee that the Actor will return only this many items.<br>It only ensures you won't be charged for more than this number of items.<br>Only works for pay-per-result Actors.<br>Value can be accessed in the actor run using `ACTOR_MAX_PAID_DATASET_ITEMS` environment variable.<br>|
|maxTotalChargeUsd|query|number(double)|false|Specifies the maximum total cost of the run.<br>Use it to cap the total amount charged for all pricing models.<br>You can access the maximum cost in your Actor<br>by using the `ACTOR_MAX_TOTAL_CHARGE_USD` environment variable.<br>|
|restartOnError|query|boolean|false|Determines whether the run will be restarted if it fails.<br>|
|build|query|string|false|Specifies the Actor build to run. It can be either a build tag or build number.<br>By default, the run uses the build from its configuration (typically `latest`).<br>|
|webhooks|query|string|false|Specifies optional webhooks associated with the Actor run, which can be used to receive a notification<br>e.g. when the Actor finished or failed. The value is a Base64-encoded JSON array whose items follow<br>the WebhookRepresentation schema. For more information, see<br>[Webhooks documentation](https://docs.apify.com/platform/integrations/webhooks).<br>|
|format|query|string|false|Format of the results, possible values are: `json`, `jsonl`, `csv`, `html`, `xlsx`, `xml` and `rss`. The default value is `json`.<br>|
|clean|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then the API endpoint returns only non-empty items and skips hidden fields (i.e. fields starting with the # character).<br>The `clean` parameter is just a shortcut for `skipHidden=true` and `skipEmpty=true` parameters.<br>Note that since some objects might be skipped from the output, that the result might contain less items than the `limit` value.<br>|
|offset|query|number(double)|false|Number of items that should be skipped at the start. The default value is `0`.<br>|
|limit|query|number(double)|false|Maximum number of items to return. By default there is no limit.|
|fields|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of fields which should be picked from the items, only these fields will remain in the resulting record objects.<br>Note that the fields in the outputted items are sorted the same way as they are specified in the `fields` query parameter.<br>You can use this feature to effectively fix the output format.<br>|
|outputFields|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of output field names that positionally rename the fields specified in the `fields` parameter.<br>For example, `?fields=headline,url&outputFields=title,link` renames `headline` to `title` and `url` to `link` in the output.<br>The number of names in `outputFields` must match the number of names in `fields`.<br>Requires the `fields` parameter to be specified as well.<br>|
|omit|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of fields which should be omitted from the items.|
|unwind|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of fields which should be unwound, in order which they should be processed. Each field should be either an array or an object.<br>If the field is an array then every element of the array will become a separate record and merged with parent object.<br>If the unwound field is an object then it is merged with the parent object.<br>If the unwound field is missing or its value is neither an array nor an object and therefore cannot be merged with a parent object then the item gets preserved as it is.<br>Note that the unwound items ignore the `desc` parameter.<br>|
|flatten|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of fields which should transform nested objects into flat structures.<br><br>For example, with `flatten="foo"` the object `{"foo":{"bar": "hello"}}` is turned into `{"foo.bar": "hello"}`.<br><br>The original object with properties is replaced with the flattened object.<br>|
|desc|query|boolean|false|By default, results are returned in the same order as they were stored.<br>To reverse the order, set this parameter to `true` or `1`.<br>|
|attachment|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then the response will define the `Content-Disposition:<br>attachment` header, forcing a web browser to download the file rather<br>than to display it. By default this header is not present.<br>|
|delimiter|query|string|false|A delimiter character for CSV files, only used if `format=csv`. You<br>might need to URL-encode the character (e.g. use `%09` for tab or `%3B`<br>for semicolon). The default delimiter is a simple comma (`,`).<br>|
|bom|query|boolean|false|All text responses are encoded in UTF-8 encoding. By default, the<br>`format=csv` files are prefixed with the UTF-8 Byte Order Mark (BOM), while `json`, `jsonl`, `xml`, `html` and `rss` files are not.<br><br>If you want to override this default behavior, specify `bom=1` query parameter to include the BOM or `bom=0` to skip it.<br>|
|xmlRoot|query|string|false|Overrides default root element name of `xml` output. By default the root element is `items`.<br>|
|xmlRow|query|string|false|Overrides default element name that wraps each page or page function result object in `xml` output. By default the element name is `item`.<br>|
|skipHeaderRow|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then header row in the `csv` format is skipped.|
|skipHidden|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then hidden fields are skipped from the output, i.e. fields starting with the `#` character.<br>|
|skipEmpty|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then empty items are skipped from the output.<br><br>Note that if used, the results might contain less items than the limit value.<br>|
|simplified|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then, the endpoint applies the `fields=url,pageFunctionResult,errorInfo`<br>and `unwind=pageFunctionResult` query parameters. This feature is used to emulate simplified results provided by the<br>legacy Apify Crawler product and it's not recommended to use it in new integrations.<br>|
|view|query|string|false|Defines the view configuration for dataset items based on the schema definition.<br>This parameter determines how the data will be filtered and presented.<br>For complete specification details, see the [dataset schema documentation](/storage/dataset-schema).<br>|
|skipFailedPages|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then, the all the items with errorInfo property will be skipped from the output.<br><br>This feature is here to emulate functionality of API version 1 used for the legacy Apify Crawler product and it's not recommended to use it in new integrations.<br>|
|feedTitle|query|string|false|Overrides the auto-generated RSS channel `<title>` element.<br>Only used when `format=rss`. If not provided, the title defaults to `Dataset <label>`.<br>|
|feedDescription|query|string|false|Overrides the auto-generated RSS channel `<description>` element.<br>Only used when `format=rss`. If not provided, the description defaults to `Items in dataset with id "<datasetId>".`<br>|
|body|body|object|true|none|

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|201|X-Apify-Pagination-Offset|string||The offset of the first item in the current page.|
|201|X-Apify-Pagination-Limit|string||The maximum number of items returned per page.|
|201|X-Apify-Pagination-Count|string||The number of items returned in the current page.|
|201|X-Apify-Pagination-Total|string||The total number of items available.|
|201|X-Apify-Pagination-Desc|string||Whether the items are sorted in descending order.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Get last run of an Actor task

<a id="opIdactorTask_runs_last_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-tasks/janedoe~my-task/runs/last \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actor-tasks/{actorTaskId}/runs/last`

This is not a single endpoint, but an entire group of endpoints that lets you to
retrieve and manage the last run of given actor task or any of its default storages.
All the endpoints require an authentication token.

The base path represents the last actor task run object is:

`/v2/actor-tasks/{actorTaskId}/runs/last{?token,status,origin}`

Using the `status` query parameter you can ensure to only get a run with a certain status
(e.g. `status=SUCCEEDED`). Similarly, the `origin` query parameter filters runs by the means
by which they were started (e.g. `origin=API`). The output of this endpoint and other query
parameters are the same as in the [Get Actor run](/api/v2/actor-run-get) endpoint.

##### Convenience endpoints for last Actor task run

* [Last Actor task run's default dataset](/api/v2/last-actor-task-runs-default-dataset)

* [Last Actor task run's default key-value store](/api/v2/last-actor-task-runs-default-key-value-store)

* [Last Actor task run's default request queue](/api/v2/last-actor-task-runs-default-request-queue)

* [Last Actor task run's log](/api/v2/last-actor-task-runs-log)


<h3 id="get-last-run-of-an-actor-task-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorTaskId|path|string|true|Task ID or a tilde-separated owner's username and task's name.|
|status|query|string|false|Filter for the run status.|
|origin|query|string|false|Filter for the run origin, i.e. the means by which the run was started.|
|waitForFinish|query|number(double)|false|The maximum number of seconds the server waits for the run to finish. By<br>default it is `0`, the maximum value is `60`. <!-- MAX_ACTOR_JOB_ASYNC_WAIT_SECS --><br>If the run finishes in time then the returned run object will have a terminal status (e.g. `SUCCEEDED`),<br>otherwise it will have a transitional status (e.g. `RUNNING`).<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|origin|DEVELOPMENT|
|origin|WEB|
|origin|API|
|origin|SCHEDULER|
|origin|TEST|
|origin|WEBHOOK|
|origin|ACTOR|
|origin|CLI|
|origin|CI|
|origin|STANDBY|
|origin|MCP|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

<h1 id="apify-api-storagedatasets">Storage/Datasets</h1>

This section describes API endpoints to manage Datasets.

Dataset is a storage for structured data, where each record stored has the same attributes,
such as online store products or real estate offers. You can imagine it as a table,
where each object is a row and its attributes are columns. Dataset is an append-only
storage - you can only add new records to it but you cannot modify or remove existing
records. Typically it is used to store crawling results.

For more information, see the [Datasets documentation](https://docs.apify.com/platform/storage/dataset).

:::note

Some of the endpoints do not require the authentication token, the calls
are authenticated using the hard-to-guess ID of the dataset.

:::


## Get list of datasets

<a id="opIddatasets_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/datasets \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/datasets`

Lists all of a user's datasets.

The response is a JSON array of objects,
where each object contains basic information about one dataset.

By default, the objects are sorted by the `createdAt` field in ascending
order, therefore you can use pagination to incrementally fetch all datasets while new
ones are still being created. To sort them in descending order, use `desc=1`
parameter. The endpoint supports pagination using `limit` and `offset`
parameters and it will not return more than 1000 array elements.


<h3 id="get-list-of-datasets-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|offset|query|number(double)|false|Number of items that should be skipped at the start. The default value is `0`.<br>|
|limit|query|number(double)|false|Maximum number of items to return. The default value as well as the maximum is `1000`.<br>|
|unnamed|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then all the storages are returned. By default, only<br>named storages are returned.<br>|
|ownership|query|string|false|Filter by ownership. If this parameter is omitted, all accessible datasets are returned.<br><br>- `ownedByMe`: Return only datasets owned by the user.<br>- `sharedWithMe`: Return only datasets shared with the user by other users.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|ownership|ownedByMe|
|ownership|sharedWithMe|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "total": 1,
    "offset": 0,
    "limit": 1000,
    "desc": false,
    "count": 1,
    "unnamed": false,
    "items": [
      {
        "id": "WkzbQMuFYuamGv3YF",
        "name": "d7b9MDYsbtX5L7XAj",
        "userId": "tbXmWu7GCxnyYtSiL",
        "createdAt": "2019-12-12T07:34:14.202Z",
        "modifiedAt": "2019-12-13T08:36:13.202Z",
        "accessedAt": "2019-12-14T08:36:13.202Z",
        "itemCount": 7,
        "cleanItemCount": 5,
        "actId": "zdc3Pyhyz3m8vjDeM",
        "actRunId": "HG7ML7M8z78YcAPEB",
        "title": "My Dataset",
        "username": "janedoe",
        "generalAccess": "RESTRICTED",
        "stats": {
          "readCount": 22,
          "writeCount": 3,
          "storageBytes": 783,
          "inflatedBytes": 0
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-list-of-datasets-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Create dataset

<a id="opIddatasets_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/datasets \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/datasets`

Creates a dataset and returns its object.
Keep in mind that data stored under unnamed dataset follows [data retention period](https://docs.apify.com/platform/storage#data-retention).
It creates a dataset with the given name if the parameter name is used.
If a dataset with the given name already exists then returns its object.


<h3 id="create-dataset-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|query|string|false|Custom unique name to easily identify the dataset in the future.|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|

|201|Created||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

## Get dataset statistics

<a id="opIddataset_statistics_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/datasets/WkzbQMuFYuamGv3YF/statistics \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/datasets/{datasetId}/statistics`

Returns statistics for given dataset.

Provides only [field statistics](https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/development/actor-definition/dataset-schema/validation#dataset-field-statistics).


<h3 id="get-dataset-statistics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|datasetId|path|string|true|Dataset ID or `username~dataset-name`.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

<h1 id="apify-api-storagekey-value-stores">Storage/Key-value stores</h1>

This section describes API endpoints to manage Key-value stores.
Key-value store is a simple storage for saving and reading data records or files.
Each data record is represented by a unique key and associated with a MIME content type.
Key-value stores are ideal for saving screenshots, Actor inputs and outputs, web pages,
PDFs or to persist the state of crawlers.

For more information, see the [Key-value store documentation](https://docs.apify.com/platform/storage/key-value-store).

:::note

Some of the endpoints do not require the authentication token, the calls
are authenticated using a hard-to-guess ID of the key-value store.

:::


## Get list of key-value stores

<a id="opIdkeyValueStores_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/key-value-stores \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/key-value-stores`

Gets the list of key-value stores owned by the user.

The response is a list of objects, where each objects contains a basic
information about a single key-value store.

The endpoint supports pagination using the `limit` and `offset` parameters
and it will not return more than 1000 array elements.

By default, the records are sorted by the `createdAt` field in ascending
order, therefore you can use pagination to incrementally fetch all key-value stores
while new ones are still being created. To sort the records in descending order, use
the `desc=1` parameter.


<h3 id="get-list-of-key-value-stores-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|offset|query|number(double)|false|Number of items that should be skipped at the start. The default value is `0`.<br>|
|limit|query|number(double)|false|Maximum number of items to return. The default value as well as the maximum is `1000`.<br>|
|unnamed|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then all the storages are returned. By default, only<br>named storages are returned.<br>|
|ownership|query|string|false|Filter by ownership. If this parameter is omitted, all accessible key-value stores are returned.<br><br>- `ownedByMe`: Return only key-value stores owned by the user.<br>- `sharedWithMe`: Return only key-value stores shared with the user by other users.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|ownership|ownedByMe|
|ownership|sharedWithMe|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "total": 1,
    "offset": 0,
    "limit": 1000,
    "desc": false,
    "count": 1,
    "unnamed": false,
    "items": [
      {
        "id": "WkzbQMuFYuamGv3YF",
        "name": "d7b9MDYsbtX5L7XAj",
        "title": "My Store",
        "userId": "BPWDBd7Z9c746JAnF",
        "username": "janedoe",
        "createdAt": "2019-12-12T07:34:14.202Z",
        "modifiedAt": "2019-12-13T08:36:13.202Z",
        "accessedAt": "2019-12-14T08:36:13.202Z",
        "actId": null,
        "actRunId": null,
        "schema": {},
        "generalAccess": "RESTRICTED",
        "stats": {
          "readCount": 9,
          "writeCount": 3,
          "deleteCount": 6,
          "listCount": 2,
          "s3StorageBytes": 18
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Create key-value store

<a id="opIdkeyValueStores_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/key-value-stores \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/key-value-stores`

Creates a key-value store and returns its object. The response is the same
object as returned by the [Get key-value store](/api/v2/key-value-store-get)
endpoint.

Keep in mind that data stored under unnamed store follows [data retention
period](https://docs.apify.com/platform/storage#data-retention).

It creates a store with the given name if the parameter name is used.
If there is another store with the same name, the endpoint does not create a
new one and returns the existing object instead.


<h3 id="create-key-value-store-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|query|string|false|Custom unique name to easily identify the store in the future.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

<h1 id="apify-api-storagerequest-queues">Storage/Request queues</h1>

This section describes API endpoints to create, manage, and delete request queues.

Request queue is a storage for a queue of HTTP URLs to crawl, which is typically
used for deep crawling of websites where you
start with several URLs and then recursively follow links to other pages.
The storage supports both breadth-first and depth-first crawling orders.

For more information, see the [Request queue documentation](https://docs.apify.com/platform/storage/request-queue).

:::note

Some of the endpoints do not require the authentication token, the calls
are authenticated using the hard-to-guess ID of the queue.

:::


## Get list of request queues

<a id="opIdrequestQueues_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/request-queues \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/request-queues`

Lists all of a user's request queues. The response is a JSON array of
objects, where each object
contains basic information about one queue.

By default, the objects are sorted by the `createdAt` field in ascending order,
therefore you can use pagination to incrementally fetch all queues while new
ones are still being created. To sort them in descending order, use `desc=1`
parameter. The endpoint supports pagination using `limit` and `offset`
parameters and it will not return more than 1000
array elements.


<h3 id="get-list-of-request-queues-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|offset|query|number(double)|false|Number of items that should be skipped at the start. The default value is `0`.<br>|
|limit|query|number(double)|false|Maximum number of items to return. The default value as well as the maximum is `1000`.<br>|
|unnamed|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then all the storages are returned. By default, only<br>named storages are returned.<br>|
|ownership|query|string|false|Filter by ownership. If this parameter is omitted, all accessible request queues are returned.<br><br>- `ownedByMe`: Return only request queues owned by the user.<br>- `sharedWithMe`: Return only request queues shared with the user by other users.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|ownership|ownedByMe|
|ownership|sharedWithMe|

> Example responses

```json
{

    "desc": false,
    "count": 1,
    "unnamed": false,
    "items": [
      {
        "id": "WkzbQMuFYuamGv3YF",
        "name": "some-name",
        "title": "My Queue",
        "userId": "wRsJZtadYvn4mBZmm",

        "expireAt": "2019-06-02T17:15:06.751Z",
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

<h3 id="get-list-of-request-queues-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|object|true|none|A paginated list of request queues.|
|» total|integer|true|none|The total number of items available across all pages.|
|» offset|integer|true|none|The starting position for this page of results.|
|» limit|integer|true|none|The maximum number of items returned per page.|
|» desc|boolean|true|none|Whether the results are sorted in descending order.|
|» count|integer|true|none|The number of items returned in this response.|
|» unnamed|boolean|false|none|Whether the listing was filtered to only unnamed request queues.|
|» items|[object]|true|none|The array of request queues.|
|» » id|string|true|none|A unique identifier assigned to the request queue.|
|» » name|string \| null|false|none|The name of the request queue.|
|» » title|string \| null|false|none|The title of the request queue.|
|» » userId|string|true|none|The ID of the user who owns the request queue.|
|» » username|string|false|none|The username of the user who owns the request queue.|
|» » createdAt|string(date-time)|true|none|The timestamp when the request queue was created.|
|» » modifiedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|The timestamp when the request queue was last modified. Modifications include adding, updating, or removing requests, as well as locking or unlocking requests in the request queue.|
|» » accessedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|The timestamp when the request queue was last accessed.|
|» » expireAt|string(date-time)|false|none|The timestamp when the request queue will expire and be deleted.|
|» » totalRequestCount|integer|true|none|The total number of requests in the request queue.|
|» » handledRequestCount|integer|true|none|The number of requests that have been handled.|
|» » pendingRequestCount|integer|true|none|The number of requests that are pending and have not been handled yet.|
|» » actId|string \| null|false|none|The ID of the Actor that created this request queue.|
|» » actRunId|string \| null|false|none|The ID of the Actor run that created this request queue.|
|» » hadMultipleClients|boolean|true|none|Whether the request queue has been accessed by multiple different clients.|
|» » generalAccess|string \| null|false|none|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|string|false|none|Defines the general access level for the resource.|
|» » » *anyOf*|null|false|none|none|
|» » stats|object|false|none|Statistics about request queue operations and storage, as returned in request queue lists.|
|» » » deleteCount|integer|false|none|The number of delete operations performed on the request queue.|
|» » » headItemReadCount|integer|false|none|The number of times requests from the head were read.|
|» » » readCount|integer|false|none|The total number of read operations performed on the request queue.|
|» » » writeCount|integer|false|none|The total number of write operations performed on the request queue.|
|» » » s3StorageBytes|integer|false|none|The storage size in bytes of requests stored in S3.|
|» » » dynamodbStorageBytes|integer|false|none|The storage size in bytes of requests stored in DynamoDB.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|» » » *anyOf*|ANYONE_WITH_ID_CAN_READ|
|» » » *anyOf*|ANYONE_WITH_NAME_CAN_READ|
|» » » *anyOf*|FOLLOW_USER_SETTING|
|» » » *anyOf*|RESTRICTED|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Create request queue

<a id="opIdrequestQueues_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/request-queues \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/request-queues`

Creates a request queue and returns its object.
Keep in mind that requests stored under unnamed queue follows [data
retention period](https://docs.apify.com/platform/storage#data-retention).

It creates a queue of given name if the parameter name is used. If a queue
with the given name already exists then the endpoint returns
its object.


<h3 id="create-request-queue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|query|string|false|Custom unique name to easily identify the queue in the future.|

<h3 id="create-request-queue-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns the existing request queue object if a queue with the given name already exists.|Inline|
|201|Created||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

<h3 id="create-request-queue-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|object|true|none|A request queue object containing metadata and statistics.|
|» id|string|true|none|A unique identifier assigned to the request queue.|
|» name|string \| null|false|none|The name of the request queue.|
|» title|string \| null|false|none|The title of the request queue.|
|» userId|string|true|none|The ID of the user who owns the request queue.|
|» actId|string \| null|false|none|The ID of the Actor that created this request queue.|
|» actRunId|string \| null|false|none|The ID of the Actor run that created this request queue.|
|» createdAt|string(date-time)|true|none|The timestamp when the request queue was created.|
|» modifiedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|The timestamp when the request queue was last modified. Modifications include adding, updating, or removing requests, as well as locking or unlocking requests in the request queue.|
|» accessedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|The timestamp when the request queue was last accessed.|
|» totalRequestCount|integer|true|none|The total number of requests in the request queue.|
|» handledRequestCount|integer|true|none|The number of requests that have been handled.|
|» pendingRequestCount|integer|true|none|The number of requests that are pending and have not been handled yet.|
|» hadMultipleClients|boolean|true|none|Whether the request queue has been accessed by multiple different clients.|
|» consoleUrl|string(uri)|true|none|The URL to view the request queue in the Apify console.|
|» stats|object|false|none|Statistics about request queue operations and storage.|
|» » deleteCount|integer|false|none|The number of delete operations performed on the request queue.|
|» » headItemReadCount|integer|false|none|The number of times requests from the head were read.|
|» » readCount|integer|false|none|The total number of read operations performed on the request queue.|
|» » storageBytes|integer|false|none|The total storage size in bytes used by the request queue.|
|» » writeCount|integer|false|none|The total number of write operations performed on the request queue.|
|» generalAccess|string \| null|false|none|none|
|» » *anyOf*|string|false|none|Defines the general access level for the resource.|
|» » *anyOf*|null|false|none|none|

<h1 id="apify-api-storagerequest-queuesrequests-locks">Storage/Request queues/Requests locks</h1>

This section describes API endpoints to create, manage, and delete request locks within request queues.

Request queue is a storage for a queue of HTTP URLs to crawl, which is typically
used for deep crawling of websites where you
start with several URLs and then recursively follow links to other pages.
The storage supports both breadth-first and depth-first crawling orders.

For more information, see the [Request queue documentation](https://docs.apify.com/platform/storage/request-queue).

:::note

Some of the endpoints do not require the authentication token, the calls
are authenticated using the hard-to-guess ID of the queue.

:::


## Get and lock request queue head

<a id="opIdrequestQueue_head_lock_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.apify.com/v2/request-queues/WkzbQMuFYuamGv3YF/head/lock?lockSecs=60' \
  -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/request-queues/{queueId}/head/lock`

Returns the given number of first requests from the queue and locks them for
the given time.

If this endpoint locks the request, no other client or run will be able to get and
lock these requests.

The response contains the `hadMultipleClients` boolean field which indicates
that the queue was accessed by more than one client (with unique or empty
`clientKey`).


<h3 id="get-and-lock-request-queue-head-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|queueId|path|string|true|Queue ID or `username~queue-name`.|
|lockSecs|query|number(double)|true|How long the requests will be locked for (in seconds).|
|limit|query|number(double)|false|How many items from the queue should be returned.|
|clientKey|query|string|false|A unique identifier of the client accessing the request queue. It must<br>be a string between 1 and 32 characters long. This identifier is used to<br>determine whether the queue was accessed by multiple clients. If<br>`clientKey` is not provided,<br>the system considers this API call to come from a new client. For<br>details, see the `hadMultipleClients` field returned by the [Get request queue head](/api/v2/request-queue-head-get) endpoint.<br>|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

<h1 id="apify-api-webhookswebhooks">Webhooks/Webhooks</h1>

This section describes API endpoints to manage webhooks.

Webhooks provide an easy and reliable way to configure the Apify platform
to carry out an action (e.g. a HTTP request to another service) when a certain
system event occurs.
For example, you can use webhooks to start another Actor when an Actor run finishes
or fails.

For more information see [Webhooks documentation](https://docs.apify.com/platform/integrations/webhooks).


## Get list of webhooks

<a id="opIdwebhooks_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/webhooks \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/webhooks`

Gets the list of webhooks that the user created.

The endpoint supports pagination using the `limit` and `offset` parameters
and it will not return more than 1000 records.
By default, the records are sorted by the `createdAt` field in ascending
order. To sort the records in descending order, use the `desc=1`
parameter.


<h3 id="get-list-of-webhooks-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|offset|query|number(double)|false|Number of items that should be skipped at the start. The default value is `0`.<br>|
|limit|query|number(double)|false|Maximum number of items to return. The default value as well as the maximum is `1000`.<br>|

> Example responses

## Create webhook

<a id="opIdwebhooks_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/webhooks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "isAdHoc": false,
    "eventTypes": [
      "ACTOR.RUN.SUCCEEDED"
    ],
    "condition": {
      "actorId": "hksJZtadYvn4mBuin",
      "actorTaskId": "asdLZtadYvn4mBZmm",
      "actorRunId": "hgdKZtadYvn4mBpoi"
    },
    "idempotencyKey": "fdSJmdP3nfs7sfk3y",
    "ignoreSslErrors": false,
    "doNotRetry": false,
    "requestUrl": "http://example.com/",
    "payloadTemplate": "{\\n \"userId\": {{userId}}...",
    "headersTemplate": "{\\n \"Authorization\": \"Bearer ...\"}",
    "description": "this is webhook description",
    "shouldInterpolateStrings": false
  }'
```

`POST /v2/webhooks`

Creates a new webhook with settings provided by the webhook object passed as
JSON in the payload.
The response is the created webhook object.

To avoid duplicating a webhook, use the `idempotencyKey` parameter in the
request body.
Multiple calls to create a webhook with the same `idempotencyKey` will only
create the webhook with the first call and return the existing webhook on
subsequent calls.
Idempotency keys must be unique, so use a UUID or another random string with
enough entropy.

To assign the new webhook to an Actor or task, the request body must contain
`requestUrl`, `eventTypes`, and `condition` properties.

* `requestUrl` is the webhook's target URL, to which data is sent as a POST
request with a JSON payload.
* `eventTypes` is a list of events that will trigger the webhook, e.g. when
the Actor run succeeds.
* `condition` should be an object containing the ID of the Actor or task to
which the webhook will be assigned.
* `payloadTemplate` is a JSON-like string, whose syntax is extended with the
use of variables.
* `headersTemplate` is a JSON-like string, whose syntax is extended with the
use of variables. Following values will be re-written to defaults: "host",
"Content-Type", "X-Apify-Webhook", "X-Apify-Webhook-Dispatch-Id",
"X-Apify-Request-Origin"
* `description` is an optional string.
* `shouldInterpolateStrings` is a boolean indicating whether to interpolate
variables contained inside strings in the `payloadTemplate`

```
    "isAdHoc" : false,
    "requestUrl" : "https://example.com",
    "eventTypes" : [
        "ACTOR.RUN.SUCCEEDED",
        "ACTOR.RUN.ABORTED"
    ],
    "condition" : {
        "actorId": "5sTMwDQywwsLzKRRh",
        "actorTaskId" : "W9bs9JE9v7wprjAnJ"
    },
    "payloadTemplate": "",
    "headersTemplate": "",
    "description": "my awesome webhook",
    "shouldInterpolateStrings": false,
```

**Important**: The request must specify the `Content-Type: application/json`
HTTP header.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "isAdHoc": false,
  "eventTypes": [
    "ACTOR.RUN.SUCCEEDED"
  ],
  "condition": {
    "actorId": "hksJZtadYvn4mBuin",
    "actorTaskId": "asdLZtadYvn4mBZmm",
    "actorRunId": "hgdKZtadYvn4mBpoi"
  },
  "idempotencyKey": "fdSJmdP3nfs7sfk3y",
  "ignoreSslErrors": false,
  "doNotRetry": false,
  "requestUrl": "http://example.com/",
  "payloadTemplate": "{\\n \"userId\": {{userId}}...",
  "headersTemplate": "{\\n \"Authorization\": \"Bearer ...\"}",
  "description": "this is webhook description",
  "shouldInterpolateStrings": false
}
```

## Get webhook

<a id="opIdwebhook_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/webhooks/pVJtoTelgYUq4qJOt \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/webhooks/{webhookId}`

Gets webhook object with all details.

<h3 id="get-webhook-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|webhookId|path|string|true|Webhook ID.|

## Update webhook

<a id="opIdwebhook_put"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/webhooks/pVJtoTelgYUq4qJOt \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "isAdHoc": false,
    "eventTypes": [
      "ACTOR.RUN.SUCCEEDED"
    ],
    "condition": {
      "actorId": "hksJZtadYvn4mBuin",
      "actorTaskId": "asdLZtadYvn4mBZmm",
      "actorRunId": "hgdKZtadYvn4mBpoi"
    },
    "ignoreSslErrors": false,
    "doNotRetry": false,
    "requestUrl": "http://example.com/",
    "payloadTemplate": "{\\n \"userId\": {{userId}}...",
    "headersTemplate": "{\\n \"Authorization\": \"Bearer ...\"}",
    "description": "this is webhook description",
    "shouldInterpolateStrings": false
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/webhooks/{webhookId}`

Updates a webhook using values specified by a webhook object passed as JSON
in the POST payload.
If the object does not define a specific property, its value will not be
updated.

The response is the full webhook object as returned by the
[Get webhook](/api/v2/webhook-get) endpoint.

The request needs to specify the `Content-Type: application/json` HTTP
header!

When providing your API authentication token, we recommend using the
request's `Authorization` header, rather than the URL.
For details, see [Authentication](/api/v2#authentication).


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "isAdHoc": false,
  "eventTypes": [
    "ACTOR.RUN.SUCCEEDED"
  ],
  "condition": {
    "actorId": "hksJZtadYvn4mBuin",
    "actorTaskId": "asdLZtadYvn4mBZmm",
    "actorRunId": "hgdKZtadYvn4mBpoi"
  },
  "ignoreSslErrors": false,
  "doNotRetry": false,
  "requestUrl": "http://example.com/",
  "payloadTemplate": "{\\n \"userId\": {{userId}}...",
  "headersTemplate": "{\\n \"Authorization\": \"Bearer ...\"}",
  "description": "this is webhook description",
  "shouldInterpolateStrings": false
}
```

## Delete webhook

<a id="opIdwebhook_delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/webhooks/pVJtoTelgYUq4qJOt \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/webhooks/{webhookId}`

Deletes a webhook.

<h3 id="delete-webhook-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|webhookId|path|string|true|Webhook ID.|

> Example responses

> 204 Response

```json
{}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "record-not-found",
    "message": "The requested resource was not found."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

<h3 id="delete-webhook-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found - the requested resource does not exist.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

## Test webhook

<a id="opIdwebhook_test_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/webhooks/pVJtoTelgYUq4qJOt/test \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/webhooks/{webhookId}/test`

Tests a webhook. Creates a webhook dispatch with a dummy payload.

<h3 id="test-webhook-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|webhookId|path|string|true|Webhook ID.|

## Get list of webhook's dispatches

<a id="opIdwebhook_webhookDispatches_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/webhooks/pVJtoTelgYUq4qJOt/dispatches \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/webhooks/{webhookId}/dispatches`

Gets a given webhook's list of dispatches.

<h3 id="get-list-of-webhooks-dispatches-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|webhookId|path|string|true|Webhook ID.|
|offset|query|number(double)|false|Number of items that should be skipped at the start. The default value is `0`.<br>|
|limit|query|number(double)|false|Maximum number of items to return. The default value as well as the maximum is `1000`.<br>|

httpBearer, apiKey

<h1 id="apify-api-webhookswebhook-dispatches">Webhooks/Webhook dispatches</h1>

This section describes API endpoints to get webhook dispatches.

## Get list of webhook dispatches

<a id="opIdwebhookDispatches_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/webhook-dispatches \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/webhook-dispatches`

Gets the list of webhook dispatches that the user have.

The endpoint supports pagination using the `limit` and `offset` parameters
and it will not return more than 1000 records.
By default, the records are sorted by the `createdAt` field in ascending
order. To sort the records in descending order, use the `desc=1`
parameter.


<h3 id="get-list-of-webhook-dispatches-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|offset|query|number(double)|false|Number of items that should be skipped at the start. The default value is `0`.<br>|
|limit|query|number(double)|false|Maximum number of items to return. The default value as well as the maximum is `1000`.<br>|

> Example responses

<h3 id="get-list-of-webhook-dispatches-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

<h3 id="get-list-of-webhook-dispatches-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|object|true|none|none|
|» total|integer|true|none|The total number of items available across all pages.|
|» offset|integer|true|none|The starting position for this page of results.|
|» limit|integer|true|none|The maximum number of items returned per page.|
|» desc|boolean|true|none|Whether the results are sorted in descending order.|
|» count|integer|true|none|The number of items returned in this response.|
|» items|[object]|true|none|none|
|» » id|string|true|none|none|
|» » userId|string|true|none|none|
|» » webhookId|string|true|none|none|

## Get webhook dispatch

<a id="opIdwebhookDispatch_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/webhook-dispatches/Zib4xbZsmvZeK55ua \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/webhook-dispatches/{dispatchId}`

Gets webhook dispatch object with all details.

<h3 id="get-webhook-dispatch-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dispatchId|path|string|true|Webhook dispatch ID.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

<h1 id="apify-api-schedules">Schedules</h1>

This section describes API endpoints for managing schedules.

Schedules are used to automatically start your Actors at certain times. Each schedule
can be associated with a number of Actors and Actor tasks. It is also possible
to override the settings of each Actor (task) similarly to when invoking the Actor
(task) using the API.
For more information, see [Schedules documentation](https://docs.apify.com/platform/schedules).

Each schedule is assigned actions for it to perform. Actions can be of two types
- `RUN_ACTOR` and `RUN_ACTOR_TASK`.

For details, see the documentation of the [Get schedule](/api/v2/schedule-get) endpoint.


## Get list of schedules

<a id="opIdschedules_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/schedules \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/schedules`

Gets the list of schedules that the user created.

The endpoint supports pagination using the `limit` and `offset` parameters.
It will not return more than 1000 records.

By default, the records are sorted by the `createdAt` field in ascending
order. To sort the records in descending order, use the `desc=1` parameter.


<h3 id="get-list-of-schedules-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|offset|query|number(double)|false|Number of items that should be skipped at the start. The default value is `0`.<br>|
|limit|query|number(double)|false|Maximum number of items to return. The default value as well as the maximum is `1000`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "total": 1,
    "offset": 0,
    "limit": 1000,
    "desc": false,
    "count": 1,
    "items": [
      {
        "id": "asdLZtadYvn4mBZmm",
        "userId": "wRsJZtadYvn4mBZmm",
        "name": "my-schedule",
        "cronExpression": "* * * * *",
        "timezone": "UTC",
        "isEnabled": true,
        "isExclusive": true,
        "createdAt": "2019-12-12T07:34:14.202Z",
        "modifiedAt": "2019-12-20T06:33:11.202Z",
        "nextRunAt": "2019-04-12T07:34:10.202Z",
        "lastRunAt": "2019-04-12T07:33:10.202Z",
        "title": "string",
        "notifications": {
          "email": true
        },
        "integrationTracking": {
          "platform": "zapier",
          "appId": "string",
          "isAiTool": false
        },
        "actions": [
          {
            "id": "ZReCs7hkdieq8ZUki",
            "type": "RUN_ACTOR",
            "actorId": "HKhKmiCMrDgu9eXeE"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-list-of-schedules-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

## Create schedule

<a id="opIdschedules_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/schedules \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "my-schedule",
    "isEnabled": true,
    "isExclusive": true,
    "cronExpression": "* * * * *",
    "timezone": "UTC",
    "description": "Schedule of actor ...",
    "title": "string",
    "notifications": {
      "email": true
    },
    "actions": [
      {
        "type": "RUN_ACTOR",
        "actorId": "jF8GGEvbEg4Au3NLA",
        "runInput": {
          "body": "{\\n   \"foo\": \"actor\"\\n}",
          "contentType": "application/json; charset=utf-8"
        },
        "runOptions": {
          "build": "latest",
          "timeoutSecs": 300,
          "memoryMbytes": 1024,
          "maxItems": 1000,
          "maxTotalChargeUsd": 5,
          "restartOnError": false,
          "isMaxTotalChargeUsdSetByUser": true,
          "forcePermissionLevel": "LIMITED_PERMISSIONS"
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v2/schedules`

Creates a new schedule with settings provided by the schedule object passed
as JSON in the payload. The response is the created schedule object.

The request needs to specify the `Content-Type: application/json` HTTP header!

When providing your API authentication token, we recommend using the
request's `Authorization` header, rather than the URL.
For details, see [Authentication](/api/v2#authentication).


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "my-schedule",
  "isEnabled": true,
  "isExclusive": true,
  "cronExpression": "* * * * *",
  "timezone": "UTC",
  "description": "Schedule of actor ...",
  "title": "string",
  "notifications": {
    "email": true
  },
  "actions": [
    {
      "type": "RUN_ACTOR",
      "actorId": "jF8GGEvbEg4Au3NLA",
      "runInput": {
        "body": "{\\n   \"foo\": \"actor\"\\n}",
        "contentType": "application/json; charset=utf-8"
      },
      "runOptions": {
        "build": "latest",
        "timeoutSecs": 300,
        "memoryMbytes": 1024,
        "maxItems": 1000,
        "maxTotalChargeUsd": 5,
        "restartOnError": false,
        "isMaxTotalChargeUsdSetByUser": true,
        "forcePermissionLevel": "LIMITED_PERMISSIONS"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

## Get schedule

<a id="opIdschedule_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/schedules/asdLZtadYvn4mBZmm \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/schedules/{scheduleId}`

Gets the schedule object with all details.

<h3 id="get-schedule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|scheduleId|path|string|true|Schedule ID.|

## Update schedule

<a id="opIdschedule_put"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/schedules/asdLZtadYvn4mBZmm \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "my-schedule",
    "isEnabled": true,
    "isExclusive": true,
    "cronExpression": "* * * * *",
    "timezone": "UTC",
    "description": "Schedule of actor ...",
    "title": "string",
    "notifications": {
      "email": true
    },
    "actions": [
      {
        "type": "RUN_ACTOR",
        "actorId": "jF8GGEvbEg4Au3NLA",
        "runInput": {
          "body": "{\\n   \"foo\": \"actor\"\\n}",
          "contentType": "application/json; charset=utf-8"
        },
        "runOptions": {
          "build": "latest",
          "timeoutSecs": 300,
          "memoryMbytes": 1024,
          "maxItems": 1000,
          "maxTotalChargeUsd": 5,
          "restartOnError": false,
          "isMaxTotalChargeUsdSetByUser": true,
          "forcePermissionLevel": "LIMITED_PERMISSIONS"
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/schedules/{scheduleId}`

Updates a schedule using values specified by a schedule object passed as
JSON in the POST payload. If the object does not define a specific property,
its value will not be updated.

The response is the full schedule object as returned by the
[Get schedule](/api/v2/schedule-get) endpoint.

**The request needs to specify the `Content-Type: application/json` HTTP
header!**

When providing your API authentication token, we recommend using the
request's `Authorization` header, rather than the URL.
For details, see [Authentication](/api/v2#authentication).


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "my-schedule",
  "isEnabled": true,
  "isExclusive": true,
  "cronExpression": "* * * * *",
  "timezone": "UTC",
  "description": "Schedule of actor ...",
  "title": "string",
  "notifications": {
    "email": true
  },
  "actions": [
    {
      "type": "RUN_ACTOR",
      "actorId": "jF8GGEvbEg4Au3NLA",
      "runInput": {
        "body": "{\\n   \"foo\": \"actor\"\\n}",
        "contentType": "application/json; charset=utf-8"
      },
      "runOptions": {
        "build": "latest",
        "timeoutSecs": 300,
        "memoryMbytes": 1024,
        "maxItems": 1000,
        "maxTotalChargeUsd": 5,
        "restartOnError": false,
        "isMaxTotalChargeUsdSetByUser": true,
        "forcePermissionLevel": "LIMITED_PERMISSIONS"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

## Delete schedule

<a id="opIdschedule_delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/schedules/asdLZtadYvn4mBZmm \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/schedules/{scheduleId}`

Deletes a schedule.

|---|---|---|---|---|
|scheduleId|path|string|true|Schedule ID.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Invoke schedule

<a id="opIdschedule_invoke_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/schedules/asdLZtadYvn4mBZmm/invoke \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/schedules/{scheduleId}/invoke`

Immediately runs all actions of the schedule, the same way as the **Run now** button in Apify Console.

The invocation is recorded in the [schedule log](/api/v2/schedule-log-get). It doesn't change the schedule's
`lastRunAt` or `nextRunAt`. The response doesn't contain the started runs.


<h3 id="invoke-schedule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|scheduleId|path|string|true|Schedule ID.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "record-not-found",
    "message": "The requested resource was not found."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|

|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found - the requested resource does not exist.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

## Get schedule log

<a id="opIdschedule_log_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/schedules/asdLZtadYvn4mBZmm/log \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/schedules/{scheduleId}/log`

Gets the schedule log as a JSON array containing information about up to a
1000 invocations of the schedule.


<h3 id="get-schedule-log-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|scheduleId|path|string|true|Schedule ID.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "message": "Schedule invoked",
      "level": "INFO",
      "createdAt": "2019-03-26T12:28:00.370Z"
    },
    {
      "message": "Cannot start Actor task \\\"iEvfA6pm6DWjRTGxS\\\": Provided input must be object, got \\\"string\\\" instead.",
      "level": "ERROR",
      "createdAt": "2019-03-26T12:30:00.325Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "record-not-found",
    "message": "The requested resource was not found."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-schedule-log-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found - the requested resource does not exist.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

<h3 id="get-schedule-log-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|[object]|true|none|none|
|» message|string|true|none|none|
|» level|string|true|none|none|
|» createdAt|string(date-time)|true|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

<h1 id="apify-api-store">Store</h1>

[Apify Store](https://apify.com/store) is home to thousands of public Actors available
to the Apify community.
The API endpoints described in this section are used to retrieve these Actors.

:::note

These endpoints do not require the authentication token.

:::


## Get list of Actors in Store

<a id="opIdstore_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/store \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/store`

Gets the list of public Actors in Apify Store. You can use `search`
parameter to search Actors by string in title, name, description, username
and readme.
If you need detailed info about a specific Actor, use the [Get Actor](/api/v2/actor-get) endpoint.

The endpoint supports pagination using the `limit` and `offset` parameters.
It will not return more than 1,000 records.


<h3 id="get-list-of-actors-in-store-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|number(double)|false|Maximum number of items to return. The default value as well as the maximum is `1000`.<br>|
|offset|query|number(double)|false|Number of items that should be skipped at the start. The default value is `0`.<br>|
|search|query|string|false|String to search by. The search runs on the following fields: `title`,<br>`name`, `description`, `username`, `readme`.<br>|
|sortBy|query|string|false|Specifies the field by which to sort the results. The supported values<br>are `relevance` (default), `popularity`, `newest` and `lastUpdate`.<br>|
|category|query|string|false|Filters the results by the specified category.|
|username|query|string|false|Filters the results by the specified username.|
|pricingModel|query|string|false|Only return Actors with the specified pricing model.<br>|
|allowsAgenticUsers|query|boolean|false|If true, only return Actors that allow agentic users. If false, only<br>return Actors that do not allow agentic users.<br>|
|responseFormat|query|string|false|Controls the shape of the response. Use `full` (default) for the<br>complete response including image URLs and all fields. Use `agent`<br>for a reduced field set optimized for LLM consumers, which only<br>includes `id`, `title`, `name`, `username`, `description`, `notice`,<br>`badge`, `categories`, and minimal `stats`.<br>|
|includeUnrunnableActors|query|boolean|false|By default, search results exclude Actors that are not safe to run<br>automatically (e.g. Actors from developers who haven't passed KYC, or<br>full-permission Actors without a large user base). Set to `true` to<br>bypass this safety filtering and include all Actors in the results.<br>|
|includeInputSchema|query|boolean|false|If `true`, each Actor in the results includes an `inputSchema` field with a compact version of the input<br>schema of its default build (property types and required properties only). With this parameter, `limit`<br>defaults to and can't exceed `10`.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|pricingModel|FREE|
|pricingModel|PRICE_PER_DATASET_ITEM|
|pricingModel|PAY_PER_EVENT|
|responseFormat|full|
|responseFormat|agent|
