<h1 id="apify-api-logs">Logs</h1>

The API endpoints described in this section are used the download the logs
generated by Actor builds and runs. Note that only the trailing 5M characters
of the log are stored, the rest is discarded.

:::note

Note that the endpoints do not require the authentication token, the calls
are authenticated using a hard-to-guess ID of the Actor build or run.

:::


## Get Actor build or run log

<a id="opIdlog_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/logs/HG7ML7M8z78YcAPE \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/logs/{buildOrRunId}`

Retrieves logs for a specific Actor build or run.


<h3 id="get-actor-build-or-run-log-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|buildOrRunId|path|string|true|ID of the Actor build or run.|
|stream|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then the logs will be streamed as long as the run or build is running.<br>|
|download|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then the web browser will download the log file rather than open it in a tab.<br>|
|raw|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1`, the logs will be kept verbatim. By default, the API removes<br>ANSI escape codes from the logs, keeping only printable characters.<br>|

<aside class="warning">
Authentication is optional for this operation. To authenticate, use one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

<h1 id="apify-api-users">Users</h1>

The API endpoints described in this section return information about
user accounts.


## Get public user data

<a id="opIduser_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/users/HGzIk8z78YcAPEB \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/users/{userId}`

Returns public information about a specific user account, similar to what
can be seen on public profile pages (e.g. https://apify.com/apify).

This operation requires no authentication token.

When the request is authenticated with an API token of the requested user account, or with a token
that impersonates it, the response also contains the private information, the same as in
[Get private user data](/api/v2/users-me-get). Tokens with limited permissions never receive it.


<h3 id="get-public-user-data-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|userId|path|string|true|User ID or username.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "username": "d7b9MDYsbtX5L7XAj",
    "profile": {
      "bio": "I started web scraping in 1985 using Altair BASIC.",
      "readme": "### Hello world 👋🏻\nI build web scrapers.",
      "name": "Jane Doe",
      "pictureUrl": "https://apify.com/img/anonymous_user_picture.png",
      "githubUsername": "torvalds.",
      "websiteUrl": "http://www.example.com",
      "twitterUsername": "@BillGates"
    }
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "record-not-found",
    "message": "The requested resource was not found."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-public-user-data-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found - the requested resource does not exist.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

## Get private user data

<a id="opIdusers_me_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/users/me \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/users/me`

Returns information about the current user account, including both public
and private information.

The user account is identified by the provided authentication token.

The fields `plan`, `email` and `profile` are omitted when this endpoint is accessed from Actor run.

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Get git provider integrations

<a id="opIdintegrations_git_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/integrations/git \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/integrations/git`

Gets your connected git provider accounts (GitHub App, GitLab and Bitbucket), each with the workspaces you can
create a repository in. Only authorized accounts are returned, and accounts whose access was revoked are left
out.

Use the `id` of an integration as the `providerId` in the
[Create git repository](/api/v2/integrations-git-create-repo-post) and
[Register deployment key](/api/v2/integrations-git-register-deployment-key-post) endpoints.


> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "github-app",
      "provider": "github",
      "workspaces": [
        {
          "id": "janedoe",
          "label": "janedoe"
        }
      ],
      "addWorkspaceUrl": "https://github.com/apps/apify/installations/new"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-git-provider-integrations-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

<h3 id="get-git-provider-integrations-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|[object]|true|none|none|
|» id|string|true|none|The provider ID to use in the `providerId` path parameter: `github-app` for the GitHub App, or the ID of a<br>connected GitLab or Bitbucket integration.<br>|
|» provider|string|true|none|none|
|» workspaces|[object]|true|none|The workspaces the account can create a repository in. Empty if listing them failed.|
|» » id|string|true|none|The workspace identifier to pass as `workspace` when creating a repository: the account or organization login<br>on GitHub, the numeric namespace ID on GitLab, or the workspace slug on Bitbucket.<br>|
|» » label|string|true|none|none|
|» addWorkspaceUrl|string|false|none|URL where the user can install the GitHub App on another account or organization. Only for the GitHub App.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|» provider|github|
|» provider|gitlab|
|» provider|bitbucket|

Status Code **400**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|error|object|true|none|none|
|» type|string|false|none|Machine-processable error type identifier.|
|» message|string|false|none|Human-readable error message describing what went wrong.|
|» data|object|false|none|Additional machine-readable details about the error. Present only for some error types.|

</aside>

## Create git repository

<a id="opIdintegrations_git_createRepo_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/integrations/git/github-app/create-repo \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "workspace": "janedoe",
    "repoName": "my-actor",
    "isPrivate": true,
    "files": [
      {
        "path": "src/main.js",
        "content": "console.log('\''Hello'\'');",
        "encoding": "utf-8"
      }
    ],
    "templateArchiveUrl": "https://github.com/apify/actor-templates/blob/master/dist/templates/js-start.zip?raw=true"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/integrations/git/{providerId}/create-repo`

Creates a repository through a connected git account and commits the initial files into it, either the given
`files` or the files of an Actor template archive (`templateArchiveUrl`).


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "workspace": "janedoe",
  "repoName": "my-actor",
  "isPrivate": true,
  "files": [
    {
      "path": "src/main.js",
      "content": "console.log('Hello');",
      "encoding": "utf-8"
    }
  ],
  "templateArchiveUrl": "https://github.com/apify/actor-templates/blob/master/dist/templates/js-start.zip?raw=true"
}
```

<h3 id="create-git-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|providerId|path|string|true|The connected git account to use: `github-app` for the GitHub App, or the ID of a connected GitLab or<br>Bitbucket integration, as returned by [Get git provider integrations](/api/v2/integrations-git-get).<br>|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» workspace|body|string|true|Where to create the repository, as the `id` of one of the provider's workspaces. On GitLab, this is the<br>numeric namespace ID.<br>|
|» repoName|body|string|true|none|
|» isPrivate|body|boolean|true|none|
|» files|body|[object]|false|Files to commit as the initial commit. Can't be combined with `templateArchiveUrl`.|
|» » path|body|string|true|none|
|» » content|body|string|true|none|
|» » encoding|body|string|true|none|
|» templateArchiveUrl|body|string|false|URL of an Actor template archive whose files are committed as the initial commit. Can't be combined with<br>`files`.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » encoding|utf-8|
|» » encoding|base64|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "sshUrl": "git@github.com:janedoe/my-actor.git",
    "httpsUrl": "https://github.com/janedoe/my-actor.git",
    "htmlUrl": "https://github.com/janedoe/my-actor"
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

```json
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

```json
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",

  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "record-not-found",
    "message": "The requested resource was not found."
  }
}
```

```json
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
```

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Register deployment key

<a id="opIdintegrations_git_registerDeploymentKey_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/integrations/git/github-app/register-deployment-key \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "actorId": "janedoe~my-actor",
    "repoName": "https://github.com/janedoe/my-actor"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/integrations/git/{providerId}/register-deployment-key`

Registers the Actor's deployment key (a read-only SSH key generated for every Actor) on a repository through a
connected git account, so that Apify can clone the repository when building the Actor.

You need write access to the Actor. The repository's host must match the provider of the connected account.
If the key is already registered on the repository, nothing changes. On GitHub, registering the key on another
repository removes it from the previously linked one.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "actorId": "janedoe~my-actor",
  "repoName": "https://github.com/janedoe/my-actor"
}
```

<h3 id="register-deployment-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|providerId|path|string|true|The connected git account to use: `github-app` for the GitHub App, or the ID of a connected GitLab or<br>Bitbucket integration, as returned by [Get git provider integrations](/api/v2/integrations-git-get).<br>|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» actorId|body|string|true|ID or `username~name` of the Actor whose deployment key to register.|
|» repoName|body|string|true|URL of the repository to register the key on. Its host must match the provider.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "repoName": "https://github.com/janedoe/my-actor"
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "record-not-found",
    "message": "The requested resource was not found."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 413 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "request-too-large",
    "message": "The POST payload is too large (limit: 9437184 bytes, actual length: 10485760 bytes)."
  }
}
```

> 415 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "unsupported-content-encoding",
    "message": "Content-Encoding \"bla\" is not supported."
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

<h1 id="apify-api-usersusage">Users/Usage</h1>

The API endpoints described in this section return your account's usage for the
current monthly cycle and let you view and update your account limits.

For details, see the [Limits](https://docs.apify.com/account/limits).


## Get user's monthly usage

<a id="opIdusers_me_usage_monthly_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/users/me/usage/monthly \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/users/me/usage/monthly`

Returns a complete summary of your usage for the current monthly usage cycle,
an overall sum, as well as a daily breakdown of usage. It is the same
information you will see on your account's [Billing > Historical usage page](https://console.apify.com/billing/historical-usage). The information
includes your use of Actors, compute, data transfer, and storage.

Using the `date` parameter will show your usage in the monthly usage cycle that
includes that date.


<h3 id="get-users-monthly-usage-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|date|query|string|false|Date in the YYYY-MM-DD format.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Get user's limits

<a id="opIdusers_me_limits_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/users/me/limits \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/users/me/limits`

Returns a complete summary of your account's limits. It is the same
information you will see on your account's [Limits page](https://console.apify.com/billing#/limits). The returned data
includes the current usage cycle, a summary of your limits, and your current usage.


> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "monthlyUsageCycle": {
      "startAt": "2022-10-02T00:00:00.000Z",
      "endAt": "2022-11-01T23:59:59.999Z"
    },
    "limits": {
      "maxMonthlyUsageUsd": 300,
      "maxMonthlyActorComputeUnits": 1000,
      "maxMonthlyExternalDataTransferGbytes": 7,
      "maxMonthlyProxySerps": 50,
      "maxMonthlyResidentialProxyGbytes": 0.5,
      "maxActorMemoryGbytes": 16,
      "maxActorCount": 100,
      "maxActorTaskCount": 1000,
      "maxConcurrentActorJobs": 256,
      "maxTeamAccountSeatCount": 9,
      "dataRetentionDays": 90,
      "maxScheduleCount": 100,
      "maxMonthlyUnblockerUnits": 1000000
    },
    "current": {
      "monthlyUsageUsd": 43,
      "monthlyActorComputeUnits": 500.784475,
      "monthlyExternalDataTransferGbytes": 3.00861903931946,
      "monthlyProxySerps": 34,
      "monthlyResidentialProxyGbytes": 0.4,
      "actorMemoryGbytes": 8,
      "actorCount": 31,
      "actorTaskCount": 130,
      "activeActorJobCount": 0,
      "teamAccountSeatCount": 5,
      "scheduleCount": 77,
      "monthlyUnblockerUnits": 1520
    }
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-users-limits-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Update user's limits

<a id="opIdusers_me_limits_put"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/users/me/limits \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "maxMonthlyUsageUsd": 300,
    "dataRetentionDays": 90
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/users/me/limits`

Updates the account's limits manageable on your account's [Limits page](https://console.apify.com/billing#/limits).
Specifically the: `maxMonthlyUsageUsd` and `dataRetentionDays` limits (see request body schema for more details).


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "maxMonthlyUsageUsd": 300,
  "dataRetentionDays": 90
}
```

<h3 id="update-users-limits-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» maxMonthlyUsageUsd|body|number|false|If your platform usage in the billing period exceeds the prepaid usage, you will be charged extra. Setting this property you can update your hard limit on monthly platform usage to prevent accidental overage or to limit the extra charges.<br>|
|» dataRetentionDays|body|integer|false|Apify securely stores your ten most recent Actor runs indefinitely, ensuring they are always accessible. Unnamed storages and other Actor runs are automatically deleted after the retention period. If you're subscribed, you can change it to keep data for longer or to limit your usage. [Lear more](https://docs.apify.com/storage#data-retention).<br>|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 413 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "request-too-large",
    "message": "The POST payload is too large (limit: 9437184 bytes, actual length: 10485760 bytes)."
  }
}
```

```json
  }
}
```

```json
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",

  }
}
```

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Get user's monthly usage by ID

<a id="opIdusers_usage_monthly_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/users/HGzIk8z78YcAPEB/usage/monthly \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/users/{userId}/usage/monthly`

Returns the same summary of monthly usage as [Get user's monthly usage](/api/v2/users-me-usage-monthly-get),
for an account given by its ID or username.

You can only access your own account, or the organization your API token belongs to. API tokens with
limited permissions can't use this endpoint.

Using the `date` parameter will show the usage in the monthly usage cycle that
includes that date.


<h3 id="get-users-monthly-usage-by-id-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|userId|path|string|true|User ID or username of your account, or of the organization your API token belongs to.|
|date|query|string|false|Date in the YYYY-MM-DD format.|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Get user's limits by ID

<a id="opIdusers_limits_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/users/HGzIk8z78YcAPEB/limits \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/users/{userId}/limits`

Returns the same summary of limits as [Get user's limits](/api/v2/users-me-limits-get), for an account given by
its ID or username.

You can only access your own account, or the organization your API token belongs to. API tokens with
limited permissions can't use this endpoint.


<h3 id="get-users-limits-by-id-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|userId|path|string|true|User ID or username of your account, or of the organization your API token belongs to.|

> Example responses

## Update user's limits by ID

<a id="opIdusers_limits_put"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/users/HGzIk8z78YcAPEB/limits \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "maxMonthlyUsageUsd": 300,
    "dataRetentionDays": 90
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/users/{userId}/limits`

Updates the same limits as [Update user's limits](/api/v2/users-me-limits-put), for an account given by its ID
or username.

You can only access your own account, or the organization your API token belongs to. API tokens with
limited permissions can't use this endpoint.
For an organization, you also need the permission to manage the organization.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "maxMonthlyUsageUsd": 300,
  "dataRetentionDays": 90
}
```

<h3 id="update-users-limits-by-id-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|userId|path|string|true|User ID or username of your account, or of the organization your API token belongs to.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» maxMonthlyUsageUsd|body|number|false|If your platform usage in the billing period exceeds the prepaid usage, you will be charged extra. Setting this property you can update your hard limit on monthly platform usage to prevent accidental overage or to limit the extra charges.<br>|
|» dataRetentionDays|body|integer|false|Apify securely stores your ten most recent Actor runs indefinitely, ensuring they are always accessible. Unnamed storages and other Actor runs are automatically deleted after the retention period. If you're subscribed, you can change it to keep data for longer or to limit your usage. [Lear more](https://docs.apify.com/storage#data-retention).<br>|

<h1 id="apify-api-toolsencoding">Tools/Encoding</h1>

The API endpoints described in this section provide utility tools for encoding and decoding data.


## Encode and sign object

<a id="opIdtools_encode_and_sign_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/tools/encode-and-sign \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "key": "value"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/tools/encode-and-sign`

Encodes and signs any JSON object. The encoded value includes a signature
tied to the authenticated user's ID, which can later be verified using the
decode-and-verify endpoint.

**Important**: The request must specify the `Content-Type: application/json`
HTTP header.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "key": "value"
}
```

<h3 id="encode-and-sign-object-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "encoded": "eyJwYXlsb2FkIjoiLi4uIiwic2lnbmF0dXJlIjoiLi4uIn0="
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-token",
    "message": "Authentication token is not valid."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient-permissions",
    "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 413 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "request-too-large",
    "message": "The POST payload is too large (limit: 9437184 bytes, actual length: 10485760 bytes)."
  }
}
```

> 415 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "unsupported-content-encoding",
    "message": "Content-Encoding \"bla\" is not supported."
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

<h3 id="encode-and-sign-object-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized - authentication required or invalid token.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden - insufficient permissions to perform this action.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|413|Payload Too Large|Payload too large - the request body exceeds the size limit.|Inline|
|415|Unsupported Media Type|Unsupported media type - the Content-Encoding of the request is not supported.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

## Decode and verify object

<a id="opIdtools_decode_and_verify_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/tools/decode-and-verify \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "encoded": "eyJwYXlsb2FkIjoiLi4uIiwic2lnbmF0dXJlIjoiLi4uIn0="
  }'
```

`POST /v2/tools/decode-and-verify`

Decodes and verifies an encoded value previously created by the
encode-and-sign endpoint. Returns the original decoded object along with
information about the user who encoded it and whether that user is verified.

**Important**: The request must specify the `Content-Type: application/json`
HTTP header.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "encoded": "eyJwYXlsb2FkIjoiLi4uIiwic2lnbmF0dXJlIjoiLi4uIn0="
}
```

<h3 id="decode-and-verify-object-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» encoded|body|string|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "decoded": null,
    "encodedByUserId": "wRwJZtadYvn4mBZmm",
    "isVerifiedUser": false
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid-input",
    "message": "Invalid input: The request body contains invalid data."
  }
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "method-not-allowed",
    "message": "This API end-point can only be accessed using the following HTTP methods: OPTIONS,GET"
  }
}
```

> 413 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "request-too-large",
    "message": "The POST payload is too large (limit: 9437184 bytes, actual length: 10485760 bytes)."
  }
}
```

> 415 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "unsupported-content-encoding",
    "message": "Content-Encoding \"bla\" is not supported."
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate-limit-exceeded",
    "message": "You have exceeded the rate limit. Please try again later."
  }
}
```

<h3 id="decode-and-verify-object-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request - invalid input parameters or request body.|Inline|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.|Inline|
|413|Payload Too Large|Payload too large - the request body exceeds the size limit.|Inline|
|415|Unsupported Media Type|Unsupported media type - the Content-Encoding of the request is not supported.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests - rate limit exceeded.|Inline|

<h3 id="decode-and-verify-object-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|object|true|none|none|
|» decoded|object|true|none|The original object that was encoded.|
|» encodedByUserId|string \| null|true|none|none|
|» isVerifiedUser|boolean|true|none|none|

Status Code **400**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|error|object|true|none|none|
|» type|string|false|none|Machine-processable error type identifier.|
|» message|string|false|none|Human-readable error message describing what went wrong.|
|» data|object|false|none|Additional machine-readable details about the error. Present only for some error types.|

<h1 id="apify-api-default-dataset">Default dataset</h1>

The API endpoints described in this section are convenience endpoints that provide access to Actor run's default dataset without the need to resolve the dataset ID first.

Subset of functionality described in: [Datasets](/api/v2/storage-datasets)


## Get the default dataset statistics for an Actor run

<a id="opIdactorRun_dataset_statistics_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-runs/3KH8gEpp4d8uQSe8T/dataset/statistics \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actor-runs/{runId}/dataset/statistics`

Returns statistics for the Actor run's default dataset.

This endpoint is a shortcut that resolves the run's `defaultDatasetId` and proxies to the
[Get dataset statistics](/api/v2/dataset-statistics-get) endpoint.


<h3 id="get-the-default-dataset-statistics-for-an-actor-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|runId|path|string|true|Actor run ID.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

<h1 id="apify-api-default-request-queue">Default request queue</h1>

The API endpoints described in this section are convenience endpoints that provide access to Actor run's default request queue without the need to resolve the request queue ID first.

Subset of functionality described in: [Request queues](/api/v2/storage-request-queues)


## Get and lock the default request queue head for an Actor run

<a id="opIdactorRun_requestQueue_head_lock_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-runs/3KH8gEpp4d8uQSe8T/request-queue/head/lock?lockSecs=60' \
  -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/actor-runs/{runId}/request-queue/head/lock`

Returns the given number of first requests from the default request queue of the Actor run
and locks them for the given time.

This endpoint is a shortcut for getting the run's `defaultRequestQueueId` and then using the
[Get and lock request queue head](/api/v2/request-queue-head-lock-post) endpoint.


<h3 id="get-and-lock-the-default-request-queue-head-for-an-actor-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|runId|path|string|true|Actor run ID.|
|lockSecs|query|number(double)|true|How long the requests will be locked for (in seconds).|
|limit|query|number(double)|false|How many items from the queue should be returned.|
|clientKey|query|string|false|A unique identifier of the client accessing the request queue. It must<br>be a string between 1 and 32 characters long. This identifier is used to<br>determine whether the queue was accessed by multiple clients. If<br>`clientKey` is not provided,<br>the system considers this API call to come from a new client. For<br>details, see the `hadMultipleClients` field returned by the [Get request queue head](/api/v2/request-queue-head-get) endpoint.<br>|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

<h1 id="apify-api-last-actor-runs-default-dataset">Last Actor run's default dataset</h1>

The API endpoints described in this section are convenience endpoints that provide access to Actor's last run's default dataset without the need to resolve the dataset ID first.

Subset of functionality described in: [Datasets](/api/v2/storage-datasets)


## Get the default dataset statistics for an Actor's last run

<a id="opIdactor_runs_last_dataset_statistics_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/runs/last/dataset/statistics \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actors/{actorId}/runs/last/dataset/statistics`

Returns statistics for the last Actor run's default dataset.

This endpoint is a shortcut that resolves the last run's `defaultDatasetId` and proxies to the
[Get dataset statistics](/api/v2/dataset-statistics-get) endpoint.


<h3 id="get-the-default-dataset-statistics-for-an-actors-last-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|status|query|string|false|Filter for the run status.|
|origin|query|string|false|Filter for the run origin, i.e. the means by which the run was started.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|origin|DEVELOPMENT|
|origin|WEB|
|origin|API|
|origin|SCHEDULER|
|origin|TEST|
|origin|WEBHOOK|
|origin|ACTOR|
|origin|CLI|
|origin|CI|
|origin|STANDBY|
|origin|MCP|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

<h1 id="apify-api-last-actor-runs-log">Last Actor run's log</h1>

The API endpoint described in this section is convenience endpoint that provides access to last Actor run's log.

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actors/{actorId}/runs/last/log`

Retrieves last Actor run's logs.

This endpoint is a shortcut for getting last Actor run's log. Same as [Get Actor build or run log](/api/v2/log-get) endpoint.


<h3 id="get-log-of-an-actors-last-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|status|query|string|false|Filter for the run status.|
|origin|query|string|false|Filter for the run origin, i.e. the means by which the run was started.|
|stream|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then the logs will be streamed as long as the run or build is running.<br>|

|raw|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1`, the logs will be kept verbatim. By default, the API removes<br>ANSI escape codes from the logs, keeping only printable characters.<br>|

|origin|ACTOR|
|origin|CLI|
|origin|CI|
|origin|STANDBY|
|origin|MCP|

<h1 id="apify-api-last-actor-runs-abort">Last Actor run's abort</h1>

The API endpoint described in this section is a convenience endpoint that aborts the Actor's last run.

Same as of functionality described in: [Abort Actor run](/api/v2/actor-run-abort-post)


## Abort Actor's last run

<a id="opIdactor_runs_last_abort_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/runs/last/abort \
  -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/actors/{actorId}/runs/last/abort`

Aborts the last run of the specified Actor and returns an object that
contains all the details about the run.

This endpoint is a shortcut for [Abort Actor run](/api/v2/actor-run-abort-post)
on the Actor's last run. Only runs that are starting or running are aborted.
For runs with status `FINISHED`, `FAILED`, `ABORTING` and `TIMED-OUT` this call
does nothing.


<h3 id="abort-actors-last-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|status|query|string|false|Filter for the run status.|
|origin|query|string|false|Filter for the run origin, i.e. the means by which the run was started.|
|gracefully|query|boolean|false|If true passed, the Actor run will abort gracefully.<br>It will send `aborting` and `persistState` event into run and force-stop the run after 30 seconds.<br>It is helpful in cases where you plan to resurrect the run later.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|origin|DEVELOPMENT|
|origin|WEB|
|origin|API|
|origin|SCHEDULER|
|origin|TEST|
|origin|WEBHOOK|
|origin|ACTOR|
|origin|CLI|
|origin|CI|
|origin|STANDBY|
|origin|MCP|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

<h1 id="apify-api-last-actor-runs-metamorph">Last Actor run's metamorph</h1>

The API endpoint described in this section is a convenience endpoint that metamorphs the Actor's last run into a run of another Actor.

Same as of functionality described in: [Metamorph Actor run](/api/v2/actor-run-metamorph-post)


## Metamorph Actor's last run

<a id="opIdactor_runs_last_metamorph_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/runs/last/metamorph?targetActorId=HDSasDasz78YcAPEB' \
  -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/actors/{actorId}/runs/last/metamorph`

Transforms the last run of the specified Actor into a run of another Actor with
a new input.

This endpoint is a shortcut for [Metamorph Actor run](/api/v2/actor-run-metamorph-post)
on the Actor's last run.


<h3 id="metamorph-actors-last-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|status|query|string|false|Filter for the run status.|
|origin|query|string|false|Filter for the run origin, i.e. the means by which the run was started.|
|targetActorId|query|string|true|ID of a target Actor that the run should be transformed into.|
|build|query|string|false|Optional build of the target Actor.<br><br>It can be either a build tag or build number. By default, the run uses<br>the build specified in the default run configuration for the target<br>Actor (typically `latest`).<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|origin|DEVELOPMENT|
|origin|WEB|
|origin|API|
|origin|SCHEDULER|
|origin|TEST|
|origin|WEBHOOK|
|origin|ACTOR|
|origin|CLI|
|origin|CI|
|origin|STANDBY|
|origin|MCP|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

contains all the details about the rebooted run.

|origin|query|string|false|Filter for the run origin, i.e. the means by which the run was started.|

|origin|ACTOR|
|origin|CLI|
|origin|CI|
|origin|STANDBY|
|origin|MCP|

This endpoint is a shortcut for [Metamorph Actor run](/api/v2/actor-run-metamorph-post)
on the Actor task's last run.


<h3 id="metamorph-last-run-of-an-actor-task-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorTaskId|path|string|true|Task ID or a tilde-separated owner's username and task's name.|
|status|query|string|false|Filter for the run status.|
|origin|query|string|false|Filter for the run origin, i.e. the means by which the run was started.|
|targetActorId|query|string|true|ID of a target Actor that the run should be transformed into.|
|build|query|string|false|Optional build of the target Actor.<br><br>It can be either a build tag or build number. By default, the run uses<br>the build specified in the default run configuration for the target<br>Actor (typically `latest`).<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|origin|DEVELOPMENT|
|origin|WEB|
|origin|API|
|origin|SCHEDULER|
|origin|TEST|
|origin|WEBHOOK|
|origin|ACTOR|
|origin|CLI|
|origin|CI|
|origin|STANDBY|
|origin|MCP|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

<h1 id="apify-api-last-actor-task-runs-reboot">Last Actor task run's reboot</h1>

The API endpoint described in this section is a convenience endpoint that reboots the Actor task's last run.

Same as of functionality described in: [Reboot Actor run](/api/v2/actor-run-reboot-post)


## Reboot last run of an Actor task

<a id="opIdactorTask_runs_last_reboot_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-tasks/janedoe~my-task/runs/last/reboot \
  -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/actor-tasks/{actorTaskId}/runs/last/reboot`

Reboots the last run of the specified Actor task and returns an object that
contains all the details about the rebooted run.

This endpoint is a shortcut for [Reboot Actor run](/api/v2/actor-run-reboot-post)
on the Actor task's last run. Only runs with status `RUNNING` can be rebooted. The run's
container will be restarted, so any data not persisted in the key-value store, dataset,
or request queue will be lost.


<h3 id="reboot-last-run-of-an-actor-task-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorTaskId|path|string|true|Task ID or a tilde-separated owner's username and task's name.|
|status|query|string|false|Filter for the run status.|
|origin|query|string|false|Filter for the run origin, i.e. the means by which the run was started.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|origin|DEVELOPMENT|
|origin|WEB|
|origin|API|
|origin|SCHEDULER|
|origin|TEST|
|origin|WEBHOOK|
|origin|ACTOR|
|origin|CLI|
|origin|CI|
|origin|STANDBY|
|origin|MCP|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

<a id="opIdactorTask_runs_last_requestQueue_head_lock_post"></a>

```bash
  -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/actor-tasks/{actorTaskId}/runs/last/request-queue/head/lock`

Returns the given number of first requests from the default request queue of the last Actor task run
and locks them for the given time.

This endpoint is a shortcut for getting the last task run's `defaultRequestQueueId` and then using the
[Get and lock request queue head](/api/v2/request-queue-head-lock-post) endpoint.

<h1 id="apify-api-default">Default</h1>

## Update Actor version

<a id="opIdactor_version_put"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/{actorId}/versions/{versionNumber}' \
  -X PUT \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`PUT /v2/actors/{actorId}/versions/{versionNumber}`

Updates Actor version using values specified by a `Version` object passed as JSON in the POST payload.

If the object does not define a specific property, its value will not be
updated.

An update that sends `sourceType`, `sourceFiles`, or `tarballUrl` without
`actorPath` removes the version's stored `actorPath`. For a monorepo
version, send `actorPath` again with every upload.

The request needs to specify the `Content-Type: application/json` HTTP
header!

When providing your API authentication token, we recommend using the
request's `Authorization` header, rather than the URL.
For details, see [Authentication](/api/v2#authentication).

The response is the `Version` object as
returned by the [Get Actor version](/api/v2/actor-version-get) endpoint.


<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Get the default dataset items from an Actor's last run

<a id="opIdactor_runs_last_dataset_items_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/runs/last/dataset/items \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actors/{actorId}/runs/last/dataset/items`

Returns data stored in the default dataset of the last Actor run in the desired format.

This endpoint is a shortcut that resolves the last run's `defaultDatasetId` and proxies to the
[Get dataset items](/api/v2/dataset-items-get) endpoint.


<h3 id="get-the-default-dataset-items-from-an-actors-last-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|status|query|string|false|Filter for the run status.|
|origin|query|string|false|Filter for the run origin, i.e. the means by which the run was started.|
|format|query|string|false|Format of the results, possible values are: `json`, `jsonl`, `csv`, `html`, `xlsx`, `xml` and `rss`. The default value is `json`.<br>|
|clean|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then the API endpoint returns only non-empty items and skips hidden fields (i.e. fields starting with the # character).<br>The `clean` parameter is just a shortcut for `skipHidden=true` and `skipEmpty=true` parameters.<br>Note that since some objects might be skipped from the output, that the result might contain less items than the `limit` value.<br>|
|offset|query|number(double)|false|Number of items that should be skipped at the start. The default value is `0`.<br>|
|limit|query|number(double)|false|Maximum number of items to return. By default there is no limit.|
|fields|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of fields which should be picked from the items, only these fields will remain in the resulting record objects.<br>Note that the fields in the outputted items are sorted the same way as they are specified in the `fields` query parameter.<br>You can use this feature to effectively fix the output format.<br>|
|outputFields|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of output field names that positionally rename the fields specified in the `fields` parameter.<br>For example, `?fields=headline,url&outputFields=title,link` renames `headline` to `title` and `url` to `link` in the output.<br>The number of names in `outputFields` must match the number of names in `fields`.<br>Requires the `fields` parameter to be specified as well.<br>|
|omit|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of fields which should be omitted from the items.|
|unwind|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of fields which should be unwound, in order which they should be processed. Each field should be either an array or an object.<br>If the field is an array then every element of the array will become a separate record and merged with parent object.<br>If the unwound field is an object then it is merged with the parent object.<br>If the unwound field is missing or its value is neither an array nor an object and therefore cannot be merged with a parent object then the item gets preserved as it is.<br>Note that the unwound items ignore the `desc` parameter.<br>|
|flatten|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of fields which should transform nested objects into flat structures.<br><br>For example, with `flatten="foo"` the object `{"foo":{"bar": "hello"}}` is turned into `{"foo.bar": "hello"}`.<br><br>The original object with properties is replaced with the flattened object.<br>|
|desc|query|boolean|false|By default, results are returned in the same order as they were stored.<br>To reverse the order, set this parameter to `true` or `1`.<br>|
|attachment|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then the response will define the `Content-Disposition:<br>attachment` header, forcing a web browser to download the file rather<br>than to display it. By default this header is not present.<br>|
|delimiter|query|string|false|A delimiter character for CSV files, only used if `format=csv`. You<br>might need to URL-encode the character (e.g. use `%09` for tab or `%3B`<br>for semicolon). The default delimiter is a simple comma (`,`).<br>|
|bom|query|boolean|false|All text responses are encoded in UTF-8 encoding. By default, the<br>`format=csv` files are prefixed with the UTF-8 Byte Order Mark (BOM), while `json`, `jsonl`, `xml`, `html` and `rss` files are not.<br><br>If you want to override this default behavior, specify `bom=1` query parameter to include the BOM or `bom=0` to skip it.<br>|
|xmlRoot|query|string|false|Overrides default root element name of `xml` output. By default the root element is `items`.<br>|
|xmlRow|query|string|false|Overrides default element name that wraps each page or page function result object in `xml` output. By default the element name is `item`.<br>|
|skipHeaderRow|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then header row in the `csv` format is skipped.|
|skipHidden|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then hidden fields are skipped from the output, i.e. fields starting with the `#` character.<br>|
|skipEmpty|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then empty items are skipped from the output.<br><br>Note that if used, the results might contain less items than the limit value.<br>|
|simplified|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then, the endpoint applies the `fields=url,pageFunctionResult,errorInfo`<br>and `unwind=pageFunctionResult` query parameters. This feature is used to emulate simplified results provided by the<br>legacy Apify Crawler product and it's not recommended to use it in new integrations.<br>|
|view|query|string|false|Defines the view configuration for dataset items based on the schema definition.<br>This parameter determines how the data will be filtered and presented.<br>For complete specification details, see the [dataset schema documentation](/storage/dataset-schema).<br>|
|skipFailedPages|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then, the all the items with errorInfo property will be skipped from the output.<br><br>This feature is here to emulate functionality of API version 1 used for the legacy Apify Crawler product and it's not recommended to use it in new integrations.<br>|
|feedTitle|query|string|false|Overrides the auto-generated RSS channel `<title>` element.<br>Only used when `format=rss`. If not provided, the title defaults to `Dataset <label>`.<br>|
|feedDescription|query|string|false|Overrides the auto-generated RSS channel `<description>` element.<br>Only used when `format=rss`. If not provided, the description defaults to `Items in dataset with id "<datasetId>".`<br>|
|signature|query|string|false|Signature used for the access.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|origin|DEVELOPMENT|
|origin|WEB|
|origin|API|
|origin|SCHEDULER|
|origin|TEST|
|origin|WEBHOOK|
|origin|ACTOR|
|origin|CLI|
|origin|CI|
|origin|STANDBY|
|origin|MCP|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Store items in the default dataset of an Actor's last run

<a id="opIdactor_runs_last_dataset_items_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actors/compass~google-maps-extractor/runs/last/dataset/items \
  -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/actors/{actorId}/runs/last/dataset/items`

Appends an item or an array of items to the end of the last Actor run's default dataset.

This endpoint is a shortcut that resolves the last run's `defaultDatasetId` and proxies to the
[Store items in dataset](/api/v2/dataset-items-post) endpoint.

To save bandwidth and speed up your upload, you can send the request payload compressed and set the `Content-Encoding` header accordingly.

Below is a list of supported `Content-Encoding` types.

* Brotli: `Content-Encoding: br`
* Gzip: `Content-Encoding: gzip`
* Zstandard: `Content-Encoding: zstd`
* Deflate: `Content-Encoding: deflate`

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|actorId|path|string|true|Actor ID or the username of the Actor owner and the Actor name, separated by a tilde (`~`).|
|status|query|string|false|Filter for the run status.|
|origin|query|string|false|Filter for the run origin, i.e. the means by which the run was started.|
|Content-Encoding|header|string|false|Compression encoding of the request body.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|origin|DEVELOPMENT|
|origin|WEB|
|origin|API|
|origin|SCHEDULER|
|origin|TEST|
|origin|WEBHOOK|
|origin|ACTOR|
|origin|CLI|
|origin|CI|
|origin|STANDBY|
|origin|MCP|
|Content-Encoding|br|
|Content-Encoding|gzip|
|Content-Encoding|zstd|
|Content-Encoding|deflate|
|Content-Encoding|identity|

<h3 id="list-requests-in-the-default-request-queue-of-an-actors-last-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|clientKey|query|string|false|A unique identifier of the client accessing the request queue. It must<br>be a string between 1 and 32 characters long. This identifier is used to<br>determine whether the queue was accessed by multiple clients. If<br>`clientKey` is not provided,<br>the system considers this API call to come from a new client. For<br>details, see the `hadMultipleClients` field returned by the [Get request queue head](/api/v2/request-queue-head-get) endpoint.<br>|

|limit|query|number(double)|false|Number of keys to be returned. Maximum value is `10000`.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A cursor string for pagination, returned in the previous response as `nextCursor`. Use this to retrieve the next page of requests.|
|filter|query|[string]|false|Filter requests by their state. Possible values are `locked` and `pending`. You can combine multiple values separated by commas, which will mean the union of these filters – requests matching any of the specified states will be returned. (Not compatible with deprecated `exclusiveStartId` parameter.)|

## Get the default dataset items from an Actor task's last run

<a id="opIdactorTask_runs_last_dataset_items_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-tasks/janedoe~my-task/runs/last/dataset/items \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actor-tasks/{actorTaskId}/runs/last/dataset/items`

Returns data stored in the default dataset of the last Actor task run in the desired format.

This endpoint is a shortcut that resolves the last task run's `defaultDatasetId` and proxies to the
[Get dataset items](/api/v2/dataset-items-get) endpoint.


<h3 id="get-the-default-dataset-items-from-an-actor-tasks-last-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actorTaskId|path|string|true|Task ID or a tilde-separated owner's username and task's name.|
|status|query|string|false|Filter for the run status.|
|origin|query|string|false|Filter for the run origin, i.e. the means by which the run was started.|
|format|query|string|false|Format of the results, possible values are: `json`, `jsonl`, `csv`, `html`, `xlsx`, `xml` and `rss`. The default value is `json`.<br>|
|clean|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then the API endpoint returns only non-empty items and skips hidden fields (i.e. fields starting with the # character).<br>The `clean` parameter is just a shortcut for `skipHidden=true` and `skipEmpty=true` parameters.<br>Note that since some objects might be skipped from the output, that the result might contain less items than the `limit` value.<br>|
|offset|query|number(double)|false|Number of items that should be skipped at the start. The default value is `0`.<br>|
|limit|query|number(double)|false|Maximum number of items to return. By default there is no limit.|
|fields|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of fields which should be picked from the items, only these fields will remain in the resulting record objects.<br>Note that the fields in the outputted items are sorted the same way as they are specified in the `fields` query parameter.<br>You can use this feature to effectively fix the output format.<br>|
|outputFields|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of output field names that positionally rename the fields specified in the `fields` parameter.<br>For example, `?fields=headline,url&outputFields=title,link` renames `headline` to `title` and `url` to `link` in the output.<br>The number of names in `outputFields` must match the number of names in `fields`.<br>Requires the `fields` parameter to be specified as well.<br>|
|omit|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of fields which should be omitted from the items.|
|unwind|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of fields which should be unwound, in order which they should be processed. Each field should be either an array or an object.<br>If the field is an array then every element of the array will become a separate record and merged with parent object.<br>If the unwound field is an object then it is merged with the parent object.<br>If the unwound field is missing or its value is neither an array nor an object and therefore cannot be merged with a parent object then the item gets preserved as it is.<br>Note that the unwound items ignore the `desc` parameter.<br>|
|flatten|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of fields which should transform nested objects into flat structures.<br><br>For example, with `flatten="foo"` the object `{"foo":{"bar": "hello"}}` is turned into `{"foo.bar": "hello"}`.<br><br>The original object with properties is replaced with the flattened object.<br>|
|desc|query|boolean|false|By default, results are returned in the same order as they were stored.<br>To reverse the order, set this parameter to `true` or `1`.<br>|
|attachment|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then the response will define the `Content-Disposition:<br>attachment` header, forcing a web browser to download the file rather<br>than to display it. By default this header is not present.<br>|
|delimiter|query|string|false|A delimiter character for CSV files, only used if `format=csv`. You<br>might need to URL-encode the character (e.g. use `%09` for tab or `%3B`<br>for semicolon). The default delimiter is a simple comma (`,`).<br>|
|bom|query|boolean|false|All text responses are encoded in UTF-8 encoding. By default, the<br>`format=csv` files are prefixed with the UTF-8 Byte Order Mark (BOM), while `json`, `jsonl`, `xml`, `html` and `rss` files are not.<br><br>If you want to override this default behavior, specify `bom=1` query parameter to include the BOM or `bom=0` to skip it.<br>|
|xmlRoot|query|string|false|Overrides default root element name of `xml` output. By default the root element is `items`.<br>|
|xmlRow|query|string|false|Overrides default element name that wraps each page or page function result object in `xml` output. By default the element name is `item`.<br>|
|skipHeaderRow|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then header row in the `csv` format is skipped.|
|skipHidden|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then hidden fields are skipped from the output, i.e. fields starting with the `#` character.<br>|
|skipEmpty|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then empty items are skipped from the output.<br><br>Note that if used, the results might contain less items than the limit value.<br>|
|simplified|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then, the endpoint applies the `fields=url,pageFunctionResult,errorInfo`<br>and `unwind=pageFunctionResult` query parameters. This feature is used to emulate simplified results provided by the<br>legacy Apify Crawler product and it's not recommended to use it in new integrations.<br>|
|view|query|string|false|Defines the view configuration for dataset items based on the schema definition.<br>This parameter determines how the data will be filtered and presented.<br>For complete specification details, see the [dataset schema documentation](/storage/dataset-schema).<br>|
|skipFailedPages|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then, the all the items with errorInfo property will be skipped from the output.<br><br>This feature is here to emulate functionality of API version 1 used for the legacy Apify Crawler product and it's not recommended to use it in new integrations.<br>|
|feedTitle|query|string|false|Overrides the auto-generated RSS channel `<title>` element.<br>Only used when `format=rss`. If not provided, the title defaults to `Dataset <label>`.<br>|
|feedDescription|query|string|false|Overrides the auto-generated RSS channel `<description>` element.<br>Only used when `format=rss`. If not provided, the description defaults to `Items in dataset with id "<datasetId>".`<br>|
|signature|query|string|false|Signature used for the access.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|origin|DEVELOPMENT|
|origin|WEB|
|origin|API|
|origin|SCHEDULER|
|origin|TEST|
|origin|WEBHOOK|
|origin|ACTOR|
|origin|CLI|
|origin|CI|
|origin|STANDBY|
|origin|MCP|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Store items in the default dataset of an Actor task's last run

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-tasks/janedoe~my-task/runs/last/dataset/items \
  -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/actor-tasks/{actorTaskId}/runs/last/dataset/items`

Appends an item or an array of items to the end of the last Actor task run's default dataset.

This endpoint is a shortcut that resolves the last task run's `defaultDatasetId` and proxies to the
[Store items in dataset](/api/v2/dataset-items-post) endpoint.

To save bandwidth and speed up your upload, you can send the request payload compressed and set the `Content-Encoding` header accordingly.

Below is a list of supported `Content-Encoding` types.

* Brotli: `Content-Encoding: br`
* Gzip: `Content-Encoding: gzip`
* Zstandard: `Content-Encoding: zstd`
* Deflate: `Content-Encoding: deflate`

|origin|CI|

|origin|MCP|
|Content-Encoding|br|

## Get the default dataset items from an Actor run

<a id="opIdactorRun_dataset_items_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-runs/3KH8gEpp4d8uQSe8T/dataset/items \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actor-runs/{runId}/dataset/items`

Returns data stored in the default dataset of the Actor run in the desired format.

This endpoint is a shortcut that resolves the run's `defaultDatasetId` and proxies to the
[Get dataset items](/api/v2/dataset-items-get) endpoint.


<h3 id="get-the-default-dataset-items-from-an-actor-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|runId|path|string|true|Actor run ID.|
|format|query|string|false|Format of the results, possible values are: `json`, `jsonl`, `csv`, `html`, `xlsx`, `xml` and `rss`. The default value is `json`.<br>|
|clean|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then the API endpoint returns only non-empty items and skips hidden fields (i.e. fields starting with the # character).<br>The `clean` parameter is just a shortcut for `skipHidden=true` and `skipEmpty=true` parameters.<br>Note that since some objects might be skipped from the output, that the result might contain less items than the `limit` value.<br>|
|offset|query|number(double)|false|Number of items that should be skipped at the start. The default value is `0`.<br>|
|limit|query|number(double)|false|Maximum number of items to return. By default there is no limit.|
|fields|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of fields which should be picked from the items, only these fields will remain in the resulting record objects.<br>Note that the fields in the outputted items are sorted the same way as they are specified in the `fields` query parameter.<br>You can use this feature to effectively fix the output format.<br>|
|outputFields|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of output field names that positionally rename the fields specified in the `fields` parameter.<br>For example, `?fields=headline,url&outputFields=title,link` renames `headline` to `title` and `url` to `link` in the output.<br>The number of names in `outputFields` must match the number of names in `fields`.<br>Requires the `fields` parameter to be specified as well.<br>|
|omit|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of fields which should be omitted from the items.|
|unwind|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of fields which should be unwound, in order which they should be processed. Each field should be either an array or an object.<br>If the field is an array then every element of the array will become a separate record and merged with parent object.<br>If the unwound field is an object then it is merged with the parent object.<br>If the unwound field is missing or its value is neither an array nor an object and therefore cannot be merged with a parent object then the item gets preserved as it is.<br>Note that the unwound items ignore the `desc` parameter.<br>|
|flatten|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of fields which should transform nested objects into flat structures.<br><br>For example, with `flatten="foo"` the object `{"foo":{"bar": "hello"}}` is turned into `{"foo.bar": "hello"}`.<br><br>The original object with properties is replaced with the flattened object.<br>|
|desc|query|boolean|false|By default, results are returned in the same order as they were stored.<br>To reverse the order, set this parameter to `true` or `1`.<br>|
|attachment|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then the response will define the `Content-Disposition:<br>attachment` header, forcing a web browser to download the file rather<br>than to display it. By default this header is not present.<br>|
|delimiter|query|string|false|A delimiter character for CSV files, only used if `format=csv`. You<br>might need to URL-encode the character (e.g. use `%09` for tab or `%3B`<br>for semicolon). The default delimiter is a simple comma (`,`).<br>|
|bom|query|boolean|false|All text responses are encoded in UTF-8 encoding. By default, the<br>`format=csv` files are prefixed with the UTF-8 Byte Order Mark (BOM), while `json`, `jsonl`, `xml`, `html` and `rss` files are not.<br><br>If you want to override this default behavior, specify `bom=1` query parameter to include the BOM or `bom=0` to skip it.<br>|
|xmlRoot|query|string|false|Overrides default root element name of `xml` output. By default the root element is `items`.<br>|
|xmlRow|query|string|false|Overrides default element name that wraps each page or page function result object in `xml` output. By default the element name is `item`.<br>|
|skipHeaderRow|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then header row in the `csv` format is skipped.|
|skipHidden|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then hidden fields are skipped from the output, i.e. fields starting with the `#` character.<br>|
|skipEmpty|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then empty items are skipped from the output.<br><br>Note that if used, the results might contain less items than the limit value.<br>|
|simplified|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then, the endpoint applies the `fields=url,pageFunctionResult,errorInfo`<br>and `unwind=pageFunctionResult` query parameters. This feature is used to emulate simplified results provided by the<br>legacy Apify Crawler product and it's not recommended to use it in new integrations.<br>|
|view|query|string|false|Defines the view configuration for dataset items based on the schema definition.<br>This parameter determines how the data will be filtered and presented.<br>For complete specification details, see the [dataset schema documentation](/storage/dataset-schema).<br>|
|skipFailedPages|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1` then, the all the items with errorInfo property will be skipped from the output.<br><br>This feature is here to emulate functionality of API version 1 used for the legacy Apify Crawler product and it's not recommended to use it in new integrations.<br>|
|feedTitle|query|string|false|Overrides the auto-generated RSS channel `<title>` element.<br>Only used when `format=rss`. If not provided, the title defaults to `Dataset <label>`.<br>|
|feedDescription|query|string|false|Overrides the auto-generated RSS channel `<description>` element.<br>Only used when `format=rss`. If not provided, the description defaults to `Items in dataset with id "<datasetId>".`<br>|
|signature|query|string|false|Signature used for the access.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Store items in the default dataset of an Actor run

<a id="opIdactorRun_dataset_items_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/actor-runs/3KH8gEpp4d8uQSe8T/dataset/items \
  -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/actor-runs/{runId}/dataset/items`

Appends an item or an array of items to the end of the Actor run's default dataset.

This endpoint is a shortcut that resolves the run's `defaultDatasetId` and proxies to the
[Store items in dataset](/api/v2/dataset-items-post) endpoint.

To save bandwidth and speed up your upload, you can send the request payload compressed and set the `Content-Encoding` header accordingly.

Below is a list of supported `Content-Encoding` types.

* Brotli: `Content-Encoding: br`
* Gzip: `Content-Encoding: gzip`
* Zstandard: `Content-Encoding: zstd`
* Deflate: `Content-Encoding: deflate`


<h3 id="store-items-in-the-default-dataset-of-an-actor-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|runId|path|string|true|Actor run ID.|
|Content-Encoding|header|string|false|Compression encoding of the request body.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Content-Encoding|br|
|Content-Encoding|gzip|
|Content-Encoding|zstd|
|Content-Encoding|deflate|
|Content-Encoding|identity|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

|filter|query|[string]|false|Filter requests by their state. Possible values are `locked` and `pending`. You can combine multiple values separated by commas, which will mean the union of these filters – requests matching any of the specified states will be returned. (Not compatible with deprecated `exclusiveStartId` parameter.)|

|filter|pending|

`GET /v2/key-value-stores/{storeId}/keys`

Returns a list of objects describing keys of a given key-value store, as
well as some information about the values (e.g. size).

This endpoint is paginated using `exclusiveStartKey` and `limit` parameters
- see [Pagination](/api/v2#using-key) for more details.


<h3 id="get-list-of-key-value-store-keys-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|storeId|path|string|true|Key-value store ID or `username~store-name`.|
|exclusiveStartKey|query|string|false|All keys up to this one (including) are skipped from the result.|
|limit|query|number(int32)|false|Number of keys to be returned.|
|collection|query|string|false|Limit the results to keys that belong to a specific collection from the key-value store schema. The key-value store need to have a schema defined for this parameter to work.|
|prefix|query|string|false|Limit the results to keys that start with a specific prefix.|
|signature|query|string|false|Signature used for the access.|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

## Download key-value store records

<a id="opIdkeyValueStore_records_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/key-value-stores/WkzbQMuFYuamGv3YF/records \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/key-value-stores/{storeId}/records`

Downloads all records from the key-value store as a ZIP archive.
Each record is stored as a separate file in the archive, with the filename equal to the record key.

You can optionally filter the records by `collection` or `prefix` to download only a subset of the store.


<h3 id="download-key-value-store-records-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|storeId|path|string|true|Key-value store ID or `username~store-name`.|
|collection|query|string|false|If specified, only records belonging to a specific collection from the key-value store schema. The key-value store need to have a schema defined for this parameter to work.<br>|
|prefix|query|string|false|If specified, only records whose key starts with the given prefix are included in the archive.<br>|
|signature|query|string|false|Signature used for the access.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Get key-value store record

<a id="opIdkeyValueStore_record_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/key-value-stores/WkzbQMuFYuamGv3YF/records/someKey \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/key-value-stores/{storeId}/records/{recordKey}`

Gets a value stored in the key-value store under a specific key.

The response body has the same `Content-Encoding` header as it was set in
[Set key-value store record](/api/v2/key-value-store-record-put).

If the request does not define the `Accept-Encoding` HTTP header with the
right encoding, the record will be decompressed.

Most HTTP clients support decompression by default. After using the HTTP
client with decompression support, the `Accept-Encoding` header is set by
the client and body is decompressed automatically.

Please note that for security reasons, Apify API can perform small modifications
to HTML documents before they are served via this endpoint. To fetch the raw HTML
content without any modifications, use the `attachment` query parameter.


<h3 id="get-key-value-store-record-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|storeId|path|string|true|Key-value store ID or `username~store-name`.|
|recordKey|path|string|true|Key of the record.|
|attachment|query|boolean|false|If `true` or `1`, the response will be served with `Content-Disposition: attachment` header,<br>causing web browsers to offer downloading HTML records instead of displaying them.<br>|
|signature|query|string|false|Signature used for the access.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Set key-value store record

<a id="opIdkeyValueStore_record_put"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.apify.com/v2/key-value-stores/WkzbQMuFYuamGv3YF/records/someKey \
  -X PUT \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`PUT /v2/key-value-stores/{storeId}/records/{recordKey}`

Stores a value under a specific key to the key-value store.

The value is passed as the PUT payload and it is stored with a MIME content
type defined by the `Content-Type` header and with encoding defined by the
`Content-Encoding` header.

To save bandwidth, storage, and speed up your upload, send the request
payload compressed with Gzip compression and add the `Content-Encoding: gzip`
header. It is possible to set up another compression type with `Content-Encoding`
request header.

Below is a list of supported `Content-Encoding` types.

* Brotli compression: `Content-Encoding: br`
* Gzip compression: `Content-Encoding: gzip`
* Zstandard compression: `Content-Encoding: zstd`
* Deflate compression: `Content-Encoding: deflate`


<h3 id="set-key-value-store-record-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|storeId|path|string|true|Key-value store ID or `username~store-name`.|
|recordKey|path|string|true|Key of the record.|
|Content-Encoding|header|string|false|Compression encoding of the request body.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Content-Encoding|br|
|Content-Encoding|gzip|
|Content-Encoding|zstd|
|Content-Encoding|deflate|
|Content-Encoding|identity|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
httpBearer, apiKey
</aside>

## Get dataset

<a id="opIddataset_get"></a>

```bash

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/datasets/{datasetId}`

Returns dataset object for given dataset ID.

This does not return dataset items, only information about the storage itself.
To retrieve dataset items, use the [Get dataset items](/api/v2/dataset-items-get) endpoint.

:::note

Keep in mind that attributes `itemCount` and `cleanItemCount` are not propagated right away after data are pushed into a dataset.

:::

There is a short period (up to 5 seconds) during which these counters may not match with exact counts in dataset items.
